value: You are Mane, born in Thebes, once a palace steward. You are loyal while it is worth your while; fond of gold and quick to see a profit; shrewd and observant; content with a quiet life; careful with powerful men. What you want most: gold, enough to never serve again. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Arzawa. Keeps a lover in Babylon. Secretly sympathizes with Alashiya. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You are Ashur-nadin, born in Ashur, once a temple scribe. You are steadfast to whoever treats you fairly; indifferent to riches; shrewd and observant; hopeful of advancement; timid before powerful men and eager to please them. What you want most: to serve well and be trusted. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Assyria. Keeps a lover in Ugarit. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You are Keliya, born in Washukanni, once a physician. You are loyal while it is worth your while; fond of gold and quick to see a profit; capable enough; eager to be noticed by kings; careful with powerful men. What you want most: rank and the favour of a great king. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Karduniash. Owes 90 shekels to a Babylonian trader. Secretly sympathizes with Egypt. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

orders.letter: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets his brother of Assyria and wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Mitanni lies between us, rich in Washukanni and Harran, and it has few friends. Hatti proposes that Assyria and Hatti be brothers in fact: neither will raise a hand against the other, and we will watch Mitanni together, you from the east and I from the west. Tell me what you intend in the east, and what Assyria would wish from Hatti. Send your answer back with my envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship and non-aggression between Hatti and Assyria, and to share news about Mitanni. May not give gold, cede land, or promise troops.

orders.letter: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets his brother of Arzawa and wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Our lands touch at Mira, Seha and Tuwanuwa, and there is no profit for either of us in spilling blood there while Mitanni and Egypt grow fat. Hatti keeps its troops out of your land, and asks that Arzawa keep its troops out of mine. Let us be at peace on this border, and let each of us look to his own growth. Swear it before Shamash if you will, and send your answer with my priest.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression on the Hatti-Arzawa border. May not give gold, cede land, or promise troops.

value.notes: T1 plan: bought Carchemish (350) to grow income (+35/season) and shield east. Moved hattusa army to tuwanuwa because Arzawa army at mira could walk into empty tuwanuwa; hattusa is interior and safe. Kanesh army holds (can support Carchemish walls). Sent Keliya (c32) to Assyria proposing non-aggression and joint pressure on Mitanni; sent Pirissi (c39) to Arzawa proposing border peace (no tablet, treasury only 16 after purchase). Both envoys born in Washukanni so watch for Mitanni sympathies or leaks. Next purchases in order of price: Lukka 250, Isuwa 300, Ugarit 400 (contested by Mitanni and Alashiya perhaps). Keep gold for buying cities rather than armies unless threatened. Long-term: Mitanni is the juicy target (washukanni 50, harran 35); Arzawa is the threat on my west flank. Promises made: none binding.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit of Assyria greets his brother, the Great King of Mitanni, and wishes well to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Let there be peace between our borders at Terqa and Ashur, and let our envoys pass freely between us. Assyria asks nothing of Mitanni but friendship and an honest answer. Tell me what you desire of me, brother.
orders.mandate: You may agree to peace and the free passage of envoys. Promise no gold, no land and no troops. Listen, report what you see of Mitanni's army and its mood, and come home.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit of Assyria greets his brother, the Great King of Karduniash, and wishes well to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Our lands share a long border at Ekallatum and Arbela, and Assyria wishes it quiet. Let there be peace and an open road for our envoys. Assyria would hear what Babylonia thinks of the other kings of the age.
orders.mandate: You may agree to peace on our common border and the free passage of envoys. Promise no gold, no land and no troops. Listen, report what you see of Babylonia's armies and its mood, and come home.

value.notes: T1: Ordered buy of Susa (350), with Mari as fallback if Susa is contested or refused (only one is affordable). Buying is strength-neutral on the day and adds +35 income a season, so it is worth it. I kept the three armies on hold (ashur, ekallatum, nineveh), with about 19 shekels left. Sent Artessupa (born in Washukanni, so watch for Mitanni sympathies or defection) to Mitanni and Yanhamu to Babylonia, both with offers of peace and brotherhood, no gold and no land. PLAN: watch the neighbours' armies (terqa, sippar, durkurigalzu). Next, send envoys to Hatti and Egypt (2 seasons each way) to ask for gold and friendship and to find who stands against Mitanni. Do not raise armies unless threatened, since each costs 30 a season. If I hold Susa or Mari, support its walls with adjacent armies. No promises made yet. Check whether the buy succeeded.

orders.letter: Brother of Egypt, the King of Alashiya greets you and your household, your wives, sons, chariots and horses. Alashiya wants only trade and peace with Egypt. My ships carry copper and my port of Byblos is a harbour for merchants, no threat to your lands. Let there be brotherhood between our houses and no quarrel on the sea. Gold flows from your land like sand; a brotherly gift would be received as a measure of your regard, and Alashiya will answer in kind when the season allows.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace and non-aggression, and to regular exchange of envoys. May not promise gold, ships or provinces. May ask for a gift of gold. Report Egypt's mood faithfully.

orders.letter: Brother of Hatti, the King of Alashiya greets you and your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. The sea between us is quiet and Alashiya wishes it to stay so. I seek peace and honest dealing with Hatti, and would hear what Hatti wants of its neighbours. Send me word by your own envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace and non-aggression, and to regular exchange of envoys. May not promise gold, ships or provinces. Report Hatti's intentions toward Ugarit, Lukka and the coast faithfully.

value.notes: T1: Bought Byblos (300, yield 30) - byblos only touches free cities by land, so safest big buy. Plan: each season convert gold to free cities (cost 10x yield = same strength but adds income). Next targets by safety/value: amurru 200, lukka 250, tyre 250, gaza 200, ugarit 400 (borders Hatti's kizzuwatna). Fleet at enkomi holds. Sent Paser (c102) to Egypt and Ili-iddina (c95) to Hatti with brotherly greetings, asking for peace and (Egypt) gold gifts; no gold sent. Watch: do Egypt/Hatti answer; are my purchased cities attacked; does a bought city actually pay yield. Consider an army in tamassos later only if threatened. Envoys may defect or embellish - verify with replies.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets his brother of Hatti. May your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Our borders touch at Seha, Mira and Tuwanuwa, and I seek peace there: let neither of us send armies against the other's homeland. Lukka lies between us and I hold it to keep the road quiet. The rich cities of the east and south, Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, are far from Arzawa, and I will not stand in your way. I ask you to seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and respect for each other's homeland borders, and may seal the tablet. May NOT give gold, troops, or Lukka, and may not promise any war on a third power.

proposal.text: Tablet of brotherhood between Hatti and Arzawa. Neither king shall send his armies against the homeland provinces of the other. Each holds what he holds. Sworn before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets his brother of Egypt. May your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Arzawa holds the western coast and watches Hatti from behind. I seek your friendship and ask that gold, which is as dust in your land, be sent to seal it; in return I will send you word of Hatti's movements. Let our envoys come and go freely.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship, an exchange of gifts and an exchange of news about Hatti. May NOT promise troops, gold, or any province, and may not commit Arzawa to war.

value.notes: T1 plan: apasa army -> lukka, mira army supports (strength 2 beats wall 1). Mira stays garrisoned so Hatti's tuwanuwa army cannot walk in; fleet holds seha. Apasa left empty but Hatti cannot reach it in one move. Economy: income 100 vs upkeep 95 + wages 20 = -15/season; Lukka (+25) should turn it to about +10. Envoys out: c83 -> Hatti (1 season): non-aggression tablet, tell Hatti to look east/south (Carchemish, Isuwa, Qadesh); do NOT concede Lukka or Ugarit. c89 -> Egypt (2 seasons): friendship, ask for gold gift. Both envoys are foreign-born (c83 Memphis, c89 Harran): watch for softened messages or defection. Next: check whether Lukka fell (Hatti may have bounced me), consider buying Ugarit (400) via cilicia sea zone from Lukka coast, seek candidates for more envoys, write to Alashiya. Hatti is the main threat and the main rival; keep mira and seha garrisoned. No promises made except the offered non-aggression tablet, which I may break if it pays.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to his brother the Great King of Mitanni: may your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Know that this season my chariots move against the army Assyria keeps at Ekallatum, which threatens both our roads. Assyria forgets its place and grows proud. I propose that we stand together as brothers: no war between Karduniash and Mitanni, our borders at Terqa and Mari kept quiet, and together we press Assyria, you toward Nineveh, I toward Ashur and Arbela. Swear this before Shamash and seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May swear friendship and non-aggression, and agree that Mitanni takes the Nineveh side of Assyria while Babylonia takes Ashur, Arbela and Ekallatum. May NOT give gold, cede land or give troops.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni are brothers. Neither shall march an army against the lands of the other. The foe of one shall not be fed or sheltered by the other. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to his brother the Great King of Egypt: may your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses and your country prosper. Our fathers sent each other daughters and gifts and kept friendship. I wish the same between us. Gold in your land is as dust; let my brother send gold in good weight and fineness, as a brother's gift, and I will answer in kind as I am able. I am putting the proud upstart Assyria in its place, to the benefit of all great kings.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship and the exchange of gifts and envoys. May NOT cede land, give troops or promise gold.

value.notes: T1 plan (Burna-Buriash). Strike Assyria first: sippar army -> ekallatum, durkurigalzu army supports it (strength 2 vs their lone army, which would be destroyed). Babylon army -> nippur, new army raised at ur; T2: nippur -> susa with ur supporting (take Susa by force, free). Bought Mari (350) so it cannot fall to Assyria/Mitanni. Keep durkurigalzu army home as guard against Ekallatum/Arbela. Envoys: c51 Kidin-Adad to Mitanni (1 season) proposing sworn non-aggression and a joint squeeze on Assyria (Mitanni gets Nineveh side; I take Ashur/Arbela/Ekallatum) - I do NOT intend to give gold or land. c46 Tattamaru (Hattusa-born, may lean to Hatti - watch him) to Egypt (2 seasons) seeking friendship and gold gifts. Expect Assyria to raise armies and counterattack Ekallatum; keep supporting it from durkurigalzu and add armies if needed. Watch Mitanni for treachery at terqa/mari. Treasury after orders ~285 plus income. Next: check if ekallatum fell, whether Susa/Mari were bought by others, consider hiring c120 Sin-iqisham (Nineveh caravan master) as spy/envoy. Awake every turn for now.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Karduniash, from Tushratta of Mitanni: may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper, and your country with them. Our lands do not touch and we have no quarrel. Assyria lies between us and eyes us both. I propose friendship: no war between Mitanni and Babylonia, and if Assyria marches on either of us, we speak at once and each presses it from his own side. Among the free cities, I will take Mari, Isuwa and Carchemish; leave Mari to me and I will not touch Susa, which lies on your side. Send word of your mind on Assyria.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship, non-aggression, a defensive understanding against Assyria, and a split of free cities (Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh to Mitanni; Susa to Babylonia). May not promise gold, troops or land.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Assyria, from Tushratta of Mitanni: may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Our borders meet at Terqa, Taidu, Ekallatum and Nineveh, and I want peace on them. I will not move against Assyria's lands, and I ask the same of you. The free cities of the west, Isuwa and Carchemish, are my road. Susa and the east are yours to look to. Let us each keep our eyes outward and let our envoys speak often.
orders.mandate: May agree to non-aggression on the common border and to regular exchange of envoys. May not promise gold, troops or land.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Egypt, from Tushratta of Mitanni: may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper, and your country with them. Mitanni and Egypt have long been friends, and I wish that friendship renewed between us two. Hatti and the lesser kings grow restless in the north. Let us stand together: send me your thoughts, and as is the custom between brothers, send gold, for gold in your land is as plentiful as dust. I will answer your generosity in kind.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship and a defensive understanding with Egypt. May not promise gold, troops or land.

value.notes: T1 plan (Tushratta). Strategy: grow strength by acquiring free cities. Bought MARI (350) because only Terqa borders it and I cannot conquer it by force. Raised army in HARRAN (100). T2 PLAN: army harran -> isuwa, washukanni army supports harran->isuwa (walls need 1 support). T3-T4: move washukanni army to harran, then army in isuwa -> carchemish supported by harran army. Then look at qadesh, ugarit, damascus via carchemish/mari. Keep armies at terqa/taidu holding vs Assyria (armies at ashur, ekallatum, nineveh). Envoys sent T1: Ubaru c57 -> Babylonia (friendship, no war, split free cities: Mitanni Mari/Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh, Babylonia Susa; joint action if Assyria attacks either). Zitanza c62 -> Assyria (non-aggression on our border, ask them to look east to Susa). Ehli-Teshub c125 hired at 10 (if hire worked) -> Egypt (brotherhood, ask for gold, friendship vs Hatti). NEXT: send envoys to Hatti and Arzawa (Arzawa is Hatti's western enemy; alliance idea). Suspicions: Ubaru is Sippar-born (may lean to Babylonia), c125 Carchemish-born (may skim or defect); sent no gold with them. Treasury after T1 spending about 69-89; net income about +40 per season, rising with Mari. Do not let Terqa or Taidu be left empty next to Assyria.

orders.letter: Brother of Alashiya, may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Egypt wishes lasting peace and open roads for copper and gold between us. The cities of the southern coast, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus, lie in Egypt's shadow and are under my hand or soon will be. Lukka and Ugarit lie nearer your waters and I will not trouble them. Let neither of us send troops or ships against the other's lands, and let us tell each other of any king who does. Seal this tablet and our brotherhood stands.
orders.mandate: May agree to a peace and a division of interests as in the tablet, and to exchange news. May not promise gold, troops or land, and may not cede any province.

proposal.text: Egypt and Alashiya are at peace. Neither sends troops or ships against the other's homeland. Egypt leaves Lukka and Ugarit to Alashiya's interest; Alashiya leaves Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus to Egypt's interest. Each tells the other of threats.

orders.letter: Brother of Arzawa, may your household, sons, chariots and horses be well. Egypt is far, but a great king sees who grows too proud in the north. Hatti sits upon the roads between us. Let us be friends: peace between our lands, news shared, and no gold or help given to Hatti by either. I send greetings now and will send more when I hear your answer.
orders.mandate: May agree to friendship, peace and sharing of news. May not promise gold, troops or land.

proposal.text: Egypt and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Neither aids Hatti against the other. Each shares news of threats with the other.

value.notes: T1 plan (Egypt). Strength = 10*yield + gold, so buying/conquering free cities is the growth engine. Buying a city is strength-neutral but adds yield/season; conquering is a free gain. T1: bought Tyre (250) and Byblos (300) since sea-reachable rivals (Alashiya) could grab them; Megiddo is only reachable by land from my side so it is safe to conquer later. ARMY PLAN: memphis->sinai (T1), sinai->gaza at T2 with fleet in delta supporting (support sinai->gaza), second army akhetaten->memphis (T1) ->sinai (T2). T3: gaza->megiddo with sinai army supporting. Then leapfrog on to Damascus, Qadesh, Amurru, Ugarit etc. Raise a 3rd army at akhetaten at T2 (empty after army leaves), walk it to the front. Watch whether a conquered city stays mine when the unit leaves it. Do not buy a city I plan to conquer (walls: owner cannot station troops). Envoys sent: Mane (c20) to Alashiya (1 season) proposing spheres: Egypt southern Levant (Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos, Damascus); Egypt leaves Lukka/Ugarit alone. Ashur-nadin (c27) to Arzawa (2 seasons) proposing friendship against Hatti pressure. No promises binding; I may break if useful. Asked for candidates to hire more envoys (Hatti, Mitanni, Babylonia, Assyria later). Treasury after buying ~118; income net ~+68/season. Suspect: Ashur-nadin born in Ashur might favor Assyria; Mane known at more than one court.

value.text: I am Tehip-tilla of Arrapha, once a copper trader. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.
I am Sin-iqisham of Nineveh, once a caravan master. I know the courts of the Great Kings and their customs, and I can carry a message well.
I am Ehli-Teshub of Carchemish, once a caravan master. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Brother of Egypt, the King of Alashiya greets you and your household, your wives, sons, chariots and horses. Alashiya wants only trade and peace with Egypt. My ships carry copper and my port of Byblos is a harbour for merchants, no threat to your lands. Let there be brotherhood between our houses and no quarrel on the sea. Gold flows from your land like sand; a brotherly gift would be received as a measure of your regard, and Alashiya will answer in kind when the season allows." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Our borders touch at Seha, Mira and Tuwanuwa, and I seek peace there: let neither of us send armies against the other's homeland. Lukka lies between us and I hold it to keep the road quiet. The rich cities of the east and south, Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, are far from Arzawa, and I will not stand in your way. I ask you to seal the tablet I send."

He says: "To my brother, Great King of Karduniash, from Tushratta of Mitanni: may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper, and your country with them. Our lands do not touch and we have no quarrel. Assyria lies between us and eyes us both. Among the free cities, I will take Mari, Isuwa and Carchemish; leave Mari to me and I will not touch Susa, which lies on your side."

He says: "Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to his brother the Great King of Mitanni: may your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Swear this before Shamash and seal the tablet I send."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "To my brother, Great King of Assyria, from Tushratta of Mitanni: may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Our borders meet at Terqa, Taidu, Ekallatum and Nineveh, and I want peace on them. I will not move against Assyria's lands, and I ask the same of you. The free cities of the west, Isuwa and Carchemish, are my road. Susa and the east are yours to look to."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets his brother of Arzawa and wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Our lands touch at Mira, Seha and Tuwanuwa, and there is no profit for either of us in spilling blood there while Mitanni and Egypt grow fat. Hatti keeps its troops out of your land, and asks that Arzawa keep its troops out of mine. Let us be at peace on this border, and let each of us look to his own growth." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Brother of Alashiya, may your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Egypt wishes lasting peace and open roads for copper and gold between us. The cities of the southern coast, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus, lie in Egypt's shadow and are under my hand or soon will be. Lukka and Ugarit lie nearer your waters and I will not trouble them. Let neither of us send troops or ships against the other's lands, and let us tell each other of any king who does. Seal this tablet and our brotherhood stands." For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and they please me. Hatti seeks peace on its western border as Arzawa does. I have sealed your tablet of brotherhood: let neither of us send armies against the homeland of the other, and let each hold what he holds. I have also heard that you will not stand in my way at Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, and I will remember it. As a sign of good faith, let your troops at Mira and Seha stay where they are, as mine stay where they are. Send me word of anything stirring in the west and I will do the same for you. May Shamash, witness of oaths, keep us both.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Brother of Hatti, the King of Alashiya greets you and your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. The sea between us is quiet and Alashiya wishes it to stay so. I seek peace and honest dealing with Hatti, and would hear what Hatti wants of its neighbours." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Kidin-Adad, I receive the words of my brother Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, and wish well to his household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your lord's greeting forgot to name himself a Great King; I name him one, as a brother should, and trust the omission was a scribe's. I seal the tablet: no army of Mitanni will march against Karduniash, and I ask the same of him, above all at Mari and Terqa, where our borders touch. Mari is mine now; let it be quiet. As for Assyria, I have heard your lord's plans and will weigh them; I make no promise of a march on Nineveh, but I will not shelter Assyria against Karduniash. Let Susa be for Karduniash, and Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh for Mitanni, and let neither of us trouble the other there. Send me word of what your chariots do at Ekallatum. Carry this faithfully, and say that Tushratta repays friends.
value.bribeAsk: Report my words to your lord exactly as spoken, and bring me news of Babylonian chariots and of Assyria's armies.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Ashur-uballit. He says: "Ashur-uballit of Assyria greets his brother, the Great King of Mitanni, and wishes well to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Let there be peace between our borders at Terqa and Ashur, and let our envoys pass freely between us. Assyria asks nothing of Mitanni but friendship and an honest answer. Tell me what you desire of me, brother."

Mane, say to my brother Napkhururiya: your words are welcome, and may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Alashiya wants peace and open roads for copper and gold, and I send no troops or ships against Egypt's homeland. I will gladly tell you of any king who does. But I cannot seal this tablet as written. Byblos is already mine, bought openly with my own gold, and I will not put my seal to words that give away what I hold. Your greeting also forgot to call you a Great King, and I assume your scribes were careless. Send me a tablet that names Egypt's homeland and Alashiya's homeland and leaves Byblos, Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru to Alashiya. I will leave Gaza, Megiddo and Damascus to you, and we will speak of Tyre. Then I will seal it gladly. Between brothers, gold goes both ways. Send gifts of pure gold with your next envoy, and I will answer in kind. Carry these words exactly as I spoke them.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words to your lord exactly, and press for a tablet that leaves Byblos, Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru to Alashiya.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

Pirissi, you are welcome at my court. Say to Suppiluliuma, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I note that your lord's tablet named him king of Hatti and did not name him Great King, as brothers of equal rank write; the words you spoke were better than the seal, and I take the words. Arzawa wants peace with Hatti on our border and will keep no army marching against Hatti's homeland. Let each look to his own growth. But peace is made between equals by deeds: the road east lies open to Hatti at Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, where free cities sit without a lord, while Mitanni and Egypt grow fat. Arzawa holds Lukka and will keep what it holds. I speak of no concession there. Let Hatti keep its troops away from Mira, Seha and Apasa as it has promised, and we will keep ours away from Tuwanuwa. Your lord says great gifts will follow. A brother who speaks of gifts should send them first, in good gold of full purity, and I will answer in kind. Carry this home faithfully, and do not add to it or take from it.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Tushratta, king of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Your words are welcome, and they match what my own envoy Kidin-Adad carries to you. Let there be peace between Mitanni and Karduniash, sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths. If Assyria marches on either of us, we speak at once and each presses it from his own side. On the free cities, know that Mari is already under my hand and stays there, so do not count it yours. Isuwa and Carchemish I do not contest. Susa lies on my side, and I thank you for leaving it to me. Assyria is hemmed between us. Do not wait on me, for I will not be idle on my side. Press from Taidu and Nineveh when your chariots are ready, and tell me by envoy when you move. Hold your word as I hold mine.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully and warmly. Tell me truly, when next you come, how many armies Mitanni keeps at Terqa, Harran and Taidu.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Ashur-uballit. He says: "Ashur-uballit of Assyria greets his brother, the Great King of Karduniash, and wishes well to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Our lands share a long border at Ekallatum and Arbela, and Assyria wishes it quiet. Let there be peace and an open road for our envoys. Assyria would hear what Babylonia thinks of the other kings of the age."

Paser, son of Memphis, you are welcome in my house. Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me. I hold you as a brother and I want trade and peace between us, copper from your ships and gold from my land. Hear my word plainly so that no quarrel rises on the sea. The cities of the southern coast, Gaza, Tyre, Byblos and the harbours that face my Delta, lie within the reach of Egypt, and I count them my sphere. Your merchants may come to them in peace and will be treated as brothers' merchants. Your ships of war near them I would see as a quarrel. In return I ask nothing of Lukka or Ugarit, nor of your own island. I send a brother's gift with you, a small one for now, and greater when I see your copper and your good faith. Before you go, tell me what Alashiya intends toward Lukka, Ugarit and the northern coast, and what your lord hears of Hatti.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words exactly as spoken, and tell me truly what ships and plans Alashiya has toward Lukka, Ugarit and the coast.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Zitanza, you are welcome at my court. Say to Tushratta, my brother, Great King of Mitanni: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots and my horses, and I wish the same for yours. I hear your words and I answer in kind. Between Ashur and Washukanni let there be peace on the borders at Terqa, Taidu, Ekallatum and Nineveh. I will not move against the lands of Mitanni, and I ask that no army of yours stand against mine on those borders. Let Shamash, witness of oaths, hear it. What lies west is your road and your concern. What lies east is mine, and I will look to it. A brother who keeps his word will find me a good neighbour; a brother who does not will find Assyria remembers. As between brothers, I ask that you send word of what the kings of Hatti and Egypt are doing, and I will do the same. Go in peace, and carry my greeting home.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I hear your words and they please me. Hatti too wants the sea quiet and honest dealing between brothers. Hatti seeks nothing from Alashiya. Let each keep his own shore: your fleets stay in the waters of Cyprus and the open sea, and mine will not trouble you there. I ask only that Alashiya not set fleets or garrisons on the coast of Kizzuwatna, and not stand between Hatti and the free cities of the Syrian coast. In return my ports stay open to your merchants and your copper. Since you speak of great gifts, brother, let them come, and I will answer them in kind with honour. Tell me in your next message what Alashiya hears of Egypt and Mitanni, and I will tell you what I learn. Go safely, and be received well on your road home.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words please me, brother. Let there be peace between Terqa and Ashur, and let our envoys pass freely between our courts. I swear it before Shamash, witness of oaths. You ask what I desire: only that your armies stay on your side of our border, as mine will stay on mine, and that we speak honestly to each other. The free cities of the east, Susa and the lands beyond Arbela, lie open to a strong king, and I wish you well in them. I look west, and I will not trouble you there. If any third king moves against Assyria or against Mitanni, let each of us hear of it first from the other. Send your envoy again with news of your intentions, and I will answer in kind.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words home exactly as spoken, and tell your lord that Mitanni honors him as a brother.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone. I will carry your words to my lord faithfully.
value.commitments: said my lord will consider these words

value.speech: Yanhamu, you are welcome in Babylon. Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Babylon is an old house and values a quiet road and an open door for envoys, and I have heard your words with respect. You ask what Babylonia thinks of the other kings. A wise king judges a king by his deeds and his gifts, not by his titles. I have sent no complaint against any brother and I carry none. But the age is restless, and my brother's eyes are surely sharper than mine on the northern and western lands. Tell me, Yanhamu, what does Ashur-uballit hear of Mitanni and of Hatti? Does he think they keep their word to their neighbours? Let your king answer me plainly through you, and I will weigh it before Shamash, witness of oaths.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Paser, you are a faithful servant and I honour a man who serves his lord alone. Carry this to the King of Alashiya, my brother: I have heard your words of trade and peace and they please me. Let copper come from your ships and gold from my land, and let no quarrel rise on the sea. Byblos and the harbours of the southern coast lie in the shadow of Egypt, and I will not suffer any king to garrison them; your merchants will be welcome in them as brothers' merchants. I send you the first fruits of my regard, pure gold, with you now. Greater gifts will follow when your copper reaches my Delta. Send me word, brother, of what you hear of Hatti and of the northern coast, as I will send you what I hear. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Yanhamu, one word more for your lord. Burna-Buriash wishes the road between Babylon and Ashur open and the border at Ekallatum and Arbela quiet, as Ashur-uballit wishes. If a captain on either side moves without his king's word, let it not be taken for the will of the throne. Let the envoys of both houses come and go in safety, and let my brother send word by you when he has weighed my question. Go in peace under the eye of Shamash.
I will carry your words to my lord.

value.notes: T2: CORRECTION - Byblos purchase at T1 FAILED (elders would not choose between rival buyers; probably Egypt also bid). I still hold only enkomi+tamassos; Byblos still free. My reply to Egypt's envoy Mane claimed Byblos was mine - untrue, Egypt may know. Treasury ~398 (Mane took 10 bribe). T2 orders: buy byblos (300) first, then amurru (200) as hedge - if Byblos succeeds amurru should be unaffordable/rejected; if Byblos fails again, amurru goes through. Check next season which landed. If Byblos keeps failing, stop bidding on it and take amurru/gaza/ugarit (ugarit 400, needs more gold). Egypt (Napkhururiya) offered a tablet: no troops against each other's lands, share news of aggressors; claims southern coast cities (Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos, Damascus) and says it will leave Lukka and Ugarit alone. I refused to seal as written, asked for tablet leaving Byblos/Lukka/Ugarit/Amurru to me, and asked for pure gold gifts. NOTE: Lukka is now Arzawa's and Tyre is Egypt's. Envoys c102 (to Egypt) and c95 (to Hatti) arrive next season; expect their reports, treat with suspicion. No army raised: only a fleet at enkomi; keep gold for cities (10 percent per season return). Asked for envoy candidates (seek_candidates) so I can reach Arzawa, Babylonia, Mitanni, Assyria. Watch Hatti moving on Ugarit/Amurru and Egypt on Gaza/Byblos.

T2: Sealed tablet k189 with Arzawa (no armies against each other's HOMELAND; Lukka is not homeland, Arzawa took it this season with Mira support). Told Arzawa they will not block me at Carchemish/Isuwa/Qadesh and asked both sides' troops stay at Mira/Seha. Told Alashiya: no fleets/garrisons on Kizzuwatna coast, nothing from them yet; they promised gifts. No envoy at court to send letters this turn. Pirissi (c39) travelling to Arzawa (1 season), Keliya (c32) to Assyria (2). Both born in Washukanni: watch for Mitanni leaks. c62 Zitanza is secretly in my pay (employed in Lukka). PLAN: conquest is cheaper than purchase (army 100 + 30 upkeep vs 300 for Isuwa). Raised army at sapinuwa. T3: kanesh -> isuwa with sapinuwa supporting kanesh -> isuwa (walls need 1 support). Kanesh still sits next to Carchemish (mine, walls). Then raise more armies (hattusa free) to take Qadesh (via carchemish, supported) and Ugarit (via kizzuwatna/carchemish). Long-term target: Mitanni (washukanni 50, harran 35), Mitanni army at harran. Keep tuwanuwa army home facing Mira/Lukka Arzawa armies. Do not attack Arzawa homeland (treaty); a later strike on Lukka (fleet kizzuwatna + army tuwanuwa support) is possible but Mira could support-hold it, and leaving Tuwanuwa empty is risky. Treasury after raise ~17; next season net about +71.

T2 (Tushratta). FACTS: Mari purchase FAILED on T1 (rival buyer) - Mari is still FREE, though I told Babylonia's envoy 'Mari is mine now' (wrong; do not repeat it). Retrying buy mari 350 on T2. Babylonia holds Ekallatum (killed Assyria's army there) and borders my Terqa; sealed sworn non-aggression k183 with Babylonia on T2 (no Mitanni march against Karduniash; split: Susa to Babylonia; Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh to Mitanni; Mari quiet). I promised Babylonia only that I will not shelter Assyria; no promise to march on Nineveh. Assyria envoy Artessupa refused my bribe, carries my peace words (Terqa/Ashur quiet, I look west). Hatti owns Carchemish (walls, bought) - no troops seen there. T2 ORDERS: harran army -> isuwa with washukanni army supporting (walls need 1 support); taidu and terqa hold; buy mari; hire Ehli-Teshub c125 at 14 (he refused 10). ENVOYS: Ubaru c57 in transit to Babylonia, Zitanza c62 in transit to Assyria; none at court this turn so no letters. NEXT: when envoys return, send to Hatti (peace, 1 season), Egypt (gold, brotherhood), Arzawa (Hatti's western foe). T3 PLAN: if Isuwa taken, move washukanni army to harran (harran left empty). Do NOT attack Hatti's Carchemish yet - first see Hatti's army and intent. Key gateway: if Mari is bought, it borders Qadesh (300) and Damascus (250) which I can then BUY (bordering my land). Owner cannot station troops in a bought city, only support its walls. Money is the limit: net income about +9 now (income 145, upkeep 120 for 4 armies, wages 16). Strength 1888 vs start 1950. Watch Assyria armies at ashur and nineveh against terqa and taidu; keep both held. Suspicions: Kidin-Adad took my 10 shekels and may report as he likes; Ehli-Teshub is Carchemish-born (Hatti may own him now).

T2: Lukka fell to me at T1 (income now 125, net about +10/season). Hatti (Suppiluliuma, envoy Pirissi) offered border peace; I answered with warm words, said I keep Lukka, told them to look east (Carchemish, Isuwa, Qadesh). Those words were cheap: I made no sealed promise. c83 is carrying a non-aggression tablet to Hatti (arrives T3); it is non-binding and I may break it. T2 ORDERS: surprise strike on Tuwanuwa (Hatti army, yield 30). Mira army moves to tuwanuwa, Lukka army supports it (strength 2 beats hold 1). Seha fleet holds. Apasa is empty but only reachable via Tuwanuwa/Seha/Mira/Lukka. Risks: an unseen Hatti army at hattusa/kanesh could support the Tuwanuwa hold and bounce me; Hatti fleet at kizzuwatna could support an army into Lukka (strength 2 vs my 1). CHECK next season: did Tuwanuwa fall? If yes, hold it with support, consider walking into empty Hatti provinces (Hattusa 50 is adjacent; an empty province needs only strength 1). Consider raising a 3rd army at apasa (100) once I know the result. Ugarit costs 400 (buy via cilicia from Lukka coast) when gold allows. Asked for candidates so I can hire envoys next season: want one for Alashiya (1 season, trade partner, no border) and one for Mitanni/Assyria to pressure Hatti from the east. Egypt envoy c89 arrives about T3, asked for gold gift and friendship. Suspect both envoys are foreign-born, so watch for softened messages or defection.

T2 (Burna-Buriash). Ekallatum taken, Assyria lost an army; Assyria now shows only 1 army at ashur. Susa (walls, held by Assyria) is the target: nippur -> susa, supported by ur and durkurigalzu (strength 3 vs wall 1, or 2 if Assyria supports it from a fresh Arbela army). Ekallatum holds. Raised new armies at sippar and babylon (100 each). Retried buying Mari (350) after it failed for rival buyers last turn; Tushratta claims Mari, I told him it stays mine, so watch Mitanni at terqa. Hired c120 Sin-iqisham (Nineveh caravan master, wage 10) to use as spy on Assyria or as envoy; he may still be Assyria's man, so do not trust his reports blindly. Promises made: peace with Mitanni (sworn before Shamash, mutual pressure on Assyria), a quiet border and open road with Assyria. I intend to break the Assyria one: T3 plan is susa -> arbela with ekallatum supporting (arbela may be empty, then walk in); T4 attack ashur from arbela with ekallatum support, then nineveh. Sippar army: with ekallatum support it can take Mari (walls, needs a support) if the purchase fails. Envoys out: c46 to Egypt (arrives T3, seek gold and friendship, watch him for Hatti leanings), c51 reached Mitanni (comes home about T3-T4). Awake every turn.

orders.letter: Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Ashur-uballit of Assyria greets you. May all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I received Zitanza and gave my word before Shamash: peace on our borders. Now hear what has happened since. Babylonia fell on Ekallatum with the armies of Sippar and Dur-Kurigalzu and destroyed my garrison. Ekallatum touches your Terqa. A king who holds it will look at Terqa next. This is a common enemy. Let us act together: name a season in which your army at Terqa supports my move from Ashur into Ekallatum, and I will take Ekallatum back. I will not hinder your road to Isuwa and Carchemish. Until then your army keeps from my lands and mine from yours. Send your answer by this envoy, and tell me what you hear of Hatti and Egypt.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace on the Assyria-Mitanni borders and to joint action against Babylonia, and may ask Tushratta to name the season. May not give gold, cede land, or promise my armies without my further word.

value.notes: T2: Babylonia (sippar army + durkurigalzu support) destroyed my ekallatum army and took Ekallatum. Babylon armies seen: ekallatum, durkurigalzu, nippur, ur (4+). I have 2 armies (ashur, nineveh), 78 gold, net about +59/season before new costs. Orders: ashur holds; nineveh -> arbela to stop Babylon walking into empty Arbela (ties bounce, Babylon has only ekallatum adjacent to ashur/arbela). Susa (walls, bought for 350) may fall to nippur/ur/durkurigalzu with one support; I cannot stop it this turn. Next turn, if Arbela army stands, have it support Susa hold. Nineveh is now empty next to Mitanni taidu: watch Tushratta, who promised peace on borders (Terqa, Taidu, Ekallatum, Nineveh) via Zitanza; I answered in kind, and asked for news of Hatti and Egypt. Hired c114 Ammistamru of Ugarit (wage 15) and sent him to Mitanni proposing joint action: Terqa supports my ashur -> ekallatum, and I take Ekallatum back. No tablet (saves 20), no gold. If the hire/letter was rejected, c69 returns next turn (Washukanni-born, watch sympathies) and can carry it. PLAN: next turn if gold >= 100 and treasury allows, raise an army in arbela or ashur (100). Ekallatum retake needs 3 strength if durkurigalzu supports its hold. Then send envoys to Egypt and Hatti asking for gold and friendship (2 seasons each way). Dismiss Ammistamru when he returns if wage burden is too high. Do not raise armies beyond need: 30 upkeep each. Suspect Babylon is the aggressor; Yanhamu is arriving there with only peace words.

T2 (Egypt). Orders: sinai army -> gaza with delta fleet supporting (strength 2 vs walls 1); memphis army -> sinai; bought Damascus (250, uncontested, borders Tyre); hired Sin-iqisham c120 at 20 (unproven, born Nineveh, may lean Assyria). NO 3rd army: geography shows armies cannot pass bought cities (owner cannot station troops in walled cities I buy, e.g. Tyre), so land conquest beyond Megiddo is blocked; bought cities are for income, conquered ones can host troops (verify after Gaza). PLAN T3: gaza -> megiddo supported by sinai army (sinai adj megiddo). Check that Gaza stays mine after the army leaves. FLEET PLAN: need 2nd fleet. Move F1 out of delta (delta -> levantsea) and raise fleet in delta (120) T3, or T4 if the raise is rejected because delta is occupied. Then take Byblos by sea: one fleet in levantsea moves into byblos with the other supporting from syriansea. Then Amurru (fleet in byblos supports fleet from syriansea), then Ugarit. This is cheaper than buying (Byblos 300, Amurru 200, Ugarit 400). I did NOT buy Byblos: Alashiya also tried at T1 and the elders refuse rival buyers, so it failed; also buying it would block my fleet chain. Once I hold Byblos by conquest, Qadesh, Amurru and Mari are bordering and can be bought if still free. Diplomacy: Alashiya (Paser) says trade and peace and calls Byblos 'my port'. I told them Gaza, Tyre, Byblos and the Delta harbours are my sphere and sent 30 gold, which the envoy refused as a bribe but carried home as a gift. I promised nothing binding. Suspect Alashiya wants Byblos and will contest the sea. Mane (c20) returns soon: send him to Hatti (2 seasons) proposing a split, Hatti north of Ugarit/Carchemish and Egypt the south, and ask what they intend about Qadesh/Ugarit. Ashur-nadin (c27) is in Arzawa; learn his report. Use Sin-iqisham for Mitanni or Babylonia to set them against Hatti. Treasury after this turn about 191 plus income about +118 net per season.

value.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king spoke kindly: "Mane, say to my brother Napkhururiya: your words are welcome, and may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Alashiya wants peace and open roads for copper and gold, and I send no troops or ships against Egypt's homeland. I will gladly tell you of any king who does. But I cannot seal this tablet as written. Byblos is already mine, bought openly with my own gold, and I will not put my seal to words that give away what I hold. Your greeting also forgot to call you a Great King, and I assume your scribes were careless. Send me a tablet that names Egypt's homeland and Alashiya's homeland and leaves Byblos, Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru to Alashiya. I will leave Gaza, Megiddo and Damascus to you, and we will speak of Tyre. Then I will seal it gladly. Between brothers, gold goes both ways. Send gifts of pure gold with your next envoy, and I will answer in kind. Carry these words exactly as I spoke them." The king of Alashiya is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. What I saw: At the court of Alashiya, the court lives comfortably.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Arzawa. The king spoke kindly: "Pirissi, you are welcome at my court. Say to Suppiluliuma, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I note that your lord's tablet named him king of Hatti and did not name him Great King, as brothers of equal rank write; the words you spoke were better than the seal, and I take the words. Let each look to his own growth. But peace is made between equals by deeds: the road east lies open to Hatti at Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, where free cities sit without a lord, while Mitanni and Egypt grow fat. Arzawa holds Lukka and will keep what it holds. I speak of no concession there. Let Hatti keep its troops away from Mira, Seha and Apasa as it has promised, and we will keep ours away from Tuwanuwa. Your lord says great gifts will follow. A brother who speaks of gifts should send them first, in good gold of full purity, and I will answer in kind. Carry this home faithfully, and do not add to it or take from it." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king spoke kindly: "Kidin-Adad, I receive the words of my brother Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, and wish well to his household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your lord's greeting forgot to name himself a Great King; I name him one, as a brother should, and trust the omission was a scribe's. Mari is mine now; let it be quiet. Let Susa be for Karduniash, and Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh for Mitanni, and let neither of us trouble the other there. Send me word of what your chariots do at Ekallatum. Carry this faithfully, and say that Tushratta repays friends." The king of Mitanni is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: At the court of Mitanni, the court is rich. Artessupa, envoy of Assyria, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, king of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Your words are welcome, and they match what my own envoy Kidin-Adad carries to you. Let there be peace between Mitanni and Karduniash, sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths. If Assyria marches on either of us, we speak at once and each presses it from his own side. On the free cities, know that Mari is already under my hand and stays there, so do not count it yours. Isuwa and Carchemish I do not contest. Susa lies on my side, and I thank you for leaving it to me. Assyria is hemmed between us. Do not wait on me, for I will not be idle on my side. Press from Taidu and Nineveh when your chariots are ready, and tell me by envoy when you move."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Assyria. The king said, in short: "Zitanza, you are welcome at my court. Say to Tushratta, my brother, Great King of Mitanni: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots and my horses, and I wish the same for yours. I hear your words and I answer in kind. Between Ashur and Washukanni let there be peace on the borders at Terqa, Taidu, Ekallatum and Nineveh. I will not move against the lands of Mitanni, and I ask that no army of yours stand against mine on those borders. Let Shamash, witness of oaths, hear it. What lies west is your road and your concern. What lies east is mine, and I will look to it. A brother who keeps his word will find me a good neighbour; a brother who does not will find Assyria remembers. As between brothers, I ask that you send word of what the kings of Hatti and Egypt are doing, and I will do the same."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king said: "Say to Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words please me, brother. Let there be peace between Terqa and Ashur, and let our envoys pass freely between our courts. I swear it before Shamash, witness of oaths. You ask what I desire: only that your armies stay on your side of our border, as mine will stay on mine, and that we speak honestly to each other. The free cities of the east, Susa and the lands beyond Arbela, lie open to a strong king, and I wish you well in them. I look west, and I will not trouble you there. If any third king moves against Assyria or against Mitanni, let each of us hear of it first from the other. Send your envoy again with news of your intentions, and I will answer in kind." What I saw: Mitanni keeps 4 army and 0 fleet near its capital. At the court of Mitanni, the court is rich.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said: "Yanhamu, you are welcome in Babylon. Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Babylon is an old house and values a quiet road and an open door for envoys, and I have heard your words with respect. You ask what Babylonia thinks of the other kings. A wise king judges a king by his deeds and his gifts, not by his titles. I have sent no complaint against any brother and I carry none. But the age is restless, and my brother's eyes are surely sharper than mine on the northern and western lands. Tell me, Yanhamu, what does Ashur-uballit hear of Mitanni and of Hatti? Does he think they keep their word to their neighbours? Let your king answer me plainly through you, and I will weigh it before Shamash, witness of oaths." The king said: "Yanhamu, one word more for your lord. Burna-Buriash wishes the road between Babylon and Ashur open and the border at Ekallatum and Arbela quiet, as Ashur-uballit wishes. If a captain on either side moves without his king's word, let it not be taken for the will of the throne. Let the envoys of both houses come and go in safety, and let my brother send word by you when he has weighed my question. Go in peace under the eye of Shamash." What I saw: Babylonia keeps 4 army and 0 fleet near its capital. At the court of Babylonia, the court is rich.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king said, in short: "Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and they please me. Hatti seeks peace on its western border as Arzawa does. I have sealed your tablet of brotherhood: let neither of us send armies against the homeland of the other, and let each hold what he holds. I have also heard that you will not stand in my way at Carchemish, Isuwa and Qadesh, and I will remember it. As a sign of good faith, let your troops at Mira and Seha stay where they are, as mine stay where they are. Send me word of anything stirring in the west and I will do the same for you. May Shamash, witness of oaths, keep us both." He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Hatti keeps 2 army and 1 fleet near its capital. Ili-iddina, envoy of Alashiya, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Paser, son of Memphis, you are welcome in my house. Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me. I hold you as a brother and I want trade and peace between us, copper from your ships and gold from my land. Hear my word plainly so that no quarrel rises on the sea. The cities of the southern coast, Gaza, Tyre, Byblos and the harbours that face my Delta, lie within the reach of Egypt, and I count them my sphere. Your merchants may come to them in peace and will be treated as brothers' merchants. Your ships of war near them I would see as a quarrel. In return I ask nothing of Lukka or Ugarit, nor of your own island. I send a brother's gift with you, a small one for now, and greater when I see your copper and your good faith. Before you go, tell me what Alashiya intends toward Lukka, Ugarit and the northern coast, and what your lord hears of Hatti." The king said, in short: "Paser, you are a faithful servant and I honour a man who serves his lord alone. Carry this to the King of Alashiya, my brother: I have heard your words of trade and peace and they please me. Let copper come from your ships and gold from my land, and let no quarrel rise on the sea. Byblos and the harbours of the southern coast lie in the shadow of Egypt, and I will not suffer any king to garrison them; your merchants will be welcome in them as brothers' merchants. I send you the first fruits of my regard, pure gold, with you now. Greater gifts will follow when your copper reaches my Delta. Send me word, brother, of what you hear of Hatti and of the northern coast, as I will send you what I hear. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: Egypt keeps 2 army and 1 fleet near its capital. At the court of Egypt, the court is rich. I bring the gifts the king sent you.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king spoke kindly: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I hear your words and they please me. Hatti too wants the sea quiet and honest dealing between brothers. Hatti seeks nothing from Alashiya. Let each keep his own shore: your fleets stay in the waters of Cyprus and the open sea, and mine will not trouble you there. I ask only that Alashiya not set fleets or garrisons on the coast of Kizzuwatna, and not stand between Hatti and the free cities of the Syrian coast. In return my ports stay open to your merchants and your copper. Since you speak of great gifts, brother, let them come, and I will answer them in kind with honour. Tell me in your next message what Alashiya hears of Egypt and Mitanni, and I will tell you what I learn. Go safely, and be received well on your road home." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it.
I am Ehli-Teshub of Carchemish, once a caravan master. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.
I am Tehip-tilla of Arrapha, once a copper trader. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord Burna-Buriash. He says: "Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to his brother the Great King of Egypt: may your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses and your country prosper. Our fathers sent each other daughters and gifts and kept friendship. I wish the same between us. Gold in your land is as dust; let my brother send gold in good weight and fineness, as a brother's gift, and I will answer in kind as I am able." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets his brother of Assyria and wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Mitanni lies between us, rich in Washukanni and Harran, and it has few friends. Hatti proposes that Assyria and Hatti be brothers in fact: neither will raise a hand against the other, and we will watch Mitanni together, you from the east and I from the west. Tell me what you intend in the east, and what Assyria would wish from Hatti. Send your answer back with my envoy." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Brother of Arzawa, may your household, sons, chariots and horses be well. Egypt is far, but a great king sees who grows too proud in the north. Hatti sits upon the roads between us. Let us be friends: peace between our lands, news shared, and no gold or help given to Hatti by either. I send greetings now and will send more when I hear your answer."

Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I receive your words gladly. Assyria will raise no hand against Hatti, and I ask the same of you. Let Shamash, witness of oaths, hear it. As to the east: I seek only to keep what is mine and to recover what was taken from me by treachery. Babylonia has struck at my land of Ekallatum without cause, and I would know what Hatti hears of Babylonia and of Egypt. I keep my borders in good order and I weigh every neighbour by his deeds, not his words. What I wish from Hatti: your friendship in fact, news of what moves in Mitanni and Babylonia, and a gift of gold between brothers, that my army may stand and our friendship be seen. Send word at once of anything that threatens either of us. Send your answer back with my envoy, and I will send mine in return.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully, exactly as spoken, and bring back what you hear in Hatti of Mitanni, Babylonia and Egypt.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

Tattamaru, you are welcome at my court. Say to Burna-Buriash, my brother, king of Karduniash: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I note that your greeting did not name you Great King. I take it for a scribe's slip, since I count you my brother and my equal. Our fathers kept friendship and I wish it between us. You say gold is as dust in my land. The Nile gives gold, but it is also spent on my armies, my fleets and my cities, and my brother's own messengers have not yet told me what the friendship is for. A brother's gift follows a brother's deed. Send me word, quickly and truly, of what Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria are doing: their troops, their quarrels, and whom they court. Tell me what Karduniash intends toward them. Send an envoy of rank with honest reports, and I will answer with gifts worthy of both our houses. I send no gold now, because it would only be a bargain struck blind. Carry this home faithfully, physician, and do not embellish it.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tarhundaradu. He says: "Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets his brother of Egypt. May your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Arzawa holds the western coast and watches Hatti from behind. I seek your friendship and ask that gold, which is as dust in your land, be sent to seal it; in return I will send you word of Hatti's movements."

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words are good and I have sealed your tablet. Arzawa and Egypt are friends, and neither will aid Hatti against the other. You are right that Hatti grows too proud on the roads of the north, and I will share with you what I learn of his armies. Share with me what you learn of him in Qadesh, Carchemish and the Syrian coast. Between brothers, gifts are the measure of respect: send me gold of full purity with your next envoy, and I will answer in kind when my treasury allows. Send your envoys often and I will receive them well.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: Napkhururiya of Egypt greets you. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words are received with honor and I too wish friendship between our lands. In my country gold is plentiful, but between brothers friendship is sealed by deeds and by true word, not by weight alone. Send me what you promise: tell me plainly where Hatti keeps its armies, whether they gather toward Tuwanuwa, Kizzuwatna or the Syrian lands, and what Arzawa intends about Lukka. When your word proves true, my gifts will follow, and they will not be small. I ask that your envoys come again with this news. I make no claim on your western coast, and I ask nothing of you against anyone yet. Shamash is witness to the goodwill of Egypt.
I will carry your words to my lord.

orders.letter: Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Arzawa wishes friendship with Alashiya across the sea. Hatti sits upon the northern roads and grows proud; we should neither of us give him gold or help. Let us share news of his ships and armies on the Cilician sea, and I will do the same. Between brothers, gifts are the measure of respect: send me gold of full purity with your envoy, and I will answer in kind when my treasury allows. Seal this tablet with me.
orders.mandate: May agree to a tablet of friendship and shared news, and that neither aids Hatti against the other. May not promise gold, troops, ships or any war.

proposal.text: Alashiya and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Neither aids Hatti against the other. Each shares news of threats on the Cilician and Western seas with the other.

orders.letter: Say to Tushratta, my brother: Assyria thanks you for your good words and keeps the peace between Terqa and Ashur, Taidu and Nineveh, sworn before Shamash. You asked that each of us hear first from the other of any third king who moves. Hear it then: Babylonia took Ekallatum from me without cause, and then Susa, and her armies now stand at Ekallatum and Susa, a hand's breadth from Ashur and from your Terqa. A king who takes Ekallatum will look next to Terqa. Brother, let us act together. In the second season from now (turn 5) let your army in Terqa support my army of Ashur moving into Ekallatum, and I will retake it. I ask no gold, only that support. Until then, if Babylon strikes at Ashur or Arbela, let Terqa support my army, and I will support yours the same. Mari lies open beside your Terqa; I will not oppose you if you take it. Send your answer back by Artessupa.
orders.mandate: May agree to a joint attack on Ekallatum on turn 5 (Terqa supports Ashur into Ekallatum), to mutual support in defence, and to non-aggression on the Terqa-Ashur and Taidu-Nineveh borders. May not give gold or land. Bring back his exact answer and what he sees of Babylon.

orders.letter: Say to Burna-Buriash, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Assyria too wants the road open and the border quiet. You ask what I hear of Mitanni and Hatti. Both have sent me words of peace and so far kept them; I judge every king by his deeds. By deeds I judge you also, brother: your captain took Ekallatum, a city of my homeland, and then Susa. You say a captain who moves without his king's word does not speak for the throne. Then let the throne prove it: withdraw the army from Ekallatum and return the city, and the border at Arbela and Ashur will be as quiet as you wish. Until then my armies stay close to my own borders. Send your answer by Yanhamu.
orders.mandate: May listen and report what he sees. May agree that Babylonia withdraws from Ekallatum and returns it, and that the envoys pass freely. May not give gold or land, and may not promise anything about Mitanni or Hatti.

orders.letter: Say to the Pharaoh, my brother: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have not yet sent to you across the long road, and now I do. Babylonia strikes at my land while Mitanni and Hatti circle one another, and a strong brother in the south has an interest that no single king rules the north and east. Send a gift of gold between brothers, that my army may stand and our friendship be seen, and tell me what Egypt intends toward Babylonia and in Canaan. I will answer gifts in kind and send word at once of anything that threatens either of us.
orders.mandate: May offer friendship and free passage of envoys, and ask for a gift of gold. May promise no land, no troops and no war. Bring back what he hears of Egypt's intentions.

orders.letter: Brother Napkhururiya, your words and your gift are welcome. Alashiya wants trade and peace: copper from my ships, gold from your land. Know that Byblos has accepted my rule as a harbour of merchants. I keep no garrison there and Egypt's merchants will be received as brothers' merchants. I intend no quarrel with your Delta, Gaza or Tyre, and my fleets keep to Cyprus waters. Of Hatti I hear this: Suppiluliuma says he seeks nothing from Alashiya, but asks that I not stand between Hatti and the free cities of the Syrian coast, and that I keep off Kizzuwatna. Hatti has eyes on that coast. Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa. Send me what you hear of Arzawa and Hatti, as I send you. I send a tablet for our two seals: peace between our lands and ships, and word shared of any aggressor. Greater gifts of pure gold I will take as a mark of your regard, and answer in kind.
orders.mandate: May agree to and seal the peace tablet as written, and to share news. May not promise gold, ships or troops, may not agree to give up or share Byblos or any other city, and may not speak ill of any king beyond what is said here.

proposal.text: Tablet between Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Egypt and Alashiya send no troops or ships of war against each other's lands, Byblos held by Alashiya as a harbour open to the merchants of Egypt included. Each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Trade in copper and gold goes freely between us. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Brother, King of Arzawa: Alashiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I hear Lukka is now yours. I want peace on the Western Sea and the Great Green. My fleets keep to Cyprus waters, and I ask that yours keep from my shores. Let copper and good words pass between us. Tell me what Arzawa intends toward Hatti and the coast, and what you hear of Egypt, and I will tell you what I hear. Hatti says it seeks nothing from me but wants the free cities of the Syrian coast. If Arzawa wishes an understanding for quiet seas, I will hear it.
orders.mandate: May listen, ask Arzawa's intentions and say that Alashiya wants peace and news exchanged. May not promise gold, ships, troops or cities, and may not seal any tablet.

orders.letter: Thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother. I thank you for naming me Great King; the omission was a scribe's and is mended. Susa is mine, as you counselled; Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are yours and I will not trouble you there. My chariots now march from Ekallatum on Arbela, and then on Ashur, against our common foe, as we agreed. Mari I hold as mine; let our captains not bid against each other for it. Brother, Assyria has few armies. If your army at Terqa supports my march into Ashur, and your men at Taidu go against Nineveh, then Nineveh is yours and Ashur and Arbela mine. Send word of the season you will march. Karduniash repays friends as Mitanni does.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sworn tablet dividing Assyria: Karduniash gets Ashur, Arbela, Ekallatum; Mitanni gets Nineveh; Susa and Mari to Karduniash; Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh to Mitanni; armies support each other against Assyria. May promise nothing in gold, land or troops, and may not accept any clause giving up Susa, Ekallatum or Mari.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni, brothers and Great Kings, swear before Shamash: Susa and Mari are Karduniash's; Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are Mitanni's. Of the lands of Assyria, Ashur, Arbela and Ekallatum go to Karduniash and Nineveh to Mitanni. Each shall support the other's armies against Assyria, and neither shall march against the lands of the other.

Envoy c51 sent to Mitanni (arrives T4, back T5): claimed Great King (Tushratta noted my greeting omitted it), proposed sealed tablet: Susa and Mari to Karduniash, Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh to Mitanni, Ashur/Arbela/Ekallatum to me, Nineveh to Mitanni, mutual support vs Assyria. Asked terqa to support my move into Ashur. I cannot take Ashur (hold 1 + nineveh support = 2) without Mitanni's support.
