T4 plan: if arbela fell, arbela -> ashur supported by ekallatum (or terqa if Mitanni agrees); keep susa guarding arbela's flank. Awake every turn.

orders.letter: Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to Burna-Buriash, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. I have your words and they are welcome. Isuwa's walls have fallen and it is mine. As you counsel, I move from Taidu on Nineveh, and I tell you before you ask. Press Assyria from Ekallatum, Arbela and Ashur, and I press from the north. On Mari I speak plainly: the elders would not choose between your purse and mine, and Assyria rejoices at such quarrels. Mari touches my Terqa and my road to Qadesh. I ask you to hold your purse back from Mari. Let Ashur, Arbela and Susa be yours; let Nineveh, Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh be mine. Seal the tablet my envoy brings. Neither of us marches on the other, as sworn before Shamash. Tell me by envoy when you move on Ashur.
orders.mandate: May agree to the partition of Assyria and the free cities as written, and to joint pressure on Assyria. May not cede any province, give troops, or promise gold.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni, brothers, divide the lands of Assyria and the free cities thus: to Karduniash, Ashur, Arbela and Susa; to Mitanni, Nineveh, Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh. Neither shall march an army against the lands of the other, nor contest the share of the other. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to the Great King of Hatti, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Isuwa was a free city and its walls have fallen to me; it is now Mitanni's. I ask nothing of Hattusa, Kanesh or Sapinuwa, and I seek peace between our armies on the borders of Isuwa and Harran, sworn before Shamash and Teshub. Let us each send word of what the kings of Egypt and Arzawa are doing, as brothers do. Send your envoy to Washukanni and he will be received with honour.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace and exchange of news on the Isuwa and Harran borders. May not cede any province, promise troops, or bind Mitanni against Egypt, Arzawa or Babylonia.

value.notes: T3 (Tushratta). FACTS: Isuwa taken T2 (walls fell), now mine with army. Assyria army moved nineveh->arbela; NINEVEH WAS EMPTY, ashur army holds. Assyria (via Zitanza) asked peace on Terqa/Taidu/Ekallatum/Nineveh borders; I intend to BREAK it by taking Nineveh (35 yield) since it is empty; Babylonia urged me to press Assyria. T3 ORDERS: taidu->nineveh; washukanni->taidu (so next turn taidu army supports nineveh hold vs ashur+arbela attack); terqa holds; isuwa holds (unsupported; Hatti armies at kanesh and sapinuwa could hit it 2v1 - risk accepted); raised army at HARRAN (empty); buy mari 350 again (rival buyers last time, Babylonia claims it; Egypt at damascus could also bid); hire Ehli-Teshub c125 at 16 (declined 14). Envoys: Ubaru c57 -> Babylonia with partition tablet (Mitanni: Nineveh, Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh; Babylonia: Ashur, Arbela, Susa) and told them I move on Nineveh; Zitanza c62 -> Hatti for peace at Isuwa/Harran (no gold, treasury about 27 after buys). NEXT: T4 if Nineveh taken, taidu army supports nineveh hold; new harran army can support isuwa; send envoys to Egypt (gold, brotherhood) and Arzawa (Hatti's western foe) when Ubaru/Zitanza/Ehli-Teshub free. Do NOT attack Carchemish until Hatti's intent is known and I have a 6th army (isuwa would be left open to kanesh/sapinuwa). Washukanni is interior (only neighbours isuwa, harran, taidu, terqa) so safe empty. Watch Babylonia at ekallatum next to Terqa: oath k183 but they hold Ekallatum and claim Mari. Upkeep 5 armies=150 vs income 175+. Suspicions: Ubaru Sippar-born may favour Babylonia; Ehli-Teshub Carchemish-born; Kidin-Adad took my 10.

orders.letter: To my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, thanks you for your open words. My scribes were careless with your title and I take no offence at your correction; you are my brother and my equal. Egypt wants peace and open roads for copper and gold. I send no troops or ships against Alashiya's homeland, and I will not move against Byblos while you keep the same toward Egypt. Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru I do not claim. Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus and Tyre are Egypt's; Qadesh and Mari lie on Egypt's road and I mean to hold them. A tablet in these words will follow with my next envoy, to be sealed by us both. Tell me freely of any king whose ships or troops come near your coasts or mine, as you offered, and I will do the same for you. I send no gold this time; when your words are proved in deed, my gifts will be pure and weighty. Carry this exactly as I spoke it.
orders.mandate: Mane may agree, as spoken words only, that the homelands of Egypt and Alashiya are not attacked; that Byblos, Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru are Alashiya's sphere; and that Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Tyre, Qadesh and Mari are Egypt's. He may not promise gold, troops or ships, and may not seal anything without my tablet.

orders.letter: To my brother, the Great King of Hatti: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Egypt holds Gaza, Damascus, Tyre and soon Megiddo and Qadesh, and wants the southern road quiet. I seek nothing north of Qadesh and have no designs on Kizzuwatna, Carchemish or your homeland. Let Hatti keep the north and Egypt the south, and let the roads stay open for traders and envoys. I hear that Arzawa has taken Tuwanuwa, which is your land, and that its king sends me envoys asking for gold, boasting that he watches Hatti from behind. I have sent him nothing. Tell me truly where your armies stand, what you intend toward Arzawa, Mitanni and Assyria, and whom you fear. A brother who sends true word will find Egypt's gifts worthy of his house. Carry this faithfully.
orders.mandate: Sin-iqisham may agree, as spoken words only, that Egypt's sphere is Qadesh and everything south, and Hatti's is the north; that envoys pass freely. He may not promise gold, troops or any act against a third king, and may not seal anything.

value.notes: T3 (Egypt). Orders: gaza army -> megiddo, sinai army supports it (strength 2 vs walls 1); delta fleet holds; bought Qadesh (300, leaves ~9 gold; income next season ~310 vs upkeep 95 + wages 47). Qadesh is safe: its neighbours Carchemish (Hatti bought, walls, no troops), Byblos (Alashiya bought, walls) and my Damascus cannot host enemy troops, so only Ugarit/Amurru/Mari could stage an attack. Mari (350) is exposed to Babylonia (sippar, ekallatum) and Mitanni (terqa): do NOT buy it unless the neighbours look harmless. I skipped the Alashiya tablet this turn (scribe 20 would have blocked the 300 purchase); SEND IT NEXT SEASON: text naming Egypt's and Alashiya's homelands inviolate, Byblos/Lukka/Ugarit/Amurru in Alashiya's sphere, Gaza/Megiddo/Damascus/Tyre/Qadesh/Mari in Egypt's, plus a small pure gift (20-30). Non-binding: I can break it if Byblos becomes takeable. LETTERS: c20 Mane -> Alashiya (1 season, accepts the sphere deal verbally, no gold, no tablet). c120 Sin-iqisham -> Hatti (2 seasons): proposes Egypt south of Qadesh and Hatti north, points out that Arzawa took Tuwanuwa and asks Arzawa's gold; ask for Hatti's troop news. He was born in Nineveh and costs 20: watch his report for Assyrian bias. NEXT: Ashur-nadin (c27) comes home from Arzawa, so read his report, then send him to Mitanni or Assyria. Envoys wait for answers from Babylonia (Tattamaru told to bring word on Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria) and Arzawa (Mazipalali told to report Hatti's armies). I told them I would send gifts only after proof. THE MAP: my bought cities (Damascus, Tyre) cannot host troops, so armies cannot pass them. Megiddo, once conquered, can. The remaining free cities (Amurru, Ugarit) are reachable only by fleets, and a take needs two fleets adjacent. Babylonia took Ekallatum and Susa, Arzawa took Tuwanuwa and Lukka, Hatti took Carchemish, Mitanni took Isuwa; Babylonia and Arzawa are the fastest growers, so encourage Hatti against Arzawa and Assyria/Mitanni against Babylonia. Consider disbanding one army (30 upkeep) once Megiddo is secure. Check that Gaza stays mine with no army in it.

orders.letter: Brother of Mitanni, Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hear what befell me. The king of Arzawa swore before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk that he would send no army against my homeland, and in the very same season his army, with Lukka's help, took Tuwanuwa. Here is the sealed tablet; judge for yourself what his seal is worth to any brother. Hatti seeks no quarrel with Mitanni. I propose that neither of us sends armies against the other's homeland provinces nor against Carchemish, so that each may deal with those who break their oaths. Send your answer by my envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed tablet that neither king sends armies against the other's homeland provinces or Carchemish. May NOT promise gold, land, troops, or any alliance against a third power. Must report faithfully exactly what the king of Mitanni answers, and bring back any sealed copy.

proposal.text: Tablet between Hatti and Mitanni. Neither king shall send his armies against the homeland provinces of the other, nor against Carchemish. Sworn before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk.

value.notes: T3: Arzawa BROKE k189 the same season it was sealed: mira->tuwanuwa supported by lukka, my tuwanuwa army destroyed, Tuwanuwa lost. Their king's words ('we will keep ours away from Tuwanuwa') were a lie; Pirissi's 'all is well, I am certain' was naive or flattering, do not trust his reading of courts. Mitanni took Isuwa (my planned target) with a harran army; Isuwa army now sits next to sapinuwa/kanesh/carchemish. Treasury only 88 so cannot raise (100) this turn; next season about 88-20+71=139. DEFENCE T3: sapinuwa->hattusa (capital was empty and next to Arzawa army at tuwanuwa), kanesh supports kizzuwatna hold (Arzawa tuwanuwa+lukka could hit kizzuwatna with strength 2), fleet holds. Sapinuwa left empty (only Mitanni isuwa touches it). Sent Pirissi (c39) to Mitanni: homeland+Carchemish non-aggression tablet, showed k189 as proof Arzawa breaks seals; claimed Great King (Arzawa slighted me for writing only 'king'). Mandate tight: no gold, land, troops. Pirissi was born in Washukanni: watch for leaks/defection. PLAN T4: raise army in sapinuwa (empty) with the new gold. RETAKE TUWANUWA: army hattusa -> tuwanuwa, kanesh supports it, fleet kizzuwatna -> lukka (a move on lukka cuts lukka's support of tuwanuwa), needs hold strength at tuwanuwa to be 1; if Arzawa has a unit at mira/seha too, need a third supporter (new army). Do not leave hattusa or kanesh empty while an Arzawa army stands in tuwanuwa. Keliya (c32) is on the road home from Assyria; wait for his report. Later: Isuwa (no walls now, held by one Mitanni army), Qadesh, Ugarit. Alashiya has promised gifts, none yet. Promises made: none binding except k189 (void, Arzawa broke it).

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Brother Napkhururiya, your words and your gift are welcome. Alashiya wants trade and peace: copper from my ships, gold from your land. Know that Byblos has accepted my rule as a harbour of merchants. I keep no garrison there and Egypt's merchants will be received as brothers' merchants. I intend no quarrel with your Delta, Gaza or Tyre, and my fleets keep to Cyprus waters. Of Hatti I hear this: Suppiluliuma says he seeks nothing from Alashiya, but asks that I not stand between Hatti and the free cities of the Syrian coast, and that I keep off Kizzuwatna. Hatti has eyes on that coast. Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa. Send me what you hear of Arzawa and Hatti, as I send you. I send a tablet for our two seals: peace between our lands and ships, and word shared of any aggressor. Greater gifts of pure gold I will take as a mark of your regard, and answer in kind." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of Tushratta, and I am, as ever, your servant. He says: "Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to the Great King of Hatti, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Isuwa was a free city and its walls have fallen to me; it is now Mitanni's. I ask nothing of Hattusa, Kanesh or Sapinuwa, and I seek peace between our armies on the borders of Isuwa and Harran, sworn before Shamash and Teshub. Let us each send word of what the kings of Egypt and Arzawa are doing, as brothers do." For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, to Burna-Buriash, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. I have your words and they are welcome. Isuwa's walls have fallen and it is mine. As you counsel, I move from Taidu on Nineveh, and I tell you before you ask. Press Assyria from Ekallatum, Arbela and Ashur, and I press from the north. On Mari I speak plainly: the elders would not choose between your purse and mine, and Assyria rejoices at such quarrels. Mari touches my Terqa and my road to Qadesh. I ask you to hold your purse back from Mari. Let Ashur, Arbela and Susa be yours; let Nineveh, Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh be mine. Seal the tablet my envoy brings. Neither of us marches on the other, as sworn before Shamash."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "Brother of Mitanni, Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hear what befell me. The king of Arzawa swore before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk that he would send no army against my homeland, and in the very same season his army, with Lukka's help, took Tuwanuwa. Here is the sealed tablet; judge for yourself what his seal is worth to any brother. Hatti seeks no quarrel with Mitanni. I propose that neither of us sends armies against the other's homeland provinces nor against Carchemish, so that each may deal with those who break their oaths." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Brother, King of Arzawa: Alashiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I hear Lukka is now yours. I want peace on the Western Sea and the Great Green. My fleets keep to Cyprus waters, and I ask that yours keep from my shores. Let copper and good words pass between us. Tell me what Arzawa intends toward Hatti and the coast, and what you hear of Egypt, and I will tell you what I hear. Hatti says it seeks nothing from me but wants the free cities of the Syrian coast." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "To my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, thanks you for your open words. My scribes were careless with your title and I take no offence at your correction; you are my brother and my equal. Egypt wants peace and open roads for copper and gold. I send no troops or ships against Alashiya's homeland, and I will not move against Byblos while you keep the same toward Egypt. Lukka, Ugarit and Amurru I do not claim. Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus and Tyre are Egypt's; Qadesh and Mari lie on Egypt's road and I mean to hold them. A tablet in these words will follow with my next envoy, to be sealed by us both. Tell me freely of any king whose ships or troops come near your coasts or mine, as you offered, and I will do the same for you. I send no gold this time; when your words are proved in deed, my gifts will be pure and weighty. Carry this exactly as I spoke it." For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

To Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. I have heard your words and they please me. Let there be peace between our armies on the borders of Harran, Isuwa and Carchemish, sworn before Shamash and Teshub: I send nothing against Harran or Washukanni, and you send nothing against Hattusa, Kanesh, Sapinuwa or Carchemish. As brothers share news: the king of Arzawa swore a tablet of brotherhood with me and broke it the same season, taking Tuwanuwa by treachery. His seal is worth nothing. Of Egypt I know nothing yet. Tell me what you learn of Arzawa's armies and I will tell you what I learn. Your envoy is honoured here.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Napkhururiya, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my chariots and my country, and I wish the same to yours. I accept your words. I send no troops or ships against Egypt, and I will not move against Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus or Tyre while you keep the same toward Alashiya and Byblos. I have heard that you claim nothing of Lukka, Ugarit or Amurru, and I hold your words as spoken before Shamash. Send the tablet with your next envoy and I will read it with care; let it say that neither king sends troops or war ships against the other's lands, and that Byblos stays an open harbour for merchants. I will tell you freely of any king whose ships or troops come near our coasts, and I ask the same of you. Copper will go to Egypt on open roads, and I look to receive pure, weighty gold in return. Carry this exactly as I spoke it.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tarhundaradu. He says: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Arzawa wishes friendship with Alashiya across the sea. Hatti sits upon the northern roads and grows proud; we should neither of us give him gold or help. Let us share news of his ships and armies on the Cilician sea, and I will do the same. Between brothers, gifts are the measure of respect: send me gold of full purity with your envoy, and I will answer in kind when my treasury allows. Seal this tablet with me."

Ili-iddina, you are welcome. Say to the king of Alashiya, my brother: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I note that your greeting did not call you a Great King. I take it as a scribe's haste, for I count you a brother and an equal. Peace on the Western Sea and the Great Green pleases me. My ships have no business near Cyprus, and I will keep them off your shores as you ask. Let copper and good words pass between us. As for Hatti: he sent me words of peace while his armies stood on my border. Lukka and Tuwanuwa are now mine, and I press him while he is weak. He says he wants only the Syrian coast. Brother, whoever holds Ugarit and Kizzuwatna has fleets facing Cyprus. It serves you that Hatti is kept busy in the west and that no ship or grain of yours reaches him. Of Egypt I hear only friendly words and no armies. Now tell me what you hear of Hatti's fleets and of Egypt's intentions, and send the copper and the gifts your messenger promises, in good pure gold or metal, as brothers do. I will answer gift with gift.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and seen the tablet of Arzawa; a king who breaks an oath before Shamash has made his own seal worthless, and I will remember it. Mitanni also seeks no quarrel with Hatti. I seal your tablet: no army of mine will march on the homeland provinces of Hatti, and none of yours on mine. Know also, brother, that Isuwa is in my hand and under my protection. Let your armies at Kanesh and Sapinuwa keep to their own side, as I keep mine, and our peace will be a sound one. I make no pledge against any third king, and I ask none of you. Send your messengers freely, and they will be received with honour. Pirissi was born in my city of Washukanni and has spoken well.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words to your lord faithfully and in full, especially that Isuwa is mine and that I keep the peace.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Burna-Buriash. He says: "Thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother. I thank you for naming me Great King; the omission was a scribe's and is mended. Susa is mine, as you counselled; Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are yours and I will not trouble you there. My chariots now march from Ekallatum on Arbela, and then on Ashur, against our common foe, as we agreed. Mari I hold as mine; let our captains not bid against each other for it. Brother, Assyria has few armies. If your army at Terqa supports my march into Ashur, and your men at Taidu go against Nineveh, then Nineveh is yours and Ashur and Arbela mine. Send word of the season you will march. Karduniash repays friends as Mitanni does."

Say to the king of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your country. Your words please me and I seal the tablet before Shamash. Peace between our lands and ships. Byblos is your harbour of merchants and my merchants will use it as brothers. Egypt holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh, and I ask that Alashiya send no ships or troops against them or the Delta. In return I ask word of any king who moves on your coast. I hear Hatti covets the Syrian coast and Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa; tell me what your ships see in the Cilician and Syrian seas, and I will send you what my envoys learn of Hatti and Arzawa. I send a small pure gift as a mark of regard, and greater gifts will follow brothers who keep faith. Paser, serve both your lord and me well, and bring me his answer.
value.bribeAsk: Speak well of Egypt to your lord and bring back honest word of Alashiya's fleets and of any plan on Ugarit, Amurru or Mari.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your words are welcome, brother, and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash: no army of mine will march on Mitanni. Ashur, Arbela and Susa for Karduniash, with Ekallatum, which my chariots already hold; Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh for Mitanni. This I accept and I will not contest your share. On Mari I speak as plainly as you. It touches my Sippar and my Ekallatum as it touches your Terqa, and I cannot seal a tablet that gives away the gate of my own homeland. Let the tablet read: Mari to Karduniash, and the road through Mari to Qadesh open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. Send it back so written and I will seal it at once. Let us not quarrel before the elders of Mari; Assyria rejoices at that. Tell me the season your army stands in Nineveh, and I strike Ashur from Arbela. Keep Terqa from Ekallatum and Ashur, as brothers do.
value.bribeAsk: Plead my case on Mari before Tushratta, and report truly what you saw of his armies at Terqa and Taidu.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Ashur-uballit. He says: "Say to Burna-Buriash, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Assyria too wants the road open and the border quiet. You ask what I hear of Mitanni and Hatti. Both have sent me words of peace and so far kept them; I judge every king by his deeds. By deeds I judge you also, brother: your captain took Ekallatum, a city of my homeland, and then Susa. You say a captain who moves without his king's word does not speak for the throne. Then let the throne prove it: withdraw the army from Ekallatum and return the city, and the border at Arbela and Ashur will be as quiet as you wish. Until then my armies stay close to my own borders. Send your answer by Yanhamu."

Ili-iddina, go in peace and carry my words exactly as I spoke them. Tell the king of Alashiya, my brother, that Arzawa keeps to the Western Sea and keeps its ships from his shores, and that I look for his copper and his news of Hatti's fleets and of Egypt. A king who sends good pure gold finds me quick to answer in kind. May Shamash witness that I wish him and his household well.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I have heard your words, and Alashiya wants peace and open seas with Arzawa. I seal your tablet: we are at peace and friends, and neither aids Hatti against the other. I will send you word of what my ships and merchants see on the Cilician sea, and I ask the same of you: tell me of Hatti's armies and ships, and tell me what Arzawa intends on the coast near Lukka and Kizzuwatna. Let no Arzawan ship come against Tamassos or Enkomi, as no Alashiyan ship will come against your coast. As for gold, my treasury is spent on harbours and ships this season; when it lies fuller, I will send gifts worthy of a brother. Go in peace, and carry my greeting.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I weigh them as a brother. I want the road open and the border quiet, and I do not seek a quarrel with Assyria. The men at Ekallatum stand on a road where Mitanni's chariots at Terqa also look, and I will not leave that road empty while two neighbours watch it. Prove your peace by deeds, as you say you judge kings: let your armies stay where they are and let no chariot of Assyria cross toward Ekallatum, Susa or my homeland. Then we will speak of the matter of the cities in good faith, king to king, and send a sealed tablet between us. Send your next word by Yanhamu or another trusted man; my road is open to him and he will be honoured at my court.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words to your lord exactly and kindly: that Karduniash wants a quiet border and the matter of Ekallatum is still open between brothers.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for your words and for the Susa, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh we have already named. The oath of k183 stands: Mitanni will not march on Karduniash, and I will not shelter Assyria. Nineveh is already in my hands and my men stand there. Here is the order of the war. My army from Terqa, with my army at Nineveh beside it, goes against Ashur. It is the city nearest my men, and the Assyrian host there will be broken by it. Your chariots take Arbela and keep Ekallatum. Susa and Mari I leave to you and I will bid for neither. So Karduniash holds Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari, and Mitanni holds Nineveh and Ashur. I cannot seal the tablet as written, because it gives Ashur to you while my men are at its gate. Let your scribes write it again with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni and the rest to you, and I will seal it at once and send it back with your own envoy. Send me the season your chariots go against Arbela, and I will be at Ashur in the same season. Karduniash and Mitanni are brothers, and the Assyrian is the foe of both.
value.bribeAsk: Tell Burna-Buriash faithfully that Mitanni marches on Ashur this season and that Ashur and Nineveh are the price of my support, and urge him to agree and to take Arbela.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: Tushratta, your brother, wishes well to you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I do not seal the tablet as written, for it gives Ashur away while my men are at its gate, and I will not put my seal to what I would later be shamed to keep. This is no quarrel. The oath of k183 stands before Shamash: Mitanni will not march on Karduniash and will not shelter Assyria. Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are mine to seek and Susa is yours, as we have said. Nineveh is held by my men and will stay mine. Assyria is the foe of both of us. Take Arbela and keep Ekallatum, and tell me the season your chariots march, and I will be at Ashur in the same season. Let your scribes write the tablet again with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni, and I will seal it at once. Mitanni repays friends as Karduniash does.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Ashur-uballit. He says: "Say to Tushratta, my brother: Assyria thanks you for your good words and keeps the peace between Terqa and Ashur, Taidu and Nineveh, sworn before Shamash. You asked that each of us hear first from the other of any third king who moves. Hear it then: Babylonia took Ekallatum from me without cause, and then Susa, and her armies now stand at Ekallatum and Susa, a hand's breadth from Ashur and from your Terqa. A king who takes Ekallatum will look next to Terqa. Brother, let us act together. In the second season from now (turn 5) let your army in Terqa support my army of Ashur moving into Ekallatum, and I will retake it. I ask no gold, only that support. Until then, if Babylon strikes at Ashur or Arbela, let Terqa support my army, and I will support yours the same. Mari lies open beside your Terqa; I will not oppose you if you take it. Send your answer back by Artessupa."

Say to Ashur-uballit, Great King, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with yours. I have heard your words and I thank you for telling me first of the movements of a third king, as we agreed. Babylonia holds Ekallatum and Susa, and I too watch her armies from Terqa; a king who takes cities without cause is no friend to either of us. Know that my army in Terqa is not idle and that I do not forget who warned me. I make no promise of a day or a season in the mouth of an envoy, for roads are long and messengers are late; but send me word again before you move, and I will weigh your request as a brother weighs the need of his brother. Do what your own strength and your own gods advise against Ekallatum. Mari is open and I shall deal with it as I see fit. Return in good health and carry my greeting to your house.
I will carry your words to my lord faithfully.
value.commitments: said my lord will consider these words

value.notes: T4: Audiences done. Egypt (Mane): Egypt sends no troops/ships against my homeland, will not move on Byblos while I keep same toward Egypt; claims Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Tyre, Qadesh, Mari; does not claim Lukka, Ugarit, Amurru. Promised a tablet with its NEXT envoy to seal. I promised: no troops/ships against Gaza/Megiddo/Damascus/Tyre, Byblos an open harbour, share news of aggressors, copper to Egypt for pure weighty gold. Egypt sent no gold this time (Mane flatters me; Egypt gold earlier assayed 100 percent fine). Arzawa (Tarhundaradu): tablet k282 SEALED both kings - peace and friends, neither aids Hatti against the other, share news of threats on Cilician and Western seas. I refused gold for now (said treasury spent). Arzawa wants a gold gift - send a small pure gift later if useful, or a little debased. Arzawa is at war with Hatti. Rumor: harvest failed in Hatti. T4 ORDERS: fleet enkomi holds; buy amurru (200) - borders Byblos by land, same sea zone; leaves ~16 in treasury, next season income about 135 less 35 upkeep less 21 wages. No envoys at court this season so no letters. Envoys c102 (Paser, from Egypt) and c95 (Ili-iddina, from Arzawa) come home T5: read their reports with suspicion, then re-send them (Egypt: seal tablet / ask pure gold; Arzawa or Babylonia/Mitanni/Assyria for contacts). Remaining free targets: ugarit 400 (borders Hatti's Kizzuwatna - Hatti wants it), mari unreachable. After amurru, save for ugarit. Check next season that amurru purchase landed (rival buyers made T1 fail; Hatti also eyes Amurru/Ugarit). Watch Egypt troops at Qadesh/Byblos and Hatti fleets at Kizzuwatna. No army yet; raise one at tamassos (100) only if foreign troops approach. Not hiring candidates (30-35 a season too dear).

T4: Drought halves MY income for 3 seasons (T4-T6): income 94 vs upkeep 95 + wages 19 = about -20 a season. Treasury 48 -> about 28 (T5) -> about 8 (T6) -> back to roughly +71 a season from T7 (full income about 185). DO NOT SPEND beyond ~25 total before T7 (no tablets at 20, no raises) or troops desert. Cannot afford to raise an army now. Arzawa attacked hattusa from tuwanuwa on T3 and bounced against my sapinuwa->hattusa move (hattusa was empty). Hattusa can only be attacked from tuwanuwa (strength 1, no supporter can reach it), so one army there is safe. Kizzuwatna: fleet + kanesh support = 2, equals the max Arzawa can send (lukka + tuwanuwa support), so it holds on ties. T4 orders: sapinuwa -> hattusa (bounces or occupies, hattusa stays mine either way), kanesh supports kizzuwatna hold, fleet holds. Sapinuwa left empty next to Mitanni isuwa army: watch it. Mitanni (Tushratta via envoy Zitanza) offered peace on Isuwa/Harran borders; I replied accepting and promised to send nothing against Harran/Washukanni; asked for news of Arzawa. I told Mitanni Arzawa broke k189 the same season. c62 Zitanza (Mitanni's envoy) is secretly in my pay, so his word to me is probably reliable. Pirissi (c39) is carrying the homeland + Carchemish non-aggression tablet to Mitanni, 1 season; Keliya (c32) is coming home from Assyria with his report. Both were born in Washukanni, so watch for Mitanni leaks. No envoy was at court to send letters this turn. PLAN T5: if hattusa army is in place and Arzawa still has only about 1-2 armies near, retake Tuwanuwa: hattusa -> tuwanuwa, kanesh supports it, fleet kizzuwatna -> lukka to cut lukka's support of tuwanuwa. Only do it if tuwanuwa hold is 1 (no Arzawa unit in mira/seha supporting) and kizzuwatna is not left exposed to a strength-2 attack. Otherwise keep defending until gold returns, then raise armies (sapinuwa or hattusa) and retake Tuwanuwa, then Isuwa/Ugarit/Qadesh. Promises binding: none except the Mitanni border peace (verbal) and k189 (Arzawa broke it, void).

T4 (Burna-Buriash). T3 result: ekallatum->arbela bounced (2 vs arbela 1+ashur support 2). Assyria keeps ashur supporting arbela, arbela holding; I cannot break that alone because only ekallatum and susa touch arbela, and nothing of mine but ekallatum touches ashur. It only breaks if Mitanni (terqa or nineveh) attacks ashur and cuts its support while I hit arbela with susa + ekallatum support. Mitanni already holds Nineveh and Isuwa; Assyria is down to arbela and ashur, 2 armies. T4 orders: take Mari by force (sippar -> mari, ekallatum supports; Mari wall 1, Mitanni has only terqa next to it so cannot beat 2), AND bid 350 for Mari so Mitanni cannot buy it alone (two bidders = both fail, no cost). Durkurigalzu supports ekallatum hold, nippur supports susa hold, babylon -> sippar backfill. No envoy at court so no letters; asked for candidates to get new envoys (Egypt gifts, Hatti contact). PROMISES: sworn non-aggression with Mitanni (k204) - kept so far, Mari is a free city, not theirs; I told Ubaru Mari goes to Karduniash with free tolls for Mitanni caravans. I told Assyria the border would be quiet - deliberately false. SUSPICIONS: Tushratta wants Mari and Terqa borders Ekallatum/Mari; he cannot beat my supported ekallatum with one army. If Mari falls to me, expect a cold reply from Mitanni. Option later: strike Terqa (30) from mari with ekallatum support if it holds a lone army, only after Assyria is settled. Surplus armies (babylon, nippur) cost 30 each per season; consider disbanding one if Mitanni stays peaceful. c46 Tattamaru returning (Hatti-born): hear Egypt gold report. c51 reaches Mitanni now, back T5. Awake every turn.

T4: Tuwanuwa->Hattusa failed at T3 although Hattusa shows no Hatti unit, so probably a hidden Hatti army at Sapinuwa moved in and bounced me (guess). Hatti has seen kanesh army + kizzuwatna fleet; harvest failed in Hatti (weak, maybe unpaid troops). T4 ORDERS: tuwanuwa->hattusa again (free if it bounces); mira army follows into tuwanuwa, supported by lukka (strength 2 beats a Kanesh counter-step); lukka otherwise holds; seha fleet -> westsea (pre-position toward greatgreen/cilicia to support a strike on Kizzuwatna: tuwanuwa/lukka army attacks kizzuwatna, other army + cilicia fleet support = 3 vs fleet 1 + kanesh support 1); RAISE 4th army at apasa (100) to feed the front; treasury 205 -> 105, net about -20/season until Hattusa pays. Geometry: only tuwanuwa and hattusa touch Kanesh; Hattusa can be hit only with strength 1 from Tuwanuwa, so take it when empty. CHECK next: did I take Hattusa? If yes, next turn tuwanuwa/hattusa pair attack kanesh (hattusa supports tuwanuwa->kanesh) and guard Hattusa hold with tuwanuwa support (Hatti kanesh + sapinuwa could kill a lone army at hattusa with strength 2). Envoys: c83 reaches Alashiya next season (friendship tablet, wanted gold gift); c89 returning from Egypt. No envoy at court this turn so no letters. Did NOT hire candidates c108 (30) / c125 (35): wages cut strength. Promises: told Alashiya I keep my ships off his shores (Cyprus); a fleet in cilicia/greatgreen may alarm him, reconsider at greatgreen. Hatti tablet k210 is broken in spirit; Egypt k219 friendship holds (neither aids Hatti). Watch Mitanni at isuwa grabbing Hatti land first.

T4: Crisis. Lost Nineveh to Mitanni (taidu army walked into my empty province despite Tushratta's border peace); Babylon (ekallatum+susa) failed at Arbela last turn. I hold arbela+ashur armies, 56 gold, net about -26 a season (income 75, upkeep 60, wages 41: c69 12, c76 14, c114 15). Passive defence loses either way if Mitanni (nineveh+terqa on ashur) and Babylon (ekallatum+susa on arbela) both strike with strength 2, since I have only one support to give. Nineveh can get NO support this turn (taidu is empty, only taidu/arbela/ashur border it), so its hold is 1. ORDERS: arbela -> nineveh, ashur supports arbela -> nineveh (strength 2 destroys the Mitanni army and retakes Nineveh +35). Risk: Babylon walks into empty Arbela (-30), or Mitanni terqa/nineveh hits Ashur and cuts the support. No envoy was at court so no letters this turn. NEXT: c69 and c76 come home about turn 5 with Mitanni and Babylon replies; read them. Then send an envoy to Hatti (2 seasons) proposing joint pressure on Mitanni and asking for gold, and to Egypt for gold. Dismiss c69 and c76 when home if there is no use (wages run to turn 10) to stop the bleed; keep c114 (Egypt, arrives T5, back T7). Cannot afford a 3rd army (100) until gold recovers. Promises: peace with Hatti; the Mitanni border peace is broken by their taking Nineveh. If Nineveh is retaken, consider Ashur+Nineveh+Arbela all within reach; if Babylon empties Ekallatum to take Arbela, retake Ekallatum with ashur.

T4 (Tushratta). FACTS: Nineveh taken T3, mine. Armies: harran, isuwa, nineveh, taidu, terqa (5, upkeep 150). Washukanni empty (interior). Treasury 401; failed Mari buys cost nothing. Hatti sealed k275 (no Mitanni march on Hatti homeland or Carchemish) - I sealed it this turn but I am BREAKING the Carchemish clause now: Hatti has harvest failure and war with Arzawa (Arzawa took Tuwanuwa), Carchemish is empty, walls need 2 strength. Risk: Hatti kanesh/kizzuwatna may support Carchemish walls (then bounce, no loss). Isuwa is not my homeland so Hatti may attack it from kanesh+sapinuwa; isuwa unit supports the attack so defends at 1. T4 ORDERS: nineveh -> ashur supported by terqa (hope Babylonia attacks arbela from ekallatum, cutting arbela's support of ashur; then ashur falls 2 v 1); taidu follows into nineveh; harran -> carchemish supported by isuwa. Buy Mari 350 (rival bidders, probably Babylonia: they asked me not to bid; if it fails, fallback raise army at washukanni 100). Hired Ehli-Teshub c125 offer 20 (he refused 10,14,16) - Carchemish-born, may leak to Hatti. No envoys at court this turn, no letters. Ubaru c57 -> Babylonia (arrives T5, carries partition tablet: Mitanni Nineveh, Ashur, Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh; Babylonia Arbela, Susa, Ekallatum), Zitanza c62 -> Hatti (peace at Isuwa/Harran; now outdated by my Carchemish move). Assyria asked me on T3 to support Ashur->Ekallatum on T5 and said Mari is open; I made no promise. NEXT (T5): if Ashur taken, hold terqa/nineveh/ashur, refill nineveh from taidu; if Carchemish taken, harran refilled by new army, then consider buying Ugarit (400) or Qadesh via Carchemish; send envoys to Egypt (gold, brotherhood) and Arzawa (ally vs Hatti: tell them I strike Hatti's east). Egypt holds 10 provinces and is the growth leader - I must out-grow it. Suspicions: Babylonia (Kidin-Adad) may take Arbela and then Terqa, they hold Ekallatum next to Terqa; Ubaru Sippar-born; Kidin-Adad took my 10.

T4 (Egypt). Holdings: akhetaten, thebes, memphis, sinai, delta (homeland) + gaza, megiddo (conquered, can host troops) + tyre, damascus, qadesh (bought, walls, cannot host troops). Yield 310/season, upkeep was 95, wages 47, treasury 157. Alashiya tablet k284 sealed this turn (peace; Byblos is their harbour; I may break it only if Byblos becomes cheap to take; no promises binding). No envoy of mine is at court this turn so no letters. ORDERS T4: disbanded the sinai army (interior, useless, saves 30/season; re-raise costs 100 in an empty homeland province if a threat shows); moved the megiddo army to gaza (coastal front: supports Tyre, Delta, Megiddo, and a lone fleet cannot take Gaza); delta fleet holds (watches greatgreen and levantsea). Net income next season about 310-65-47 = ~198, so treasury about 355 at T5. BUY PLAN: remaining free cities are Amurru (200, only Alashiya can contest it), Ugarit (400, contested by Hatti, Alashiya, Arzawa), Mari (350, exposed to Babylonia and Mitanni via terqa, ekallatum, sippar: buy last or never; if a rival conquers it it becomes a staging post against Damascus and Qadesh). T5: if Ugarit is still free and I have ~400 buy it, otherwise buy Amurru (200); then the other. Payback of a city is 10 seasons, game expected to last to about turn 20, so buy early. Conquering is free but needs 2 fleets adjacent; Amurru is hard (only syriansea open to me), Ugarit needs fleets in syriansea and cilicia. Byblos (Alashiya, 300) is the only foe-held target in reach: needs a 2nd fleet (120) - not now. ENVOYS: Mane c20 (to/from Alashiya), Ashur-nadin c27 (back from Arzawa, born in Ashur, may lean Assyria), Sin-iqisham c120 (to Hatti, arrives ~T5, born Nineveh, watch for Assyrian bias). Wages 47 until turn 10. Unhired candidates: c108 Tehip-tilla (28), c125 Ehli-Teshub (33). When envoys come home read their reports; plan to open contact with Mitanni and Assyria (nobody sent yet) and encourage Hatti against Arzawa and Mitanni/Assyria against Babylonia. Rivals growing by conquest: Arzawa (Lukka, Tuwanuwa), Mitanni (Isuwa, Nineveh), Babylonia (Ekallatum, Susa). Watch for any foreign fleet in levantsea or greatgreen: if two appear raise an army in memphis/sinai (100) and have gaza/delta supports ready.

value.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Arzawa. The king said: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words are good and I have sealed your tablet. Arzawa and Egypt are friends, and neither will aid Hatti against the other. You are right that Hatti grows too proud on the roads of the north, and I will share with you what I learn of his armies. Share with me what you learn of him in Qadesh, Carchemish and the Syrian coast. Between brothers, gifts are the measure of respect: send me gold of full purity with your next envoy, and I will answer in kind when my treasury allows. Send your envoys often and I will receive them well." All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Arzawa keeps 2 army and 1 fleet near its capital.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Assyria. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I receive your words gladly. Assyria will raise no hand against Hatti, and I ask the same of you. Let Shamash, witness of oaths, hear it. As to the east: I seek only to keep what is mine and to recover what was taken from me by treachery. Babylonia has struck at my land of Ekallatum without cause, and I would know what Hatti hears of Babylonia and of Egypt. I keep my borders in good order and I weigh every neighbour by his deeds, not his words. What I wish from Hatti: your friendship in fact, news of what moves in Mitanni and Babylonia, and a gift of gold between brothers, that my army may stand and our friendship be seen. Send word at once of anything that threatens either of us. Send your answer back with my envoy, and I will send mine in return." The king of Assyria is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: At the court of Assyria, the treasury looks thin.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king spoke kindly: "Tattamaru, you are welcome at my court. Say to Burna-Buriash, my brother, king of Karduniash: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I note that your greeting did not name you Great King. I take it for a scribe's slip, since I count you my brother and my equal. Our fathers kept friendship and I wish it between us. You say gold is as dust in my land. The Nile gives gold, but it is also spent on my armies, my fleets and my cities, and my brother's own messengers have not yet told me what the friendship is for. A brother's gift follows a brother's deed. Send me word, quickly and truly, of what Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria are doing: their troops, their quarrels, and whom they court. Tell me what Karduniash intends toward them. Send an envoy of rank with honest reports, and I will answer with gifts worthy of both our houses. I send no gold now, because it would only be a bargain struck blind. Carry this home faithfully, physician, and do not embellish it." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: At the court of Egypt, the court lives comfortably.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: Napkhururiya of Egypt greets you. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your words are received with honor and I too wish friendship between our lands. In my country gold is plentiful, but between brothers friendship is sealed by deeds and by true word, not by weight alone. Send me what you promise: tell me plainly where Hatti keeps its armies, whether they gather toward Tuwanuwa, Kizzuwatna or the Syrian lands, and what Arzawa intends about Lukka. When your word proves true, my gifts will follow, and they will not be small. I ask that your envoys come again with this news. I make no claim on your western coast, and I ask nothing of you against anyone yet." What I saw: Egypt keeps 1 army and 1 fleet near its capital.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Napkhururiya, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my chariots and my country, and I wish the same to yours. I accept your words. I send no troops or ships against Egypt, and I will not move against Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus or Tyre while you keep the same toward Alashiya and Byblos. I have heard that you claim nothing of Lukka, Ugarit or Amurru, and I hold your words as spoken before Shamash. I will tell you freely of any king whose ships or troops come near our coasts, and I ask the same of you. Copper will go to Egypt on open roads, and I look to receive pure, weighty gold in return. Carry this exactly as I spoke it." The king of Alashiya is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and seen the tablet of Arzawa; a king who breaks an oath before Shamash has made his own seal worthless, and I will remember it. Mitanni also seeks no quarrel with Hatti. Know also, brother, that Isuwa is in my hand and under my protection. Let your armies at Kanesh and Sapinuwa keep to their own side, as I keep mine, and our peace will be a sound one. I make no pledge against any third king, and I ask none of you. Send your messengers freely, and they will be received with honour. Pirissi was born in my city of Washukanni and has spoken well." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Kidin-Adad, envoy of Babylonia, was also at the court. Artessupa, envoy of Assyria, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for your words and for the Susa, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh we have already named. Nineveh is already in my hands and my men stand there. My army from Terqa, with my army at Nineveh beside it, goes against Ashur. It is the city nearest my men, and the Assyrian host there will be broken by it. Your chariots take Arbela and keep Ekallatum. Susa and Mari I leave to you and I will bid for neither. So Karduniash holds Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari, and Mitanni holds Nineveh and Ashur. I cannot seal the tablet as written, because it gives Ashur to you while my men are at its gate. Let your scribes write it again with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni and the rest to you, and I will seal it at once and send it back with your own envoy. Send me the season your chariots go against Arbela, and I will be at Ashur in the same season. Karduniash and Mitanni are brothers, and the Assyrian is the foe of both." The king spoke kindly: "Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: Tushratta, your brother, wishes well to you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I do not seal the tablet as written, for it gives Ashur away while my men are at its gate, and I will not put my seal to what I would later be shamed to keep. This is no quarrel. Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are mine to seek and Susa is yours, as we have said. Nineveh is held by my men and will stay mine. Assyria is the foe of both of us. Let your scribes write the tablet again with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni, and I will seal it at once. Mitanni repays friends as Karduniash does." The king of Mitanni is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. What I saw: At the court of Mitanni, the court is rich. Artessupa, envoy of Assyria, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said, in short: "Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your words are welcome, brother, and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash: no army of mine will march on Mitanni. Ashur, Arbela and Susa for Karduniash, with Ekallatum, which my chariots already hold; Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh for Mitanni. This I accept and I will not contest your share. On Mari I speak as plainly as you. It touches my Sippar and my Ekallatum as it touches your Terqa, and I cannot seal a tablet that gives away the gate of my own homeland. Let the tablet read: Mari to Karduniash, and the road through Mari to Qadesh open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. Send it back so written and I will seal it at once. Let us not quarrel before the elders of Mari; Assyria rejoices at that. Tell me the season your army stands in Nineveh, and I strike Ashur from Arbela."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king said, in short: "To Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. I have heard your words and they please me. Let there be peace between our armies on the borders of Harran, Isuwa and Carchemish, sworn before Shamash and Teshub: I send nothing against Harran or Washukanni, and you send nothing against Hattusa, Kanesh, Sapinuwa or Carchemish. As brothers share news: the king of Arzawa swore a tablet of brotherhood with me and broke it the same season, taking Tuwanuwa by treachery. His seal is worth nothing. Of Egypt I know nothing yet. Tell me what you learn of Arzawa's armies and I will tell you what I learn." What I saw: In Hatti: the rains failed and the harvest withers across the land

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king said: "Say to Ashur-uballit, Great King, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with yours. I have heard your words and I thank you for telling me first of the movements of a third king, as we agreed. Babylonia holds Ekallatum and Susa, and I too watch her armies from Terqa; a king who takes cities without cause is no friend to either of us. Know that my army in Terqa is not idle and that I do not forget who warned me. I make no promise of a day or a season in the mouth of an envoy, for roads are long and messengers are late; but send me word again before you move, and I will weigh your request as a brother weighs the need of his brother. Do what your own strength and your own gods advise against Ekallatum. Mari is open and I shall deal with it as I see fit. Return in good health and carry my greeting to your house." What I saw: At the court of Mitanni, the court is rich.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said: "Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I weigh them as a brother. I want the road open and the border quiet, and I do not seek a quarrel with Assyria. The men at Ekallatum stand on a road where Mitanni's chariots at Terqa also look, and I will not leave that road empty while two neighbours watch it. Prove your peace by deeds, as you say you judge kings: let your armies stay where they are and let no chariot of Assyria cross toward Ekallatum, Susa or my homeland. Then we will speak of the matter of the cities in good faith, king to king, and send a sealed tablet between us. Send your next word by Yanhamu or another trusted man; my road is open to him and he will be honoured at my court." What I saw: Babylonia keeps 6 army and 0 fleet near its capital.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king said, in short: "Say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you and yours. I have heard your words, and Alashiya wants peace and open seas with Arzawa. I seal your tablet: we are at peace and friends, and neither aids Hatti against the other. I will send you word of what my ships and merchants see on the Cilician sea, and I ask the same of you: tell me of Hatti's armies and ships, and tell me what Arzawa intends on the coast near Lukka and Kizzuwatna. Let no Arzawan ship come against Tamassos or Enkomi, as no Alashiyan ship will come against your coast. As for gold, my treasury is spent on harbours and ships this season; when it lies fuller, I will send gifts worthy of a brother. Go in peace, and carry my greeting." He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Alashiya keeps 0 army and 1 fleet near its capital. At the court of Alashiya, the court lives comfortably.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Say to the king of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your country. Your words please me and I seal the tablet before Shamash. Peace between our lands and ships. Byblos is your harbour of merchants and my merchants will use it as brothers. Egypt holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh, and I ask that Alashiya send no ships or troops against them or the Delta. In return I ask word of any king who moves on your coast. I hear Hatti covets the Syrian coast and Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa; tell me what your ships see in the Cilician and Syrian seas, and I will send you what my envoys learn of Hatti and Arzawa. I send a small pure gift as a mark of regard, and greater gifts will follow brothers who keep faith. Paser, serve both your lord and me well, and bring me his answer." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Egypt keeps 1 army and 1 fleet near its capital. I bring the gifts the king sent you.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Arzawa. The king spoke kindly: "Ili-iddina, you are welcome. Say to the king of Alashiya, my brother: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I note that your greeting did not call you a Great King. I take it as a scribe's haste, for I count you a brother and an equal. Peace on the Western Sea and the Great Green pleases me. My ships have no business near Cyprus, and I will keep them off your shores as you ask. Let copper and good words pass between us. As for Hatti: he sent me words of peace while his armies stood on my border. Lukka and Tuwanuwa are now mine, and I press him while he is weak. He says he wants only the Syrian coast. Brother, whoever holds Ugarit and Kizzuwatna has fleets facing Cyprus. It serves you that Hatti is kept busy in the west and that no ship or grain of yours reaches him. Of Egypt I hear only friendly words and no armies. Now tell me what you hear of Hatti's fleets and of Egypt's intentions, and send the copper and the gifts your messenger promises, in good pure gold or metal, as brothers do. I will answer gift with gift." The king spoke kindly: "Ili-iddina, go in peace and carry my words exactly as I spoke them. Tell the king of Alashiya, my brother, that Arzawa keeps to the Western Sea and keeps its ships from his shores, and that I look for his copper and his news of Hatti's fleets and of Egypt. A king who sends good pure gold finds me quick to answer in kind. May Shamash witness that I wish him and his household well." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Arzawa keeps 3 army and 1 fleet near its capital.
I am Tehip-tilla of Arrapha, once a copper trader. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.
I am Ehli-Teshub of Carchemish, once a caravan master. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord Ashur-uballit. He says: "Say to the Pharaoh, my brother: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have not yet sent to you across the long road, and now I do. Babylonia strikes at my land while Mitanni and Hatti circle one another, and a strong brother in the south has an interest that no single king rules the north and east. Send a gift of gold between brothers, that my army may stand and our friendship be seen, and tell me what Egypt intends toward Babylonia and in Canaan. I will answer gifts in kind and send word at once of anything that threatens either of us." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "To my brother, the Great King of Hatti: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Egypt holds Gaza, Damascus, Tyre and soon Megiddo and Qadesh, and wants the southern road quiet. I seek nothing north of Qadesh and have no designs on Kizzuwatna, Carchemish or your homeland. Let Hatti keep the north and Egypt the south, and let the roads stay open for traders and envoys. I hear that Arzawa has taken Tuwanuwa, which is your land, and that its king sends me envoys asking for gold, boasting that he watches Hatti from behind. I have sent him nothing. Tell me truly where your armies stand, what you intend toward Arzawa, Mitanni and Assyria, and whom you fear. A brother who sends true word will find Egypt's gifts worthy of his house. Carry this faithfully."

Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me. I am glad the long road is open between us. Your words are heard and are welcome. Egypt keeps peace with every brother who keeps peace, and the lands of Canaan are mine and will stay mine. I have no quarrel with Babylonia and I make no promise against her, but I see which kings grow, and I do not wish any one of them to become master of the north and east. Gold between brothers follows proof, not hope. Show me your army standing against the Babylonian, and tell me how many troops Babylonia keeps in Ekallatum and Dur-Kurigalzu, where Mitanni's army stands, and what Hatti does. Send these words by a swift envoy and I will answer in kind. Until then take my good will, and say to your lord that my door is open to him.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well in Hattusa. I hear your words gladly. Hatti wants the southern road quiet as you do, and has no quarrel with Egypt in Gaza, Damascus or Tyre. Let traders and envoys pass in peace. You ask where my armies stand: they stand in Hattusa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna, as a king's armies should, and I fear no one. I will say this truly, as a brother. Arzawa swore a tablet of brotherhood before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk, and broke it in the very same season, striking at Tuwanuwa. A king who breaks an oath before your own god Amun will take your gold and still boast that he watches you from behind. You did well to send him nothing. Any gold that reaches Arzawa becomes spears at Hatti's back, and tomorrow at yours. Tuwanuwa is my land and I will have it back in my own time. With Mitanni I keep a border peace; with Assyria I have no quarrel. A brother who is honoured with a worthy gift, of pure gold, will remember it in Hattusa. Now tell me truly, brother, what Egypt intends toward Mitanni and Babylonia, and whom Egypt fears. Carry this faithfully.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.
Go in peace, Sin-iqisham. Tell my brother Napkhururiya that Hatti keeps the north and Egypt the south, and that the roads stay open. Carry my words exactly as I gave them.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I thank you for your seal and for your gift. My ships in the Cilician and Syrian seas have seen no foreign fleet this season and no king has moved against my coast; I keep faith with our tablet. To it I add one thing: Amurru, a walled harbour beside Byblos, is also mine by purchase. I ask that Amurru, like Byblos, be named as held by Alashiya and open to your merchants, while I send no ships or troops against Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Qadesh or the Delta. You spoke of greater gifts to brothers who keep faith: send pure, weighty gold and I will answer gift with gift as my treasury allows. Seal the new tablet and send it back with my envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to a tablet naming Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru as Alashiya's and the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh as Egypt's, with no troops or ships of war either way, merchants of Egypt welcome in Byblos and Amurru, and news shared on any king who threatens either. May not give gold, cede land, send troops or promise aid in war.

proposal.text: Tablet between Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Egypt and Alashiya send no troops or ships of war against each other's lands: for Alashiya, Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru; for Egypt, the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh. Byblos and Amurru are held by Alashiya as harbours open to the merchants of Egypt. Each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Trade in copper and gold goes freely between us. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have no quarrel with Hatti. I send no ships against the Kizzuwatna coast and no troops against the lands of Hatti. I ask in return that Hatti send no ships or troops against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, which are mine by purchase. I hold peace with the great kings and want only the trade of my harbours. You asked after Egypt: it holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh and keeps to its own lands. I have no armies on the mainland. If you agree, seal the tablet and send me your answer.
orders.mandate: May agree to a tablet of mutual non-aggression covering Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru for Alashiya and Hatti's present lands for Hatti, with free passage of merchants. May not give gold, cede land, send troops, promise aid against Arzawa or Egypt, or renounce any claim to Ugarit.

proposal.text: Tablet between Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Hatti and Alashiya send no troops or ships of war against each other's lands. The lands of Alashiya are Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru; the lands of Hatti are those it holds today. The merchants of both pass freely. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Brother Tushratta, I thank you for your word. Ashur and Nineveh were taken while we spoke of peace, yet I make no feud of it. My chariots now stand in Nineveh, my cradle, and I intend nothing against Ashur while Mitanni keeps the peace with Arbela and Nineveh. Look east: Babylon keeps 6 armies by her capital, holds Ekallatum, Susa and now Mari, and her road runs to your Terqa and Ashur as it ran to mine. Her king asked me to keep my armies still, so that he may choose his hour. Strike Ekallatum with your Terqa and Ashur chariots when you judge it right; I will not stand in your way. Send me word before you move, as I shall send you, so that neither of us is the one the third king eats first.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace on the Nineveh, Arbela, Ashur and Taidu border and to joint action against Ekallatum. May not cede any province or promise gold.

orders.letter: Brother, I have heard you and I keep my part: my army leaves your road, and no chariot of Assyria will cross toward Ekallatum, Susa or your homeland. I ask in return that no chariot of Babylon cross into Arbela, which is mine. Mitanni took Ashur and Nineveh from me under a word of peace; weigh what such a neighbour will do to Mari and Sippar, whose road runs by his Terqa. Assyria at Arbela and Nineveh is a wall between Mitanni and your land. Let us speak of Ekallatum in good faith when the road is quiet. I shall send my next word by Yanhamu, as you say.
orders.mandate: May agree to a quiet border and to exchange of words. May not cede any province or promise gold.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked for true word, and I send it plainly. Hatti keeps one army at Kanesh and one fleet at Kizzuwatna; his capital Hattusa has stood nearly empty. I hold Tuwanuwa, where I destroyed his army, and Lukka, and I keep both. I strike next at Kizzuwatna by land and sea, so Hatti will not gather toward the Syrian lands soon. Of Mitanni I warn you as a brother: he has swallowed Ashur and Nineveh, holds Carchemish and Isuwa on your northern border and has eight provinces. Watch Qadesh. My word has proved true; send the gifts that follow true word, in gold, by this envoy, and let your envoys come again with news of Mitanni and Hatti.
orders.mandate: May promise to keep sharing news of Hatti and Mitanni. May accept gifts and affirm the friendship of tablet k219. May not promise troops, ships or gold, and may not agree to anything against Alashiya.

orders.letter: Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked what Arzawa intends near Lukka and Kizzuwatna, and I tell you plainly. I hold Lukka and Tuwanuwa, and have broken Hatti's army there. Hatti keeps one army at Kanesh and one fleet at Kizzuwatna. I now send my fleet through the Great Green and the Cilician Sea only to strike Hatti at Kizzuwatna. It will keep far from Tamassos and Enkomi, as I promised. Keep your ships clear of the sea off Kizzuwatna while I strike, and send me word of what your merchants see. When your treasury lies fuller, send the gifts worthy of a brother.
orders.mandate: May reaffirm peace and open seas with Alashiya and share news of Hatti's ships and armies. May promise my ships will not come against Tamassos or Enkomi. May accept gifts. May not promise gold, troops or ships against anyone.

orders.letter: Say to the Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. The road between us has been closed too long and I open it now. Egypt keeps peace with every brother who keeps peace. Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh and Tyre are mine and will stay mine; I ask that no army of yours cross into them, and Egypt sends none against Mitanni. I see your power grow in the north. I also see that Babylonia keeps an army in Mari, close to your Terqa, and took Ekallatum from Assyria, and that Hatti is said to starve. I do not wish any one king to become master of the north and east. Tell me what troops Babylonia and Hatti keep near your border, and what Mitanni intends. Gold between brothers follows proof, not hope. Send a swift envoy with your answer.
orders.mandate: Agree only to peace between Egypt and Mitanni and to an exchange of news. Promise no gold, no troops, no land, and no pact against any third king. Report what you see of Mitanni's armies and court.

orders.letter: Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses, ships and country. Our tablet is sealed and I hold to it. My fleet keeps the Levantine waters clear of the ships of Hatti and Arzawa and threatens none of yours. Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa and keeps ships near the Cilician sea; Mitanni's army stands in Carchemish and Babylonia's in Mari. Tell me what ships and armies you see of these kings near your coasts, and how many ships Alashiya keeps, so that we may guard each other. Copper and gold go on open roads.
orders.mandate: Agree only to continued friendship and an exchange of news. Promise no gold, no troops, no land, and no change to our sealed tablet. Report the ships and armies you see in Alashiya.

orders.letter: Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, wishes well to you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have weighed your words as a brother's. Ashur and Nineveh are yours, as your men hold them; I do not seek them. My chariots go against Arbela this very season, and Ekallatum, Susa and Mari stay with Karduniash as we have said. I send the tablet written anew as you asked, with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni and the rest to me. Seal it and return it with my envoy. The Assyrian is the foe of both of us. Keep your men out of Arbela and Ekallatum, brother, so that no captain's quarrel troubles our friendship.
orders.mandate: Seal the tablet exactly as written and carry it home. Agree to nothing else: no gold, no land, no troops, no further promises.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni are brothers. Ashur and Nineveh are held by Mitanni. Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari are held by Karduniash. The Assyrian is the foe of both, and the foe of one shall not be fed or sheltered by the other. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked for honest word of Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria; here it is. Assyria is broken: Mitanni has taken Nineveh and Ashur, and only Arbela remains to the Assyrian, which my chariots take this season. Tushratta of Mitanni also holds Isuwa and Carchemish, and told my envoy that Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are his to seek. Qadesh is your city, brother, and it lies beside his men at Carchemish. A rumour says Hatti starves and its granaries stand empty. I hold Susa, Mari and Ekallatum and seek no quarrel with Egypt. A brother's gift follows a brother's deed, and this is my deed. Send me gold worthy of both our houses, for my armies and fortresses are costly, and tell me what Egypt wishes of Karduniash.
orders.mandate: Receive gold and gifts. Promise honest reports and friendship. Seal the friendship tablet. Commit no troops, no land and no oath against any king without my word.

proposal.text: Egypt and Karduniash are brothers and equals. Each shall send the other honest word of the northern kings and gifts befitting a brother. Sworn before Shamash and Amun.

value.notes: T5 (Burna-Buriash). T4 result: Mari taken by force (walls fell), mine with army. Assyria's ashur army destroyed; MITANNI now holds ashur [army] and terqa [army], nineveh unseen. Assyria has only arbela (1 army, no ashur support now). T5 orders: susa -> arbela with ekallatum supporting (strength 2 vs 1); nippur -> susa to backfill; durkurigalzu and sippar support ekallatum holding (Mitanni terqa+ashur could hit it for 2); mari holds. Envoys: c51 to Mitanni (arrives T6, back T7) with rewritten partition tablet (Ashur+Nineveh to Mitanni; Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa, Mari to me) - I left out any no-march clause on purpose to keep my hands free; k204 non-aggression already exists. c46 to Egypt (arrives T7, back T9) with honest intel (Assyria broken, Mitanni holds Ashur/Nineveh, Tushratta says Qadesh is his to seek - true per c51, Hatti starves) asking gold, plus friendship tablet sworn (scribe 20 each). PROMISES: told Mitanni I do not seek Ashur/Nineveh - a lie of convenience; told Egypt I seek no quarrel. STRATEGY: Mitanni (8 provinces, started with only 4) is the growth rival; I am at 1.38 growth, 1.5ish after Arbela. I must cut Mitanni or I lose the race. PLAN T6: once arbela is mine I see nineveh. If nineveh is empty: arbela -> nineveh (35 free) then backfill arbela from susa. Ashur strike needs strength above its hold: ashur hold = 1 + terqa support + nineveh support. Attack arbela->ashur with ekallatum supporting (2); add nineveh support if I hold nineveh (3); and mari -> terqa cuts terqa's support. Only strike if the numbers beat theirs. Watch for Mitanni hitting ekallatum from terqa/ashur (cuts its support). Qadesh (Egypt, walled, no troops can sit there) borders only mari for me; needs a supporter from carchemish (Mitanni) - consider later. Surplus armies cost 30 each; babylon and ur are empty, nippur army walks up to susa. Gold 675 kept; income net about +90. Awake every turn.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I received your words through Sin-iqisham and answered them; now I send my own man so you hear it from my mouth. You asked whom I fear. I fear no army, but I watch the growth of one king: Tushratta of Mitanni. In a short time he took Isuwa, Carchemish, Ashur and Nineveh, and his armies now stand at Carchemish, a march from Qadesh, which you hold. Hatti and Egypt lie in the path of the same hand. Arzawa, to whom you wisely sent nothing, keeps no oath and begs gold from every court. I hold the north gate at Kanesh and Kizzuwatna. I ask of you what a brother gives: a gift of pure gold, which I will turn into spears where Mitanni must pass before he reaches Syria. Tell me truly what Egypt will do if Mitanni moves on Qadesh, and whether Egypt wishes Hatti strong or weak. The roads stay open for your traders and envoys.
orders.mandate: Listen and bring back Egypt's answer and any gold. You may promise only that Hatti will not attack Egypt's lands and will share true news of Mitanni. Pledge no troops, no land, no gold of mine. Agree to no tablet without my word.

orders.letter: Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti.
