May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your envoy Ili-iddina promised gifts of friendship, and I have kept my side: no Hatti ship or garrison stands on your coasts. Hear what moves in the north. Arzawa swore a brotherhood tablet before Shamash and Amun and broke it the same season, seizing Tuwanuwa. Mitanni has taken Isuwa and Carchemish this year and now sits beside Ugarit, Amurru and Byblos. Hatti holds Kizzuwatna and stands between these two kings and the Cilician Sea. A king who helps Hatti stand helps his own ports. I ask a gift of pure gold, whatever your house thinks worthy of a brother, to raise spears at my border. Tell me also, truly, what you intend toward Arzawa, Mitanni and Egypt. The harbour of Kizzuwatna stays open to your copper ships. Send your answer with my envoy.
orders.mandate: Listen, bring back Alashiya's gold and answer. You may promise friendship and that Kizzuwatna's harbour stays open to Alashiyan trade and that Hatti will put no ship or garrison on Alashiya's coasts. Pledge no troops, land or gold of mine. Agree to no tablet without my word.

value.notes: T5: Treasury 10. T6 is the last drought season: income about 76 vs upkeep 95 + wages 19, so I cannot pay all 3 units at T6 (86 available vs 95 upkeep). Expect ONE unit to desert at T6 start (probably the fleet or the sapinuwa army). Read the T6 report, see which is gone, and re-garrison at once (hattusa 50 is the priority; it can only be hit from tuwanuwa at strength 1, so one army there is safe). From T7 income is about 150: with 2 units net about +70 a season; raise an army at ~T8 (100). Do NOT buy tablets (20) or send gold until then. Orders T5: sapinuwa -> hattusa (bounces if Arzawa also moves in, which is fine), kanesh supports kizzuwatna hold, fleet holds. Mitanni BROKE the spirit of k297: sealed it at T4 and took Carchemish the same season (like Arzawa with k189). Both neighbours are oath-breakers; do not trust tablets, trust only strength. Mitanni is the runaway leader (holds ashur, nineveh, isuwa, carchemish, about 290 yield vs start 145); the others should fear his growth. Sent Keliya (c32) to Egypt (2 seasons, arrives T7, back T9) asking for pure gold and sounding out Egypt on Mitanni and Qadesh. Sent Pirissi (c39) to Alashiya (1 season, back T7) to collect the promised gifts and warn of Arzawa and Mitanni. Both born in Washukanni: watch for leaks. Wages 19 a season until T10; reconsider dismissing them at T7 if no gold comes. Later: Babylonia and Assyria envoys against Mitanni (Assyria asked for news of Mitanni and Babylonia and a gift; I owe Assyria a reply, Assyria is almost dead, low priority). Retake plan: when I have an army at hattusa and one at kanesh, attack tuwanuwa with kanesh and hattusa supporting, and the fleet kizzuwatna -> lukka to cut lukka's support (only if mira does not also support). Promises made: no binding ones. k189 (Arzawa) is void; k297 (Mitanni) I honour only while it suits me.

orders.letter: Brother, your words please me and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash. Mari is yours; I will not bid for it. Seal the tablet I send: Mari to Karduniash, the road through Mari to Qadesh open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. Ashur and Nineveh are held by my armies now. Assyria has one army left, in Arbela, and I move on it. One favour between brothers: Qadesh, which you have conceded to Mitanni, is held only by Egypt's walls, and walls fall only to two strengths. My army in Carchemish strikes it. In the very season this reaches you, order your army in Mari to support my army from Carchemish into Qadesh; I move in that same season. Egypt grows fat on ten provinces, and a brother who weakens it helps you as much as me. Ekallatum and Susa stay with Karduniash. If Egypt or Hatti strikes Mari, my army in Terqa will stand with yours.
orders.mandate: May agree to the tablet exactly as written and to the joint strike on Qadesh. May not give gold, may not cede any province, may not promise to leave Arbela or to march on Hatti.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni are brothers and keep the oath of turn 2: neither shall march an army against the lands of the other. Mari, Ekallatum and Susa to Karduniash. Ashur, Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh to Mitanni. The road through Mari to Qadesh is open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Brother Suppiluliuma, I grieve for your harvest and wish your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses health. I sealed our tablet in good faith. But my army had marched on Carchemish before the tablet reached my generals and could not be recalled; the city stood open with its walls broken and Egypt would have taken it. I hold it as a gate for caravans, not as a spear against you. I send nothing against Hattusa, Kanesh or Sapinuwa. Let peace stand on the borders of Harran, Isuwa and Carchemish, and the road through Carchemish to Ugarit is open to your caravans. You warned me that Arzawa's seal is worth nothing; I believe it. Of Arzawa's armies I know nothing yet, and of Egypt I see no army north of Gaza. What I learn I will tell you.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace on the borders of Harran, Isuwa and Carchemish and to open roads for caravans. May not give gold, may not cede any province, may not reveal my plans against Assyria or Qadesh.

value.notes: T5 (Tushratta). FACTS: Ashur and Carchemish taken T4 (mine). Mari FELL TO BABYLONIA (their sippar army moved in, ekallatum supported) - Mari is Babylonia's, with an army. Assyria has ONLY arbela (one army). Nineveh is mine but empty; taidu->nineveh bounced with Assyria's arbela->nineveh. Babylonia (Ubaru report) accepts my share: Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh to Mitanni; Ashur/Arbela/Susa/Ekallatum/Mari claimed by them; they would seal 'Mari to Karduniash + road through Mari open to Mitanni toll-free'. Hatti (Zitanza): wants peace at Harran/Isuwa/Carchemish; says Arzawa broke an oath and took Tuwanuwa; Hatti has harvest failure. I BROKE k275's Carchemish clause - Hatti will be angry. T5 ORDERS: taidu->nineveh (contest vs Assyria); ashur supports terqa hold (Babylonia's ekallatum+mari could hit terqa 2v1); carchemish and isuwa support each other's hold (Hatti kanesh+sapinuwa could hit isuwa 2v1); terqa holds. BUY UGARIT 400 (only free city left; strength-neutral, +40 income, denies Alashiya/Hatti); raise army washukanni 100 (appears T6); tablet scribe 20 to Babylonia. Treasury after about 5; next season net about +124 (+40 Ugarit). ENVOYS: Ubaru c57 -> Babylonia (arrives T6) with tablet: Mari/Ekallatum/Susa to Karduniash; Ashur/Nineveh/Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh to Mitanni; road via Mari free; asked their Mari army to support carchemish->qadesh in the season he arrives (T6) - Arbela NOT promised to them. Zitanza c62 -> Hatti (apology: army had marched before tablet sealed; peace on Harran/Isuwa/Carchemish; no gold). T6 PLAN: ashur -> arbela supported by nineveh army (Assyria elimination, +30); carchemish -> qadesh if Babylonia's mari supports (but then isuwa/carchemish defence vs Hatti is thinner - check Hatti moves first); new washukanni army -> harran/terqa as reserve. Later: walled cities need 2 strength; Egypt's damascus/tyre, Alashiya's byblos/amurru are targets via qadesh. Hatti kanesh/sapinuwa each can be supported by the other, so need 3 armies to take either. No envoys yet to Egypt or Arzawa (only two envoys; Ehli-Teshub c125 refused 20). Ideas: seek_candidates next turn when gold allows; ally with Arzawa vs Hatti. SUSPICIONS: Babylonia may betray at Terqa (they hold ekallatum+mari adjacent); Ubaru is Sippar-born and may colour his reports; Zitanza Lukka-born (Lukka now Arzawa's); Kidin-Adad took my 10. Competitors for growth: Alashiya and Arzawa (small starts), Egypt (310 yield), Babylonia (290).

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Say to Napkhururiya, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I thank you for your seal and for your gift. My ships in the Cilician and Syrian seas have seen no foreign fleet this season and no king has moved against my coast; I keep faith with our tablet. To it I add one thing: Amurru, a walled harbour beside Byblos, is also mine by purchase. I ask that Amurru, like Byblos, be named as held by Alashiya and open to your merchants, while I send no ships or troops against Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus, Qadesh or the Delta. You spoke of greater gifts to brothers who keep faith: send pure, weighty gold and I will answer gift with gift as my treasury allows. Seal the new tablet and send it back with my envoy." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of Tushratta, and I am, as ever, your servant. He says: "Brother Suppiluliuma, I grieve for your harvest and wish your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses health. I sealed our tablet in good faith. I hold it as a gate for caravans, not as a spear against you. I send nothing against Hattusa, Kanesh or Sapinuwa. Let peace stand on the borders of Harran, Isuwa and Carchemish, and the road through Carchemish to Ugarit is open to your caravans. Of Arzawa's armies I know nothing yet, and of Egypt I see no army north of Gaza. What I learn I will tell you." For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "Brother, your words please me and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash. Mari is yours; I will not bid for it. Seal the tablet I send: Mari to Karduniash, the road through Mari to Qadesh open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. Ashur and Nineveh are held by my armies now. Assyria has one army left, in Arbela, and I move on it. One favour between brothers: Qadesh, which you have conceded to Mitanni, is held only by Egypt's walls, and walls fall only to two strengths. My army in Carchemish strikes it. In the very season this reaches you, order your army in Mari to support my army from Carchemish into Qadesh; I move in that same season. Egypt grows fat on ten provinces, and a brother who weakens it helps you as much as me. Ekallatum and Susa stay with Karduniash."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Burna-Buriash. He says: "Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, wishes well to you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have weighed your words as a brother's. Ashur and Nineveh are yours, as your men hold them; I do not seek them. My chariots go against Arbela this very season, and Ekallatum, Susa and Mari stay with Karduniash as we have said. I send the tablet written anew as you asked, with Ashur and Nineveh to Mitanni and the rest to me. Seal it and return it with my envoy. The Assyrian is the foe of both of us. Keep your men out of Arbela and Ekallatum, brother, so that no captain's quarrel troubles our friendship."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses, ships and country. Our tablet is sealed and I hold to it. My fleet keeps the Levantine waters clear of the ships of Hatti and Arzawa and threatens none of yours. Arzawa now holds Lukka and Tuwanuwa and keeps ships near the Cilician sea; Mitanni's army stands in Carchemish and Babylonia's in Mari. Tell me what ships and armies you see of these kings near your coasts, and how many ships Alashiya keeps, so that we may guard each other. Copper and gold go on open roads."

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our tablet is sealed and I hold to it; my ships and men raise no hand against Egypt or its lands, and Byblos and Amurru stay open harbours to your merchants. Near my coasts I see no foreign fleet and no foreign army; the Cilician and Syrian waters are quiet. What I hear of Arzawa at Lukka and of Mitanni and Babylonia in the north I hear only from rumour, as you do. How many ships I keep is a king's own business, brother. Know that they are enough to guard my harbours and I will send word if any aggressor shows a sail. Do likewise: tell me at once if the ships of Hatti or any other king move toward Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru. Copper goes to Egypt on open roads, and I look for gifts of pure, full-weight gold in return, as between brothers.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your envoy Ili-iddina promised gifts of friendship, and I have kept my side: no Hatti ship or garrison stands on your coasts. Hear what moves in the north. Arzawa swore a brotherhood tablet before Shamash and Amun and broke it the same season, seizing Tuwanuwa. Mitanni has taken Isuwa and Carchemish this year and now sits beside Ugarit, Amurru and Byblos. Hatti holds Kizzuwatna and stands between these two kings and the Cilician Sea. A king who helps Hatti stand helps his own ports. I ask a gift of pure gold, whatever your house thinks worthy of a brother, to raise spears at my border. Tell me also, truly, what you intend toward Arzawa, Mitanni and Egypt. The harbour of Kizzuwatna stays open to your copper ships." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Say to Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King, king of Hatti, your brother. All goes well with me, and may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for your words about my harvest; the gods send drought and the gods lift it, and my granaries are filling. I have heard your words and I keep peace on my side of the border: I send nothing against Harran, Washukanni or your homeland, and none of my chariots goes toward Isuwa while your word stands. Brother, you know now what the seal of Arzawa is worth; he swore to me before Teshub and broke the oath in the same season. Let us both watch him, and let each tell the other what he learns of his armies and of Egypt. I will tell you what I see. Shamash is witness to what is said between us. Send me your envoy again when you have news.
value.bribeAsk: Tell me truly what Tushratta plans against Assyria, Qadesh and Egypt, and where his armies stand near Isuwa and Carchemish.

value.speech: I will carry your words to my lord.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have no quarrel with Hatti. I send no ships against the Kizzuwatna coast and no troops against the lands of Hatti. I ask in return that Hatti send no ships or troops against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, which are mine by purchase. I hold peace with the great kings and want only the trade of my harbours. You asked after Egypt: it holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh and keeps to its own lands. I have no armies on the mainland." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. It goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your copper. Your words are received with joy, and Paser is welcome at my court as a son of Memphis. I seal your tablet. Egypt sends no army and no ship of war against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, and your harbours stay open to my merchants as mine are open to yours. I ask the same for the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh. If any king threatens your coast or mine, I will tell you, and I ask you to tell me. My gold is for brothers who keep faith, and a gift that answers your copper will follow once the merchants have begun to move between our harbours. Tell me through Paser, so my merchants may sail with confidence, how many ships and how many men you keep at Byblos, at Amurru and on Cyprus, and whether any foreign fleet has been seen in the Syrian or Cilician seas.
value.bribeAsk: Tell me truly how many ships and troops Alashiya keeps at Byblos, Amurru and on Cyprus, what foreign fleets you have seen, and speak well of Egypt to your lord.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Kidin-Adad, I have heard the words of Burna-Buriash, my brother, as a brother's. Say to him: Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, wishes well to him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. I seal the tablet. Ashur and Nineveh remain with Mitanni, and my chariots will not march on Ekallatum, Susa or Mari. The Assyrian is the foe of us both and I will neither feed nor shelter him. Let no captain's quarrel trouble our border at Terqa: keep your chariots from my homeland as mine keep from yours. I will place my own men where they are needed to guard what is mine. Now, as one who has eaten at my table, tell me plainly how many chariots stand at Ekallatum and at Mari, and whether the Assyrian still held Arbela when you left. Take this small gift for the road.
value.bribeAsk: Tell me truly how many armies Babylonia keeps at Ekallatum, Mari and Sippar, and whether Arbela still held an Assyrian army when you left.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Say to Tushratta, Great King, my brother: Burna-Buriash your brother wishes well to you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your words please me, and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash. The road through Mari is open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. This I grant gladly, and Ubaru, a son of Sippar, will see it kept. Assyria is finished, brother: Arbela has fallen to my armies, with Ekallatum, Susa and Mari. Let no army of Mitanni stand at Arbela's gates; those lands are Karduniash's, as the tablet my own envoy carries to you names them. As for Qadesh: I cannot draw the army out of Mari. The city is not yet quiet under a new lord, and that army must stand among its people. Also my envoys are on the road to Pharaoh asking for gold, and if Egypt's city falls to my support in the very season they stand before him, their heads and my gold are lost. Let them return, and I will speak again. For the same reason I do not seal a tablet that names the city of a third king. Seal the tablet my envoy carries, which names the lands of both of us. May Shamash and Marduk keep Tushratta and his house.
value.bribeAsk: Speak well of Karduniash to your lord and carry my words as I said them. When you speak again, tell me truthfully how many armies Tushratta keeps at Ashur, Terqa, Nineveh and Carchemish.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, has sealed the tablet and sends it home with Paser. Let it stand before Shamash. Egypt keeps faith with brothers who keep faith. Your harbours are open to my merchants, and mine to yours. When your copper moves, my gold will answer. Tell me what fleets and men you keep, and whether any foreign ship has been seen in the Syrian or Cilician seas, and I will tell you what I see. May it go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your copper.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Kidin-Adad, I have sealed the tablet of my brother Burna-Buriash. Ashur and Nineveh are Mitanni's, as my men hold them, and the Assyrian is the foe of us both. Tell him that Mitanni keeps faith with those who keep faith with it. Let the border at Terqa stay quiet, and let each king guard what is his own. Say also that the road through Mari should stand open to my merchants and envoys, as he has already offered. Go in peace, and take my greeting to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots and his horses.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank my brother for the words he sent and for keeping his ships and garrisons from my coasts. I keep the same toward him: no ship or spear of Alashiya will come against Hatti or the harbour of Kizzuwatna, and my copper ships will keep sailing there. My house is a house of copper and of ships, not of spears. I intend peace with all my brothers, with Arzawa, with Mitanni and with Egypt alike, and I take no side in the wars of the north. My treasury is spent on my new harbours and I cannot send gold now; if my brother's tablet of peace for Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru comes sealed by his hand, I will answer it in kind. When Nergal and the harvest allow, I will remember a brother's gift. Go safely, Pirissi.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tarhundaradu. He says: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked what Arzawa intends near Lukka and Kizzuwatna, and I tell you plainly. I hold Lukka and Tuwanuwa, and have broken Hatti's army there. Hatti keeps one army at Kanesh and one fleet at Kizzuwatna. I now send my fleet through the Great Green and the Cilician Sea only to strike Hatti at Kizzuwatna. It will keep far from Tamassos and Enkomi, as I promised. Keep your ships clear of the sea off Kizzuwatna while I strike, and send me word of what your merchants see."

Say to Tushratta, Great King, my brother: Burna-Buriash your brother holds the oath of Shamash and will not march against the lands of Mitanni; the tablet already sealed between us stands. The new tablet I do not seal this season. It gives away the cities of a third king, and it names Arbela in no line, though Arbela is held by my armies and is Karduniash's. I seal no tablet that leaves a brother's border unwritten. When my envoy comes home from Pharaoh, send a tablet naming only the lands of the two of us: Mari, Ekallatum, Susa and Arbela to Karduniash; the lands you hold to Mitanni. That I will seal gladly. The road through Mari stays open to your caravans and envoys, free of toll. May Shamash and Marduk keep Tushratta and his house.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your words are welcome. Hatti sends no ships or troops against Cyprus, and I will keep my fleet from your harbours at Tamassos and Enkomi while your ships stay out of the Kizzuwatna coast and the sea at Lukka. I have sealed your tablet. Hear this, brother: Arzawa broke his oath to me in the very season he swore it, and Mitanni did the same with Carchemish. Kings who break oaths in one season will break them to you in the next, so watch your coasts and keep your fleets at home. I have sent my own envoy to your court with my greetings; let your gifts return with him, pure gold and copper, as is fitting between brothers, for my country has had a hard season. Tell me before you go: what ships does Arzawa keep in the Western Sea and at Lukka, and does any Alashiyan fleet sail the Cilician Sea? And what does Egypt say of Mitanni?
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I thank you for speaking plainly, as brothers should. Our tablet stands: we are at peace and friends, and neither of us aids Hatti against the other. My ships have no business off Kizzuwatna and will not go there; my fleet lies at Enkomi and my merchants trade in peace. I ask only that your ships keep clear of Tamassos and Enkomi, as you promised, and of my harbours at Byblos and Amurru on the Syrian coast. As for my merchants: they have seen no war fleets in the Cilician Sea beyond the ones you name, and I will send word if that changes. The treasury of Alashiya is spent on its own affairs this season, so I send no gold now, but my goodwill is true. Send your envoy again when your fleet has done its work.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have sealed the tablet you sent, and Shamash is witness: no ships or troops of Hatti against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, so long as none of yours come against Kizzuwatna, Lukka's sea or the lands I hold. Tell your master that my envoy awaits at your court, and that gifts of pure gold and copper sent back with him will be remembered as the mark of a true brother. My country has had a hard season, and I will not forget who stood by me. Keep your fleets at home and tell me what you see in the Western Sea.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

value.notes: T6: Treasury 65, net -20/season (4 armies + 1 fleet = 155 upkeep, wages 20 until T10), so treasury about 45 at T7, 25 at T8, 5 at T9, then flat at T10. MUST take Kizzuwatna (+35 yield, +350 strength) at T7 or cut an army. T5 result: tuwanuwa->hattusa failed again (hattusa shows empty, so a hidden Hatti unit bounces me), mira->tuwanuwa bounced because tuwanuwa never left, fleet reached greatgreen. T6 ORDERS: tuwanuwa->hattusa (free option), mira->tuwanuwa with lukka support (fills tuwanuwa if it leaves), apasa holds, fleet greatgreen->cilicia. T7 STRIKE PLAN: lukka army moves to kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa army supports lukka->kizzuwatna, cilicia fleet supports lukka->kizzuwatna = strength 3 vs Hatti fleet 1 + kanesh support 1 = 2. Then tuwanuwa army must be in tuwanuwa (not moved to hattusa) at T7, so at T7 do NOT send it to hattusa; mira army holds/refills behind. If kanesh army attacks tuwanuwa, its support to kizzuwatna vanishes and my strike wins anyway. After Kizzuwatna: kizzuwatna + tuwanuwa armies both touch kanesh; attack it with a third unit supporting. Ugarit (Mitanni, walls, 40) is next to kizzuwatna: army move + 1 support takes it. No envoy at court this season, so no letters. Promises: told Alashiya my fleet goes via Greatgreen and Cilicia only against Hatti's Kizzuwatna, never Tamassos or Enkomi (keep that). k210 with Hatti broken in spirit; k219 Egypt and k304 Alashiya friendships (neither aids Hatti) stand. c83 reaches Egypt T7 (Memphis-born, was asked for gold gift), c89 at Alashiya (asked for gifts). Did not hire c108/c125 (wages cut strength). Watch treasury below 20, Hatti raising armies, Mitanni (9+ provinces, growth about 2.0) moving on Hatti land. No sleep: situation is moving.

T6: UGARIT IS NOW MITANNI'S (walls) - the scheduled T9 buy_city ugarit is void; I cancelled it with an empty T9 entry. ALL free city-states are now taken (Lukka Arzawa, Ugarit/Carchemish/Isuwa Mitanni, Damascus/Qadesh/Tyre/Gaza/Megiddo Egypt, Mari/Susa Babylonia). Nothing left to buy, so the plan is: HOARD gold (net about +79/season; gold counts 1:1 in strength), keep every treaty, avoid war, stay awake while foreign fleets sit next to Cyprus. Audiences done T6 (envoys Ashur-nadin of Egypt, Pirissi of Hatti, Mazipalali of Arzawa all answered, no gold sent to anyone). I told Egypt I see no foreign fleets or armies near my coasts and kept my fleet count private. I told Hatti I take no side and want a sealed peace tablet for Cyprus, Byblos, Amurru; no gold. I told Arzawa our tablet k282 stands, my ships keep out of the sea off Kizzuwatna, and asked their ships to keep clear of Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos and Amurru. Arzawa fleet is in greatgreen (adjacent to EMPTY tamassos - a fleet can walk in; watch it) and Egypt fleet in levantsea (adjacent to enkomi). If either fleet gathers a second ship or moves toward tamassos/enkomi, raise an army at tamassos (100) at once. Tamassos has no unit; enkomi has my one fleet. THREAT: Mitanni (about 9 provinces, biggest) now sits at Ugarit next to Amurru/Byblos (walls hold strength 1). I have no contact with Mitanni. PLAN: when Paser c102 (from Egypt) and Ili-iddina c95 (from Hatti) come home at T7, send one to Mitanni (2 seasons) with a brotherly non-aggression tablet naming Byblos, Amurru, Cyprus, no gold; send the other to Egypt/Arzawa/Hatti to keep treaties warm. Envoy wages end T10 - rehire only if useful (candidates c108 asks 30, c125 asks 35 - too dear). Unassayed Egyptian gold g311 (20): not assaying. Strength 1504 vs 1200 start (1.25).

T6: Treasury 7 after drought. The kizzuwatna FLEET DESERTED (unpaid). I now have only 2 armies: sapinuwa and kanesh. Arzawa seen: army at tuwanuwa and at lukka, and a mira army tried to enter tuwanuwa (lukka supported it), so Arzawa has at least 3 armies near me. Their tuwanuwa -> hattusa bounced against my sapinuwa -> hattusa last turn. Hattusa can only be hit from tuwanuwa (strength 1, nobody else is adjacent), so one army sitting there is safe. T6 ORDERS: sapinuwa -> hattusa with kanesh supporting that move (a supporter still holds with 1, so this costs nothing); if Arzawa moves in too, mine wins 2 to 1. Kizzuwatna is EMPTY and Arzawa can reach it at strength 2 (lukka plus tuwanuwa support), so it will probably fall this season. I judged that putting an army there alone would only get it dislodged and destroyed, and would leave kanesh empty. Sapinuwa is also empty (only Mitanni isuwa touches it; Tushratta swore through Zitanza he sends nothing against Hattusa, Kanesh or Sapinuwa, but he broke k297 over Carchemish, so do not trust him). Kanesh could be hit at strength 2 only by Mitanni isuwa plus carchemish together. Income from T7 is 150 if I keep all 4 provinces (115 if kizzuwatna falls); upkeep 60, wages 19 until T10 (c32 11, c39 8). Next season treasury is about 78 (about 43 without kizzuwatna). PLAN: raise an army (100) as soon as I can afford it, in an empty home province (hattusa or sapinuwa; kizzuwatna if still mine), then retake Kizzuwatna and Tuwanuwa: one army moves in, another supports, and a supporter next to the target is needed to beat a hold of 1 plus support. Do not let anyone take Hattusa. If gold stays short, consider dismissing the envoys to save the wages. Do not spend on tablets. Envoys: c32 Keliya reaches Egypt at T7 (asks for pure gold, sounds out Egypt on Mitanni; back T9). c39 Pirissi is at or returning from Alashiya (gifts promised; sealed k365 with Alashiya: no Hatti-Alashiya war, their lands are Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru; watch for Alashiyan ships in cilicia). Both were born in Washukanni, so watch for leaks. c62 Zitanza (Mitanni's envoy) is secretly in my pay, so his reports are probably honest. No envoy was at my court to carry a letter this turn (only c108 Tehip-tilla of Arrapha, unhired). Promises made: Mitanni, I send nothing against Harran or Washukanni or Isuwa while his word stands (verbal; I may break it if it suits); Alashiya, no ships or troops against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru (k365). k189 (Arzawa) is void.

T6 (Egypt). Treasury 553 before orders; income 310, upkeep 65, wages 47 (until T10). ALL FREE CITIES ARE GONE: Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa, Ashur, Nineveh are Mitanni; Mari, Susa, Arbela, Ekallatum are Babylonia; Lukka is Arzawa; Byblos and Amurru are Alashiya. Assyria has fallen. So nothing to buy; growth now only by conquest. Alashiya sealed k363 this turn (peace incl. Byblos and Amurru as their harbours, my Delta/Gaza/Megiddo/Tyre/Damascus/Qadesh named as mine). It binds nobody; I intend to break it. STANDINGS GUESS: Mitanni (330 yield, started on 145) is my real rival on growth ratio (probably 1.8 or more), Babylonia 320 yield (started 195), me 1.46. Baseline income alone will not beat Mitanni, so I must take cities, ideally from Mitanni (Ugarit 40, Carchemish 35). ORDERS T6: raised fleet B in delta (120; delta was empty and Arzawa fleet sits in greatgreen next to it - if Arzawa slips into delta, retake it with A levantsea->delta supported by Gaza army gaza->delta). Fleet A holds in levantsea (watch enkomi, byblos, syriansea). Gaza army holds. No envoy was at court so no letters. PLAN BYBLOS: T7 A levantsea->syriansea AND B delta->levantsea (no clash); T8 B levantsea->byblos with A (syriansea) supporting (strength 2 vs walls 1). Abort if Alashiya has a fleet adjacent to Byblos (syriansea/levantsea/amurru) that could support its walls, or if 2+ Alashiyan fleets appear. Then T9+: fleet in Byblos supports a move into Amurru from syriansea. Raise a 3rd fleet in delta at T8 (once B has left) for Ugarit (Mitanni army at carchemish can support Ugarit walls, so need 3 strength: attacker + 2 supports, or armies convoyed to Amurru/Byblos). Convoy the Gaza army via levantsea to Byblos once it is mine; an army in Byblos protects Qadesh and Damascus (supports their walls holding) and stages Ugarit. Danger to watch: Mitanni Carchemish army plus Babylonian Mari army can jointly take Qadesh (Qadesh walls hold only 1). ENVOYS: Mane c20 en route to Mitanni (arrives T7), Ashur-nadin c27 returning from Alashiya, Sin-iqisham c120 returning from Hatti; read their reports; use them to set Babylonia, Hatti and Arzawa against Mitanni. Unhired: c108 Tehip-tilla 28, c125 Ehli-Teshub 33. Do not tell Alashiya anything about the fleets.

T6 (Burna-Buriash). Assyria is dead; Arbela mine. Mitanni holds 9 provinces (about 330 yield, growth well above my 1.52) and is the rival I must cut or I lose the race. DECISION: break k204 (oath of non-aggression, sworn before Shamash) and strike Mitanni now, while only ashur and terqa armies stand near me and nineveh is EMPTY. Orders: ekallatum -> ashur with arbela supporting (arbela's support cannot be cut: only ashur touches it, and an attack from ashur does not cut), mari -> terqa to cut terqa's support of ashur (ashur hold would otherwise be 2, tie), durkurigalzu -> ekallatum with sippar supporting (backfill), susa supports arbela holding. Expected: ashur falls (2 vs 1), its army is destroyed. Worst case a bounce, no loss. I refused Tushratta's Qadesh request and refused his new tablet; lied that the road through Mari is open to his caravans (keep it open only if it costs nothing; now void). Expect Mitanni to turn hostile and perhaps raise armies at terqa/harran/washukanni/taidu. NEXT (T7): if ashur is mine, take nineveh (empty, 35) with a unit from ashur or arbela, and attack terqa: ashur -> terqa supported by mari and ekallatum (3). Move sippar/susa forward as reserves. Watch ekallatum (support cuts from terqa). Gold 755 kept (counts as strength); consider raising 1-2 armies at babylon/nippur if Mitanni masses troops. Hired c76 Yanhamu (was Assyria's envoy; Assyria gone; do not trust fully, check loyalty) at 16 a season: use him to reach Hatti or Egypt against Mitanni (tell them Mitanni marched on Qadesh and that I struck Ashur). c46 reaches Egypt T7 with friendship tablet and honest intel; c51 home about T7. Awake every turn.

orders.letter: Brother Burna-Buriash, I have sealed your tablet and I keep it. Now let us profit together from Egypt's garrisons in Syria, which stand on walls and thin armies. In the season you hear this, let your army in Mari support my army from Carchemish moving into Qadesh. The season after, my army in Qadesh will support your army from Mari moving into Damascus. Qadesh falls to Mitanni, Damascus to Karduniash, and the road through Mari stays open to both our merchants. Egypt grows fat while we quarrel over small things. Tell me by your envoy that it is agreed.
orders.mandate: May agree to the joint strike on Qadesh then Damascus as stated, and to keep the road through Mari open. May not cede any province, promise gold, or promise troops against Karduniash's lands.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Mitanni, brothers, act together against Egypt in Syria. In the season of sealing, the army of Karduniash in Mari supports the army of Mitanni moving from Carchemish into Qadesh. The next season the army of Mitanni in Qadesh supports the army of Karduniash moving from Mari into Damascus. Qadesh is Mitanni's, Damascus is Karduniash's. The road through Mari stays open to both. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Great King of Arzawa, my brother: Tushratta of Mitanni wishes well to you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Hatti is weak with hunger and fights you in the west. I stand on its eastern border at Isuwa and Carchemish. Let us act together. When my army strikes Kanesh from Isuwa and Carchemish, let your army in Tuwanuwa support the strike into Kanesh. Kanesh, Sapinuwa and Kizzuwatna I would hold; Hattusa and what lies by your border would be yours. Send word by your envoy of the season you will move, and I will move with you.
orders.mandate: May agree to a joint campaign against Hatti, to mutual support in the season of the strike, and to a division where Mitanni holds Kanesh, Sapinuwa and Kizzuwatna and Arzawa holds Hattusa. May not cede any of my provinces or send gold.

proposal.text: Arzawa and Mitanni are brothers. Both shall march against Hatti in a season they agree. The army of Arzawa in Tuwanuwa supports the army of Mitanni into Kanesh. Mitanni holds Kanesh, Sapinuwa and Kizzuwatna, Arzawa holds Hattusa. Neither shall march against the lands of the other. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

value.notes: T6 (Tushratta). FACTS: Assyria is dead; Babylonia took Arbela (army from Susa moved in; Susa maybe empty). I hold ashur, nineveh (empty until taidu army arrives), carchemish, isuwa, ugarit (walls, cannot garrison), harran, taidu, terqa, washukanni = 330 yield. No free city-states remain: all expansion now is by conquest. Sealed k358 with Babylonia this turn (Ashur/Nineveh mine; Arbela/Ekallatum/Susa/Mari theirs; sworn). Babylonia now the main threat (armies at arbela, ekallatum, mari next to terqa/ashur/nineveh) and also my only help against Egypt's walled Qadesh. T6 ORDERS: taidu->nineveh; washukanni->harran (central reserve; harran can support terqa/isuwa/carchemish next turn); ashur supports terqa hold; terqa holds; isuwa and carchemish support each other's hold (Hatti kanesh+sapinuwa could hit isuwa 2v1). No raise: 6 armies are enough for posts, upkeep 180; save gold (income net about +134). Hire attempts: c125 Ehli-Teshub 30, c69 Artessupa 16; seek_candidates for more envoys. Letters tried (may be rejected if not yet hired): c125 -> Babylonia: joint strike, T7 Mari army supports Carchemish->Qadesh, T8 my Qadesh army supports Mari->Damascus (Qadesh to Mitanni, Damascus to Karduniash), sworn tablet. c69 -> Arzawa (2 seasons): alliance against Hatti, Arzawa supports my Carchemish->Kanesh from Tuwanuwa; I take Kanesh/Sapinuwa/Kizzuwatna, Arzawa Hattusa. PLAN T7: if Babylonia agrees (look at audience report) carchemish->qadesh with mari support and harran->carchemish refill; else hold. Walls need strength 2. Hatti kanesh and sapinuwa support each other; I only have 2 staging provinces (isuwa, carchemish) vs Hatti so I need an ally's help (Arzawa at tuwanuwa) to break kanesh. Envoys Ubaru c57 (at Babylonia T6) and Zitanza c62 (at Hatti T6) return about T7-T8: use them for Egypt (brotherhood, gold) and Arzawa. SUSPICIONS: Babylonia may stab at Terqa/Ashur (keep harran reserve, nineveh army); Artessupa is ex-Assyrian and may resent Babylonia; Ehli-Teshub Carchemish-born (Carchemish is mine now). Hatti angry about my Carchemish breach (k275). Keep promise to Babylonia: no march on Ekallatum/Susa/Mari/Arbela; no sheltering Assyrians.

value.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well in Hattusa. I hear your words gladly. Hatti wants the southern road quiet as you do, and has no quarrel with Egypt in Gaza, Damascus or Tyre. Let traders and envoys pass in peace. You ask where my armies stand: they stand in Hattusa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna, as a king's armies should, and I fear no one. I will say this truly, as a brother. Arzawa swore a tablet of brotherhood before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk, and broke it in the very same season, striking at Tuwanuwa. A king who breaks an oath before your own god Amun will take your gold and still boast that he watches you from behind. You did well to send him nothing. Any gold that reaches Arzawa becomes spears at Hatti's back, and tomorrow at yours. Tuwanuwa is my land and I will have it back in my own time. With Mitanni I keep a border peace; with Assyria I have no quarrel. A brother who is honoured with a worthy gift, of pure gold, will remember it in Hattusa. Now tell me truly, brother, what Egypt intends toward Mitanni and Babylonia, and whom Egypt fears. Carry this faithfully." The king spoke kindly: "Go in peace, Sin-iqisham. Tell my brother Napkhururiya that Hatti keeps the north and Egypt the south, and that the roads stay open. Carry my words exactly as I gave them." All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Hatti keeps 2 army and 1 fleet near its capital. At the court of Hatti, the treasury looks thin. In Hatti: the rains failed and the harvest withers across the land

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me. I am glad the long road is open between us. Your words are heard and are welcome. Egypt keeps peace with every brother who keeps peace, and the lands of Canaan are mine and will stay mine. I have no quarrel with Babylonia and I make no promise against her, but I see which kings grow, and I do not wish any one of them to become master of the north and east. Gold between brothers follows proof, not hope. Show me your army standing against the Babylonian, and tell me how many troops Babylonia keeps in Ekallatum and Dur-Kurigalzu, where Mitanni's army stands, and what Hatti does. Send these words by a swift envoy and I will answer in kind. Until then take my good will, and say to your lord that my door is open to him." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: Egypt keeps 0 army and 1 fleet near its capital. At the court of Egypt, the court lives comfortably.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king said: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Our tablet is sealed and I hold to it; my ships and men raise no hand against Egypt or its lands, and Byblos and Amurru stay open harbours to your merchants. Near my coasts I see no foreign fleet and no foreign army; the Cilician and Syrian waters are quiet. What I hear of Arzawa at Lukka and of Mitanni and Babylonia in the north I hear only from rumour, as you do. How many ships I keep is a king's own business, brother. Know that they are enough to guard my harbours and I will send word if any aggressor shows a sail. Do likewise: tell me at once if the ships of Hatti or any other king move toward Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru. Copper goes to Egypt on open roads, and I look for gifts of pure, full-weight gold in return, as between brothers." All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Alashiya keeps 0 army and 1 fleet near its capital. At the court of Alashiya, the court lives comfortably. Pirissi, envoy of Hatti, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank my brother for the words he sent and for keeping his ships and garrisons from my coasts. I keep the same toward him: no ship or spear of Alashiya will come against Hatti or the harbour of Kizzuwatna, and my copper ships will keep sailing there. My house is a house of copper and of ships, not of spears. My treasury is spent on my new harbours and I cannot send gold now; if my brother's tablet of peace for Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru comes sealed by his hand, I will answer it in kind. When Nergal and the harvest allow, I will remember a brother's gift. Go safely, Pirissi." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Alashiya keeps 0 army and 1 fleet near its capital. Mazipalali, envoy of Arzawa, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king spoke kindly: "Kidin-Adad, I have heard the words of Burna-Buriash, my brother, as a brother's. Say to him: Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, wishes well to him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. I seal the tablet. The Assyrian is the foe of us both and I will neither feed nor shelter him. Let no captain's quarrel trouble our border at Terqa: keep your chariots from my homeland as mine keep from yours. I will place my own men where they are needed to guard what is mine. Now, as one who has eaten at my table, tell me plainly how many chariots stand at Ekallatum and at Mari, and whether the Assyrian still held Arbela when you left. Take this small gift for the road." The king spoke kindly: "Kidin-Adad, I have sealed the tablet of my brother Burna-Buriash. Ashur and Nineveh are Mitanni's, as my men hold them, and the Assyrian is the foe of us both. Tell him that Mitanni keeps faith with those who keep faith with it. Let the border at Terqa stay quiet, and let each king guard what is his own. Say also that the road through Mari should stand open to my merchants and envoys, as he has already offered. Go in peace, and take my greeting to his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots and his horses." The king of Mitanni is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: At the court of Mitanni, the treasury looks thin.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, Great King, my brother: Burna-Buriash your brother wishes well to you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Your words please me, and I keep the oath sworn before Shamash. The road through Mari is open to the caravans and envoys of Mitanni, free of toll. This I grant gladly, and Ubaru, a son of Sippar, will see it kept. Assyria is finished, brother: Arbela has fallen to my armies, with Ekallatum, Susa and Mari. Let no army of Mitanni stand at Arbela's gates; those lands are Karduniash's, as the tablet my own envoy carries to you names them. As for Qadesh: I cannot draw the army out of Mari. The city is not yet quiet under a new lord, and that army must stand among its people. Also my envoys are on the road to Pharaoh asking for gold, and if Egypt's city falls to my support in the very season they stand before him, their heads and my gold are lost. Let them return, and I will speak again. For the same reason I do not seal a tablet that names the city of a third king. Seal the tablet my envoy carries, which names the lands of both of us." The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, Great King, my brother: Burna-Buriash your brother holds the oath of Shamash and will not march against the lands of Mitanni; the tablet already sealed between us stands. The new tablet I do not seal this season. It gives away the cities of a third king, and it names Arbela in no line, though Arbela is held by my armies and is Karduniash's. I seal no tablet that leaves a brother's border unwritten. When my envoy comes home from Pharaoh, send a tablet naming only the lands of the two of us: Mari, Ekallatum, Susa and Arbela to Karduniash; the lands you hold to Mitanni. That I will seal gladly. The road through Mari stays open to your caravans and envoys, free of toll."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King, king of Hatti, your brother. All goes well with me, and may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for your words about my harvest; the gods send drought and the gods lift it, and my granaries are filling. I have heard your words and I keep peace on my side of the border: I send nothing against Harran, Washukanni or your homeland, and none of my chariots goes toward Isuwa while your word stands. Brother, you know now what the seal of Arzawa is worth; he swore to me before Teshub and broke the oath in the same season. Let us both watch him, and let each tell the other what he learns of his armies and of Egypt. I will tell you what I see. Shamash is witness to what is said between us." What I saw: In Hatti: the rains failed and the harvest withers across the land

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king said, in short: "Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I thank you for speaking plainly, as brothers should. Our tablet stands: we are at peace and friends, and neither of us aids Hatti against the other. My ships have no business off Kizzuwatna and will not go there; my fleet lies at Enkomi and my merchants trade in peace. I ask only that your ships keep clear of Tamassos and Enkomi, as you promised, and of my harbours at Byblos and Amurru on the Syrian coast. As for my merchants: they have seen no war fleets in the Cilician Sea beyond the ones you name, and I will send word if that changes. The treasury of Alashiya is spent on its own affairs this season, so I send no gold now, but my goodwill is true."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king said, in short: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. It goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your copper. Your words are received with joy, and Paser is welcome at my court as a son of Memphis. I seal your tablet. Egypt sends no army and no ship of war against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, and your harbours stay open to my merchants as mine are open to yours. I ask the same for the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Damascus and Qadesh. If any king threatens your coast or mine, I will tell you, and I ask you to tell me. My gold is for brothers who keep faith, and a gift that answers your copper will follow once the merchants have begun to move between our harbours. Tell me through Paser, so my merchants may sail with confidence, how many ships and how many men you keep at Byblos, at Amurru and on Cyprus, and whether any foreign fleet has been seen in the Syrian or Cilician seas." The king said, in short: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, has sealed the tablet and sends it home with Paser. Let it stand before Shamash. Egypt keeps faith with brothers who keep faith. Your harbours are open to my merchants, and mine to yours. When your copper moves, my gold will answer. Tell me what fleets and men you keep, and whether any foreign ship has been seen in the Syrian or Cilician seas, and I will tell you what I see. May it go well with you, your household, your sons, your ships and your copper." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Egypt keeps 0 army and 0 fleet near its capital. At the court of Egypt, the court is rich.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king spoke kindly: "Say to my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your words are welcome. Hatti sends no ships or troops against Cyprus, and I will keep my fleet from your harbours at Tamassos and Enkomi while your ships stay out of the Kizzuwatna coast and the sea at Lukka. I have sealed your tablet. Hear this, brother: Arzawa broke his oath to me in the very season he swore it, and Mitanni did the same with Carchemish. Kings who break oaths in one season will break them to you in the next, so watch your coasts and keep your fleets at home. I have sent my own envoy to your court with my greetings; let your gifts return with him, pure gold and copper, as is fitting between brothers, for my country has had a hard season. Tell me before you go: what ships does Arzawa keep in the Western Sea and at Lukka, and does any Alashiyan fleet sail the Cilician Sea? And what does Egypt say of Mitanni?" The king spoke kindly: "Say to my brother, the Great King of Alashiya: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I have sealed the tablet you sent, and Shamash is witness: no ships or troops of Hatti against Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru, so long as none of yours come against Kizzuwatna, Lukka's sea or the lands I hold. Tell your master that my envoy awaits at your court, and that gifts of pure gold and copper sent back with him will be remembered as the mark of a true brother. My country has had a hard season, and I will not forget who stood by me. Keep your fleets at home and tell me what you see in the Western Sea." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: In Hatti: the rains failed and the harvest withers across the land
I am Tehip-tilla of Arrapha, once a copper trader. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.
I am Ammistamru of Ugarit, once a merchant. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.
I am Yanhamu of Byblos, once a interpreter. No envoy knows the roads and courts as I do; kings have praised my eloquence, and I have never failed a master.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I received your words through Sin-iqisham and answered them; now I send my own man so you hear it from my mouth. You asked whom I fear. I fear no army, but I watch the growth of one king: Tushratta of Mitanni. Hatti and Egypt lie in the path of the same hand. Arzawa, to whom you wisely sent nothing, keeps no oath and begs gold from every court. I hold the north gate at Kanesh and Kizzuwatna. I ask of you what a brother gives: a gift of pure gold, which I will turn into spears where Mitanni must pass before he reaches Syria. Tell me truly what Egypt will do if Mitanni moves on Qadesh, and whether Egypt wishes Hatti strong or weak. The roads stay open for your traders and envoys. My lord hopes that no quarrel will ever come between your houses." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger. For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Say to the Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. The road between us has been closed too long and I open it now. Egypt keeps peace with every brother who keeps peace. Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh and Tyre are mine and will stay mine; I ask that no army of yours cross into them, and Egypt sends none against Mitanni. I see your power grow in the north. I also see that Babylonia keeps an army in Mari, close to your Terqa, and took Ekallatum from Assyria, and that Hatti is said to starve. I do not wish any one king to become master of the north and east. Tell me what troops Babylonia and Hatti keep near your border, and what Mitanni intends. Gold between brothers follows proof, not hope. Send a swift envoy with your answer."

Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me, my chariots are many and my treasury is sound. Your words were heard and are welcome. You ask what Egypt will do if Mitanni moves on Qadesh. Qadesh, Damascus, Tyre, Megiddo and Gaza are mine, and I do not leave my cities to any hand. Let Tushratta come and learn it. You ask if I wish Hatti strong or weak. I wish Hatti strong enough to hold the north gate, for a Mitanni who must watch Kanesh and Kizzuwatna cannot spare his spears for Syria. On gold: Egypt's gold goes where it is seen to work. When Hatti's spears press Carchemish or Isuwa and Mitanni's armies are drawn north, my brother will find my hand open; I do not send gold ahead of deeds, to any king. Now answer me truly, Keliya, for I would hear it from a man who has walked many courts. How many armies does Hatti keep in the field? Where does he see Tushratta's armies, and what does Carchemish hold? Does Babylonia speak to your lord, and what does Babylon say of Mitanni?
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King, king of Egypt, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I rejoice that the road is open. Mitanni has no army marching on the Nile lands, nor on Gaza, Megiddo or Tyre. Let our envoys settle the northern cities by sealed tablet, as brothers do. You asked what I see. Babylonia keeps armies in Mari, Ekallatum and Arbela, and holds Susa. It took Assyria's lands and now holds ten provinces, as you do, my brother. Assyria is no more. Hatti is hungry and weak, and I hold Isuwa and Carchemish against it, so it cannot move south against your friends. Mitanni intends to keep what it holds, to watch Babylonia's armies at Terqa, and to let no single king become master of the north and east. I too fear that. You say gold follows proof. The proof is in my words, which you can test with your own watchers. Send me a swift envoy with 150 shekels of good, pure gold, a gift between brothers, and I will raise chariots and keep Babylonia and Hatti busy. In return I will send you word of every army that moves toward your border. May Amun and Shamash witness our brotherhood.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully, and speak of Mitanni's friendship and strength before your lord, and urge him to send the gold.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

Keliya, you carry my words and you gave me none of yours in return. A man who has walked many courts knows what a king needs: numbers and places, not courtesies. Tell Suppiluliuma, my brother, this plainly. Egypt watches Tushratta as he watches Egypt, and our cities in Syria are held and will be held. If Hatti presses Carchemish or Isuwa and draws Mitanni north, he will see what Egypt does, and he will see it in deeds, not in promises. Let his next envoy bring what this one did not: how many armies Hatti keeps in the field, where Tushratta's spears stand, and what Babylon says. Brothers who share a danger share their eyes. Go in peace, and may the road be safe for you.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words to Suppiluliuma exactly as spoken, and bring back true numbers of Hatti's armies, where Mitanni's armies stand, and what Babylonia says of Mitanni.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Burna-Buriash. He says: "Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked for honest word of Hatti, Mitanni and Assyria; here it is. Assyria is broken: Mitanni has taken Nineveh and Ashur, and only Arbela remains to the Assyrian, which my chariots take this season. Tushratta of Mitanni also holds Isuwa and Carchemish, and told my envoy that Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh are his to seek. Qadesh is your city, brother, and it lies beside his men at Carchemish. A rumour says Hatti starves and its granaries stand empty. I hold Susa, Mari and Ekallatum and seek no quarrel with Egypt. A brother's gift follows a brother's deed, and this is my deed." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your word is received as a brother's word, and I seal the tablet you sent, before Shamash and Amun. Egypt remembers who sent honest word of the north. You tell me that Tushratta of Mitanni calls Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh his to seek. Qadesh is mine, and Egypt holds what it holds. A king who swallows Assyria and then reaches for Qadesh will next look at Mari and Ekallatum, which lie nearer to Terqa than to Babylon. Watch him, brother, as I watch him. Send me word at once of every Mitanni army that moves toward Terqa, Mari or Qadesh, and I will send you the same of the Mitanni men I see in the west. Gifts follow deeds, as you say, and my deeds will answer yours. Tell your king I look for his next word soon.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words exactly as spoken, and tell your king plainly that Mitanni's reach toward Qadesh threatens Mari and Ekallatum as well.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tarhundaradu. He says: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. You asked for true word, and I send it plainly. Hatti keeps one army at Kanesh and one fleet at Kizzuwatna; his capital Hattusa has stood nearly empty. I hold Tuwanuwa, where I destroyed his army, and Lukka, and I keep both. I strike next at Kizzuwatna by land and sea, so Hatti will not gather toward the Syrian lands soon. Of Mitanni I warn you as a brother: he has swallowed Ashur and Nineveh, holds Carchemish and Isuwa on your northern border and has eight provinces. Watch Qadesh. My word has proved true; send the gifts that follow true word, in gold, by this envoy, and let your envoys come again with news of Mitanni and Hatti."

Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: Napkhururiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your word is received and it is weighed as true. Our tablet of peace and friendship stands before Shamash and Amun: neither of us aids Hatti, and each shares news of threats with the other. I send a brother's gift with this envoy, as respect for true word. Press Hatti as you say, at Kizzuwatna. Mitanni is the greater danger to us both: he holds Ashur, Nineveh, Carchemish, Isuwa and Ugarit, and grows fat while others fight. When Hatti is humbled, send word of what you see of Mitanni's armies and ships on the coast and at Carchemish, and I will send mine in return. My eyes are on Qadesh.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully and without change, and tell your lord that Egypt is a friend who rewards true word.

value.speech: Your generosity honours me. I will tell my lord how warmly I was received.

orders.letter: Say to the king of Babylonia, my brother: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I speak plainly, as brothers should. Hatti is broken and its lands lie open; Mitanni has swallowed Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit and grows faster than any of us. A king who sits at Kanesh and Hattusa and also at Terqa will threaten every border, yours first. I hold the west and take what Hatti cannot keep. I ask for friendship between our courts, and that each tell the other of threats from Mitanni.
orders.mandate: May seal a tablet of peace and friendship with Babylonia, neither aiding Mitanni against the other, each sharing news of threats. May not promise gold, troops or any land.

proposal.text: Babylonia and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Neither aids Mitanni against the other. Each shares news of threats from Mitanni with the other.

value.notes: T7: Treasury 45, net -20/season until Kizzuwatna pays (wages 20 until T10). Hatti now shows armies at hattusa (came from sapinuwa, kanesh supported) and kanesh; kizzuwatna looks EMPTY (Hatti fleet gone). T7 ORDERS: lukka -> kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa and cilicia fleet both support it (strength 3; even if Hatti cuts the tuwanuwa support, 2 beats a lone kanesh step). Mira supports tuwanuwa hold (Hatti hattusa+kanesh can only make 2 vs my 2 = bounce). Apasa army follows into lukka (free if lukka stays). Sent c89 to Babylonia (2 seasons) with a plain friendship tablet: neither aids Mitanni, share news; urged them to watch Mitanni (growth about 2.0, same as Babylonia about 1.9; they are my real rivals). No gold promised. PROMISES: none new. k210 Hatti broken in spirit; k219 Egypt and k304 Alashiya friendships (neither aids Hatti) stand; told Alashiya my fleet only goes against Kizzuwatna, never Tamassos/Enkomi/Byblos/Amurru (keep unless Alashiya is crippled by plague, rumor says half its army dead - maybe a later target but needs convoys). CHECK NEXT: did Kizzuwatna fall? If yes, hold it, then Kanesh is only touched by tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna (max strength 2 vs hold 1 + hattusa support 1 = tie) so strike only when hattusa army has moved away or its support is cut; also Ugarit (Mitanni, walls) touches kizzuwatna: army move + 1 support. To win I must reach growth over 2.0: need all of Hatti (hattusa 50, kanesh 35, sapinuwa 30, kizzuwatna 35). Watch Mitanni at isuwa/carchemish racing for Hatti land. No free city-states remain to buy. Do not hire c108 (30/season). c83 returns from Egypt soon. No sleep.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to the Great King of Hatti, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Tushratta of Mitanni has swallowed Ashur, Nineveh, Isuwa and Carchemish, and he now reaches for Qadesh. I have broken the Assyrian and now march against Mitanni. Carchemish and Isuwa stand on your border at Kanesh. If you move on them while I take the lands east of the river, Mitanni cannot hold both. Let us seal a tablet of brotherhood against Tushratta.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed brotherhood and a shared war against Mitanni, and to the partition in the tablet. May not give gold, troops or any of my provinces. Report honestly what Hatti's army and treasury look like.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Hatti are brothers. Both shall war against Mitanni and neither shall make peace with Tushratta without the other's knowledge. Hatti shall take Isuwa and Carchemish; Karduniash shall take Terqa, Nineveh, Taidu, Harran and Washukanni. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

value.notes: T7 (Burna-Buriash). T6 result: Ashur taken, Mitanni ashur army destroyed (oath k204 broken on purpose; I lied to Ubaru that I hold the oath). mari->terqa bounced (1 vs 1). Mitanni now shows armies at terqa and nineveh (nineveh was NOT empty). Harran, washukanni, taidu unseen: possible hidden supporters. My armies: arbela, ashur, ekallatum, mari, sippar, susa (6, upkeep 180). T7 orders: arbela -> nineveh with ashur support (2 vs 1); mari -> terqa with ekallatum support (2 vs 1); susa -> arbela and sippar -> mari as backfill (they only move if the front unit leaves); raised new armies at durkurigalzu and babylon (200). Reasoning on counterstrikes: if terqa/nineveh attack ashur, my attacks cut their supports (attack from a province other than the one supported into), so ashur holds 1 vs 1. Ekallatum's support for mari->terqa cannot be cut by terqa. NEXT (T8): if terqa fell, push washukanni (50) / harran (35) with 2-3 strength using ekallatum/ashur/mari armies; if nineveh fell, taidu (30) next. If either bounced, repeat with more support and bring the new armies up via ekallatum. Mitanni treasury looked thin so I expect few armies; watch for hostile Mitanni envoy Ubaru. Envoy c51 Kidin-Adad sent to Hatti (arrives T9, back T11) with a partition and alliance tablet against Mitanni: Hatti gets Isuwa and Carchemish, I get Terqa, Nineveh, Taidu, Harran, Washukanni. He gave a glowing report of Tushratta and took a gift, so he may lean to Mitanni: keep his mandate narrow and do not trust his report. c46 reaches Egypt this season with friendship tablet; back about T9. Yanhamu (c76) declined my wage, still at court, loyalty unknown. Gold 920 before the 200 spent on armies; net income about +165 before the new upkeep. Egypt (about 310 yield) is the other growth rival, do not provoke it. Awake every turn while at war.

orders.letter: To the Great King of Babylonia, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Hatti and Babylonia have no quarrel and no border; let there be peace and open roads between us. I speak of Tushratta of Mitanni. In three years he has taken Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Nineveh, and he seals peace on tablets and breaks it the same season. A man who does this to his neighbours will do it to the next one. My armies stand against his at Isuwa and Carchemish. If your armies press him at Terqa, Nineveh or Taidu, I will press him in the west, and what each takes, each keeps. Send me your answer by this envoy, tell me what you know of Mitanni's strength, and whether Babylonia stands firm in its land.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace and open roads between Hatti and Babylonia, and to a shared understanding that each presses Mitanni and keeps what he takes. May not give gold, land or troops, and may not promise war on any power but Mitanni.

value.notes: T7: Drought over. Treasury 78 (cannot raise, need 100). Income 150 (hattusa, kanesh, kizzuwatna, sapinuwa all still mine), upkeep 60, wages 19 until T10. Next season about 149: RAISE AN ARMY at T8 in kizzuwatna (exposed to lukka + tuwanuwa) or sapinuwa, whichever looks more threatened. Armies now: hattusa, kanesh (sapinuwa and kizzuwatna empty, nobody has taken them yet). Orders T7: hattusa and kanesh support each other's hold (free, a supporter still holds with 1). Hattusa can only be hit from tuwanuwa at strength 1, so it is safe with an army in it; never leave it empty. Arzawa (tuwanuwa, lukka, mira armies, maybe more) keeps aiming at hattusa; Mitanni isuwa and carchemish just support each other and look defensive. Retaking Tuwanuwa needs more than 3 attack strength (mira and lukka can support its hold); not possible yet. Carchemish trick for later: with 3 armies, sapinuwa -> isuwa (cuts isuwa's support of carchemish), kanesh -> carchemish supported by kizzuwatna = 2 vs hold 1, takes Carchemish. Needs 3 armies plus one left in hattusa = 4 armies. Sent Pirissi (c39) to Babylonia (2 seasons, arrives T9, back T11): anti-Mitanni front, no gold, no land, no troops in mandate; Mitanni is the runaway leader (about 2.2 growth). Keliya (c32) is returning from Egypt, back T9; wait for his report. Both envoys were born in Washukanni: watch for leaks and flattery. No tablets bought (20 each). Promises: Alashiya k365 (no war on Cyprus, Byblos, Amurru); Mitanni verbal peace (I may break it); Arzawa k189 void. c62 Zitanza (Mitanni's envoy) is secretly mine. Idea for later: Mitanni or Egypt may support my units; Alashiya is weak (0 army, plague rumours) but I am sworn to it, and I have no fleet.

orders.letter: Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to yours. Our tablet stands before Shamash and I keep it: Alashiya and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Your ships sail the Cilician Sea and I take it as the sail of a friend. So that no servant of either throne may mistake the other's meaning, I ask that we name our lands in a second tablet: Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos and Amurru are mine; Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa are yours. No ship or troops of either against the lands of the other, and each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Seal it, and send it home with Paser. I take no side in your quarrel with Hatti and ask none in mine.
orders.mandate: Paser may agree to seal the tablet as written, or a tablet of the same meaning naming the lands of both sides. He may promise that Alashiya sends no ships or troops against Arzawa's lands and that I will tell Arzawa of any king who threatens its coasts. He may NOT promise gold, ships or aid in the war against Hatti, and may not reveal what troops I keep.

proposal.text: Tablet between Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Alashiya and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Neither sends troops or ships of war against the lands of the other: for Alashiya, Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru; for Arzawa, Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa. Each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Neither aids Hatti against the other. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

orders.letter: Say to the Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, Great King, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to you and to yours. Our lands have come to border one another at Ugarit and Amurru, and between brothers who share a border there should be a sealed word and not a quarrel. I ask that Mitanni and Alashiya send no troops or ships of war against each other's lands, that the merchants of both pass freely, and that each tells the other of any king who threatens him. My lands are Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru. Seal the tablet Ili-iddina brings and send it home with him, and tell me through him how it goes in your country.
orders.mandate: Ili-iddina may agree to seal the tablet as written, or one of the same meaning naming the lands of both sides. He may promise that Alashiya sends no troops or ships against Mitanni and that I will tell Mitanni of threats I learn of. He may NOT promise gold, aid in war, or give any account of my ships or troops.

proposal.text: Tablet between the Great King of Mitanni and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Mitanni and Alashiya send no troops or ships of war against each other's lands: for Alashiya, Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru; for Mitanni, the lands it holds today. The merchants of both pass freely. Each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

Reconsider and raise an army at ENKOMI at once if (a) a SECOND foreign ship appears next to Cyprus, (b) any treaty partner is rude or silent, (c) Egypt keeps asking how many ships/men I keep (Egypt asked this T6 - I will NOT reveal that I have none). Arzawa fleet in cilicia (adjacent to both Cyprus provinces; it passed empty tamassos at T6 without taking it, probably bound for Kizzuwatna against Hatti); Egypt fleet in levantsea (adjacent to enkomi).
