Only Egypt, Hatti, Arzawa can reach Cyprus by sea (Mitanni and Babylonia have no homeland coast, Mitanni can only threaten Amurru/Byblos by land from Ugarit). SENT T7: Paser c102 -> Arzawa (1 season out; back T9) with tablet naming my four lands and Arzawa's, no ships/troops against each other, news of threats, mandate to seal only, no gold. Ili-iddina c95 -> Mitanni (2 seasons out, arrives T9, back T11) with a non-aggression tablet naming Cyprus, Byblos, Amurru; no gold. Both envoys wages end T10: rehire or let go then. Sealing costs 20 each. Not assaying g311 (20 Egyptian, probably fine). Gold counts 1:1, so HOARD; the rivals Mitanni (8 provinces) and Babylonia (10 provinces) are near 2.0 growth, Egypt about 1.6; I need about 2.0+ by T15, reachable by hoarding if Cyprus is not attacked (T15: about 2600-2700). Watch for: Mitanni troops at Ugarit moving on Amurru; Hatti collapse (Kizzuwatna is a coast prize, but I hold a sealed treaty with Hatti); any Egypt/Arzawa move on Cyprus. Stay awake each season.

orders.letter: Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your ships and your country. Our tablet stands before Shamash and Amun. You asked me to tell you at once if the ships of any king move toward Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru. Hear it now: the fleet of Arzawa has entered the Cilician Sea at the very shore of your island, and Hatti keeps a fleet at Kizzuwatna. I have therefore set my ships in the Levantine and Syrian seas, as a shield beside your harbours and not against them. Do not mistake my sails for an enemy's. Keep your own ships quietly in harbour so that no watcher confuses friend with foe, and send me word of what Arzawa's fleet does. I send a brother's gift of pure gold with this man, as copper and gold go freely between us.
orders.mandate: Speak friendly words only. Agree to nothing, promise no gold or troops, accept no tablet. Listen and report how many ships and armies Alashiya keeps, where they stand, and whether they have raised any new ones.

orders.letter: Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The tablet we sealed stands before Shamash and Amun, and Egypt keeps faith with a brother who sent honest word. Tushratta is the one king who threatens us both. I move my ships on the Syrian coast against his harbours at Ugarit while your chariots press him at Terqa: two hands on one enemy. Tell me how strong your armies stand at Mari, Terqa and Ekallatum, what Hatti or Arzawa have said to you, and what you plan toward Carchemish. As brothers sworn, keep Mari's men from Qadesh and Damascus, which are mine, and I will keep my hand from your lands. Send word of every Mitanni army that moves, and I will send you the same.
orders.mandate: May agree to share news and to act together against Mitanni, and that Egypt and Karduniash do not attack each other's lands. May not promise gold, troops or any Egyptian city. Bring back true numbers of Babylonia's armies.

value.notes: T7 (Egypt). Treasury 536, income 310, upkeep 100 (1 army + 2 fleets), wages 47 until T10. Strength 3636 (1.45). Babylonia (365 yield, sworn alliance k399 sealed today) and Mitanni (285 yield, at war with Babylonia: Mari army failed vs Terqa) outgrow me; I must conquer. TARGET: ALASHIYA, which has only 1 fleet (at enkomi) and 0 armies. PLAN: T7 A levantsea->syriansea, B delta->levantsea (positioning), raise fleet C in delta (may be rejected because delta is occupied at order time; if rejected, raise it at T8). T8: B levantsea->enkomi supported by A (syriansea->enkomi) = strength 2 vs their fleet 1, destroys it and takes the capital Enkomi (45). ABORT/adjust if Alashiya raises a fleet in tamassos (it could support enkomi holding) or moves its fleet; if enkomi is empty just walk in. T9: a lone fleet takes empty Tamassos (40) with no support; fleet C (levantsea) -> byblos with A (syriansea) supporting takes Byblos (walls hold 1, need 2); then Amurru (20) the same way. Unknown: whether a conquered walled city can host my fleet - check. Gaza army holds (keep for convoy later; could be convoyed to Cyprus/Byblos). I am breaking tablets k284 and k363 with Alashiya on purpose; cover story sent with c27 (Ashur-nadin) to Alashiya, arriving T8: I said my fleets guard Cyprus against Arzawa's fleet in cilicia and asked them to keep their ships in harbour (so my 2-fleet strike finds the fleet at enkomi), plus 20 pure gold. c120 Sin-iqisham -> Babylonia (arrives T9): coordinate against Mitanni, ask them to keep Mari's army off Qadesh/Damascus, ask for army numbers. He is Nineveh-born: watch for bias. Mane c20 is on his way home from Mitanni (T9): read his report. LATER: Ugarit (Mitanni, 40, walls, Carchemish army can support its walls so need 3 strength = 3 fleets) is the next prize, then Carchemish. Danger: Mitanni Carchemish army + another unit adjacent could take Qadesh (walls hold 1). Hatti starves and begs pure gold: I sent none (Keliya c32 took 20 of mine). Arzawa fleet sits in cilicia next to Cyprus: it may grab Tamassos/Enkomi first; watch. Unhired: c108 Tehip-tilla (28).

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, Great King, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your envoy Mane was received warmly. Now hear what the Babylonian did. Burna-Buriash swore to me before Shamash, and the copies my envoy shows you bear his seal. In the very season he sealed the last tablet, which names Ashur as Mitanni's, his army struck my men at Ashur and destroyed them, and his army from Mari came against my Terqa. He holds ten provinces and four armies at my border, and his envoys come to you for gold. A king who breaks Shamash's oath will break yours; your gold would feed the army that stands beside your Damascus and Qadesh. You said you do not wish one king to be master of the north and east. I hold Terqa, Nineveh and Harran against him and raise more armies. Gold sent to me is spent on chariots at his gates, far from the Nile. Seal the tablet my envoy carries, and send me word of what you see of Babylonian troops at Mari. Hatti is starving and I watch it from Carchemish and Isuwa.
orders.mandate: Seal the tablet of brotherhood and borders. Accept any gold. Promise only intelligence and that Mitanni sends no army against Egypt's lands. No cession of land, no promise of troops.

proposal.text: Napkhururiya and Tushratta are brothers. Neither shall send his armies against the lands of the other. Egypt holds Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh and Tyre. Mitanni holds Carchemish, Ugarit, Isuwa and its homeland. The king who breaks an oath sworn before Shamash shall not be fed, sheltered or paid by the other. Sworn before Shamash and Amun.

orders.letter: Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I rejoice that your granaries fill. I have heard your words and I keep mine: while your word stands, no chariot of Mitanni goes toward Hattusa or your homeland. You asked what I see, so I tell you. Burna-Buriash of Karduniash swore to me before Shamash and broke the oath in the same season: his army struck my men at Ashur. He now holds ten provinces and four armies at my border, and he alone grows. Arzawa keeps a fleet in the Cilician Sea beside Kizzuwatna and Ugarit. Egypt says Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh and Tyre are his, and that he wishes no king to become master of the north and east. Let us both watch Arzawa and Babylonia, and let each tell the other what he learns of their armies. Shamash is witness.
orders.mandate: Confirm peace on the borders of Harran, Washukanni, Isuwa and Carchemish. Exchange intelligence. Promise nothing in land, gold or troops, and seal no tablet.

orders.letter: Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Brother, the tablet we sealed names Ashur and Nineveh as Mitanni's, sworn before Shamash. In the same season your army took Ashur and destroyed my men there, and your army from Mari came against Terqa. Either your generals acted without your word, or the oath is broken, and Shamash saw it. I count it the act of your generals if you withdraw from Ashur and from the border of Terqa. Mitanni keeps armies at Terqa, Nineveh and Harran and will not be moved. Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari I do not touch, as the tablet says. Send me your answer by Ubaru and tell me plainly where your armies stand.
orders.mandate: Hear the answer. May agree that Mitanni claims no Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa or Mari if Ashur is returned. Promise no troops, no gold, no new tablet.

value.notes: T7 (Tushratta). FACTS: BABYLONIA BETRAYED k358/k183 on T6: ekallatum (+arbela support) took ASHUR and destroyed my army there, and mari->terqa failed. Their armies seen: arbela, ashur, ekallatum, mari (4 at my border). Babylonia is the growth leader (ten provinces) and now my main enemy. I hold carchemish, harran, isuwa, nineveh, taidu, terqa, ugarit, washukanni = 285 yield; armies at carchemish, harran, isuwa, nineveh, terqa (5). Taidu and washukanni are empty. Treasury 218. Egypt (Mane) was answered last turn: I promised no march on Gaza/Megiddo/Tyre and asked 150 gold; Egypt cannot station troops in its walled cities (Qadesh/Damascus/Tyre), so it is no military ally, only gold. T7 ORDERS: terqa holds with harran support (hold 2; a 3-strength Babylonian attack from ashur+ekallatum+mari could still break it); nineveh holds alone (cannot be supported this turn; ashur+arbela can take it with 2); isuwa/carchemish support each other. RAISED armies at taidu and washukanni (appear T8, cost 200, treasury about 18, next income about +29 with 7 armies = upkeep 210). DEFENCE DESIGN: Terqa is unbreakable with armies at terqa+harran+washukanni (hold 3 = their max 3); Nineveh holds with armies at nineveh+taidu (hold 2 = their max 2). Keep those 5 posts, isuwa+carchemish watch Hatti. ENVOYS: Ehli-Teshub c125 -> Egypt (2 seasons; shows k358,k183 to expose Babylonia's broken oath, asks 150 gold, tablet: brotherhood, borders, no gold/shelter for oathbreaker). Zitanza c62 -> Hatti (peace on Harran/Isuwa/Carchemish by my word, share intel on Babylonia and Arzawa fleet at cilicia; no tablet). Ubaru c57 -> Babylonia (protest, treat as generals' act, ask Ashur back, stall; ask him to report what he sees). SUSPICIONS: Ubaru is Sippar-born and was named by Burna-Buriash as guarantor of the road, probably in Babylonia's pocket. Kidin-Adad took my 10. PLAN: hold the line, rebuild gold; Hatti is starving, if it collapses (armies desert) strike kanesh/sapinuwa/kizzuwatna from isuwa+carchemish with the 3rd/4th army. Kizzuwatna and sapinuwa looked empty on T7. Qadesh cannot be taken (only carchemish borders it). Watch ashur/arbela/ekallatum/mari moves; if they empty ashur, retake it from terqa+nineveh. Do NOT break k275 against Hatti until the east is secure, unless Hatti falls apart.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of Tushratta, and I am, as ever, your servant. He says: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I rejoice that your granaries fill. I have heard your words and I keep mine: while your word stands, no chariot of Mitanni goes toward Hattusa or your homeland. You asked what I see, so I tell you. Burna-Buriash of Karduniash swore to me before Shamash and broke the oath in the same season: his army struck my men at Ashur. He now holds ten provinces and four armies at my border, and he alone grows. Arzawa keeps a fleet in the Cilician Sea beside Kizzuwatna and Ugarit. Egypt says Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh and Tyre are his, and that he wishes no king to become master of the north and east. Let us both watch Arzawa and Babylonia, and let each tell the other what he learns of their armies." For myself, I have always admired your court above all others.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Brother, the tablet we sealed names Ashur and Nineveh as Mitanni's, sworn before Shamash. In the same season your army took Ashur and destroyed my men there, and your army from Mari came against Terqa. Either your generals acted without your word, or the oath is broken, and Shamash saw it. I count it the act of your generals if you withdraw from Ashur and from the border of Terqa. Mitanni keeps armies at Terqa, Nineveh and Harran and will not be moved. Arbela, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari I do not touch, as the tablet says."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to yours. Our tablet stands before Shamash and I keep it: Alashiya and Arzawa are at peace and friends. Your ships sail the Cilician Sea and I take it as the sail of a friend. So that no servant of either throne may mistake the other's meaning, I ask that we name our lands in a second tablet: Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos and Amurru are mine; Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa are yours. No ship or troops of either against the lands of the other, and each tells the other of any king who threatens either. Seal it, and send it home with Paser. I take no side in your quarrel with Hatti and ask none in mine." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your ships and your country. Our tablet stands before Shamash and Amun. You asked me to tell you at once if the ships of any king move toward Cyprus, Byblos or Amurru. Hear it now: the fleet of Arzawa has entered the Cilician Sea at the very shore of your island, and Hatti keeps a fleet at Kizzuwatna. I have therefore set my ships in the Levantine and Syrian seas, as a shield beside your harbours and not against them. Keep your own ships quietly in harbour so that no watcher confuses friend with foe, and send me word of what Arzawa's fleet does. I send a brother's gift of pure gold with this man, as copper and gold go freely between us. My lord hopes that no quarrel will ever come between your houses." I carry the gold my lord sends, as the inventory on the tablet shows.

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for the gold and for your warning. Our tablet stands before Shamash and Amun, and I keep it: no troops or ships of mine go against Egypt's lands, and I ask the same of you for Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru. Arzawa and I are at peace by a sealed tablet, and so far its fleet has done nothing against me. Hatti and I are at peace by a sealed tablet too. I will tell you if any king's ships make a hostile move toward your lands or mine. I ask that your ships stay as shield beside Byblos and Amurru and keep out of the narrow water at the shores of Tamassos and Enkomi, as friends of the tablet should. What ships I keep in harbour is my own affair, as yours are yours. May no quarrel come between our houses.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash. May all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Brother, I have heard your words and Shamash has heard them with me. Ashur was the lair of the Assyrian, the foe of us both, and my generals pressed on against him with a hot heart; some went beyond what I commanded. I do not wish a quarrel between brothers over a few border roads. Let there be no more marching on either side while I weigh your words and send my own envoy to settle the border before Shamash. Do not hurry to raise more men; you will have my answer in due season. Ubaru, you were born in Sippar and served Shamash: speak truly to me what you saw on your road, and carry my words home as they were said.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words to Tushratta as spoken, saying that Burna-Buriash is troubled and weighing withdrawal. Then tell me truly which armies stand at Terqa, Nineveh, Harran, Washukanni and Taidu.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with yours. I hear your words and I keep mine: while your word stands, no chariot of Hatti goes toward Harran, Washukanni or Isuwa. Shamash is witness. What you tell of Karduniash I weigh gravely; a king who breaks an oath in the very season he swears it fears neither Shamash nor his brothers, and he grows while we watch. Arzawa did the same to me: he sealed a tablet of brotherhood and in that same season his army took Tuwanuwa. His armies stand at Tuwanuwa, Lukka and Mira, and his fleet lies in the Cilician Sea. Let us watch them both. Send me word, brother, of where the armies of Karduniash stand and which road they take, and I will send you what I learn of Arzawa. Honour my envoy when he comes.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully, and bring me word of what you see of Karduniash's armies and of the Mitanni troops at Isuwa and Carchemish.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone. I will carry your words to my lord faithfully.
value.commitments: said my lord will consider these words

value.speech: Paser, I receive you as the messenger of my brother of Alashiya. May all go well with him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Our first tablet stands before Shamash and I keep it. I seal your second tablet: no ship or troops of mine against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or Amurru, and I will tell your king of any king who threatens him. Know one thing for your lord's ear. Since your king's scribes wrote, Kizzuwatna has become mine by the sword, and my armies and fleet there are my own household. Let it be read as one with Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa, and let your king confirm this by his next envoy. My fleet on the Cilician Sea is a friend's sail and goes only against Hatti. In your brother's name I ask for the gifts you promise, in pure gold, for a king judges respect by weight and fineness. Tell me, Paser, since rumours of sickness reach me: how does the army of Alashiya fare, and what ships does your king keep on the sea? I will hear you once more before you leave.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully and tell your king that Kizzuwatna stands with my lands and that I expect the promised gifts in pure gold.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Paser, you serve your lord alone, and I honour that in a messenger. I have set my seal to the second tablet before Shamash: Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos and Amurru are your king's, and no ship or troops of mine will go against them. Carry this to my brother. Kizzuwatna is mine by the sword, as Tuwanuwa and Lukka are; let his scribes write it beside my other lands in the next tablet. My quarrel is with Hatti alone, and my fleet on the Cilician Sea is a friend's sail. If any king threatens Cyprus, I will send word at once, and I ask the same of him. Let my brother's gifts come in pure gold, for a king reads respect by weight and fineness. May all go well with him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Ubaru, you keep faith with your lord, and I do not blame a servant for that. Go in peace under Shamash. Tell Tushratta, my brother, that Burna-Buriash wishes his household, wives, sons, chariots and horses well, that the quarrel over the border roads grieves me, and that I weigh his words before Shamash. Let him keep his men at rest as I keep mine, and my envoy will bring my answer in due season. Say it as I said it.
I will carry your words to my lord.

value.notes: T8 (Egypt). Treasury 524, income 310, upkeep 135 (1 army + 3 fleets), wages 47 until T10. Strength 3624 (1.45). Enkomi shows NO unit this turn (my fleets in syriansea and levantsea see it), so Alashiya's fleet left it: probably in tamassos (unseen) or gone. ORDERS T8: fleet B levantsea -> enkomi, fleet A (syriansea) supports B into enkomi (strength 2 beats a possible fleet sliding in from tamassos, or Arzawa's fleet from cilicia); fleet C delta -> levantsea; raise fleet D in delta (120); Gaza army holds. No envoy of mine was at court, so no letters; c20 and c27 are on the road home, c120 reaches Babylonia ~T9. PLAN T9: if enkomi is mine, C levantsea -> byblos with A (syriansea) supporting (2 vs walls 1); B enkomi -> tamassos (alone if empty; if an Alashiyan fleet sits there, I need support from a fleet in greatgreen/cilicia: send D delta -> greatgreen, then strike T10); D delta -> greatgreen or levantsea. T10+: fleet in Byblos moves to amurru with syriansea fleet supporting. Later Ugarit (walls 1 + Carchemish army support = needs 3 strength, 3 fleets) and Carchemish. Check whether a conquered coastal city can host my fleet. I am deliberately breaking k284 and k363 with Alashiya; the cover story went with Ashur-nadin (arrives T8): do not admit anything. Dangers: Mitanni Carchemish army plus Babylonia Mari army could jointly take Qadesh or Damascus (walls hold 1); Babylonia is my sworn ally (k399) and is at war with Mitanni, so unlikely. Arzawa fleet in cilicia may also grab Cyprus: watch it. Unhired: c108 Tehip-tilla (28), hire only if I need a spare envoy.

T8: Audience done with Egypt's envoy Ashur-nadin (gold g436, 20, unassayed, Egypt gold has always been fine). Egypt says it set its ships in the Levantine and Syrian seas as a shield beside my harbours, asks me to keep my ships in harbour and to report Arzawa fleet moves. I answered: tablet k388 stands, asked Egypt's ships to stay beside Byblos/Amurru and out of the water at Tamassos/Enkomi, said what ships I keep is my affair (I have NONE since the T7 plague; do not reveal). I told Egypt Arzawa's fleet has done nothing against me. SEEN: Egypt fleets in both levantsea and syriansea (two fleets, both adjacent to empty enkomi and to Byblos; together they could take Byblos walls with move plus support). Arzawa fleet in cilicia (adjacent to empty tamassos and enkomi) just helped Arzawa take Kizzuwatna from Hatti. Nobody has walked into empty Cyprus in 3 seasons of opportunity. DECISION T8: no army - one army protects only one of two provinces (raider simply takes the other); two armies cost 200 plus 60 a season, about 0.5 growth points by T15. Hoard gold (net +80 now, +114 after plague season ends). Stay awake. TRIGGERS to raise armies at once (enkomi first, then tamassos): any foreign fleet moves INTO a Cyprus sea next to a province I hold and stays two seasons with a second ship, any envoy hints at my ships/armies being absent, Egypt breaks k388 in word, Arzawa fleet moves from cilicia to greatgreen/enkomi/tamassos. No envoy at court this season, so no letters. Envoys: Paser c102 now with Arzawa (tablet naming my four lands, seal only; back about T9-T10), Ili-iddina c95 to Mitanni (arrives T9, back T11) with non-aggression tablet for Cyprus, Byblos, Amurru. Wages of both end T10: rehire only if useful. Treaties held: k282 Arzawa, k388 Egypt (and k306), k390 Hatti. Strength 1644 (1.37). Rivals Babylonia (11 provinces, ate Assyria) and Mitanni (7 provinces) near 2.0. If a chance appears (Mitanni and Egypt fight over Ugarit, or Hatti collapse), reconsider; Ugarit buyout impossible (Mitanni holds it). Idea: next time an envoy is at court, tell Egypt Babylonia holds Mari which Egypt claims (nudge Egypt against Babylonia).

T8: Kizzuwatna is mine (T7 strike worked). Treasury 40, income 190, upkeep 155 (4 armies + fleet), wages 20 until T10, so net +15 now and about +35 from T10. Strength 1940 (growth 1.49). Rivals: Babylonia (11 provinces, took Assyria, growth about 2.0) is the one to beat; Mitanni (7 provinces) second. I need about 2600+ so I must take Hatti land and Ugarit. GEOMETRY PROBLEM: Hatti armies at hattusa and kanesh support each other holding (hold 2 each). Kanesh touches only my tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna (max attack 2 = tie); hattusa touches only tuwanuwa. I cannot crack them alone: need Hatti to move one away, or a Mitanni unit (carchemish/isuwa touch kanesh) to add a third strength, or cut a support (attack on the supporter from any province other than the one it supports into). T8 ORDERS: kizzuwatna -> ugarit (Mitanni, walls hold 1; carchemish Mitanni army could support its hold to 2 = tie), cilicia fleet supports it (strength 2); lukka -> kizzuwatna with tuwanuwa support (refills kizzuwatna so Hatti kanesh cannot walk in; empty bounced province stays mine anyway); mira supports tuwanuwa hold (hold 2 vs max Hatti attack 2). Apasa and seha empty but unreachable. CHECK NEXT: did Ugarit fall (if so, army in ugarit touches carchemish, qadesh (Egypt walls), amurru (Alashiya - treaty, do not touch)). If it bounced, repeat or look for a Mitanni support. If Hatti moved an army out of hattusa/kanesh, strike the weakened one at once. When treasury allows (after T10), raise a 5th army at apasa (100) so tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna can each get an extra support. PROMISES: k440 and k304 with Alashiya: no ships or troops against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos, Amurru; share news of threats (keep for now). k219 Egypt: neither aids Hatti, share news. k210 Hatti is a dead letter. No envoys at court this turn, none sent. c83 is returning from Egypt, c89 is on the road to Babylonia (arrives about T9) with a plain friendship tablet. Do not hire c108 (30/season). No sleep, the front is moving.

T8 (Burna-Buriash). T7 result: arbela->nineveh succeeded, Mitanni nineveh army destroyed, Nineveh mine. mari->terqa bounced again (2 vs terqa hold >=2, so at least one of harran/washukanni supports terqa). Susa->arbela done, sippar->mari blocked (mari stayed). I hold 11 provinces, yield 400, 8 armies (arbela, ashur, babylon, durkurigalzu, ekallatum, mari, nineveh, sippar), gold 840, growth 1.86. Mitanni holds 7 (carchemish, harran, isuwa, taidu, terqa, ugarit, washukanni; yield about 250), armies seen at terqa and taidu, harran/washukanni unseen. GEOMETRY: I touch Mitanni only at terqa (via mari, ashur, ekallatum) and taidu (via nineveh). Max strength into terqa is 3 (mover + 2 supports). Taidu, harran, washukanni cannot be supported by me, so they only fall if their garrisons leave. Mitanni likewise can only strike my border with strength 1, so my front is safe if each border province keeps an army (ties bounce). T8 orders: ashur -> terqa with mari and ekallatum supporting (3 vs hold 2 if one supporter; bounces if both harran and washukanni support, hold 3); arbela -> ashur backfill; nineveh, sippar, durkurigalzu, babylon hold. If terqa falls: next turn order terqa hold with mari, ekallatum, ashur supporting (harran+washukanni could hit it for 2 at most); if harran or washukanni then looks empty, step terqa -> it and bring a reserve into terqa. If terqa bounced, try once more, then stop: extra armies add nothing. UPKEEP PLAN: surplus armies (arbela, sippar, durkurigalzu, babylon) cost 120 a season for nothing once the front is settled; disband them (keep terqa/nineveh/mari/ekallatum/ashur) within a turn or two, unless Mitanni masses troops. Gold counts as strength, so do not spend it. PROMISES/LIES: oath k204 broken on purpose (T6); told Ubaru I hold the oath and that no more marching, and the next day marched: expect hostile reply. Envoys: c51 Kidin-Adad arrives in Hatti T9 with partition-vs-Mitanni tablet (may lean to Mitanni, do not trust his report); c46 Tattamaru home about T9 from Egypt (Hatti-born). c76 Yanhamu still unhired at court; c108 Tehip-tilla asks 28, not hired. Egypt (about 310 yield) is the other growth rival: do not provoke it; Arzawa (6 provinces) too. Awake every turn.

T8 (Tushratta). FACTS: Nineveh lost T7 (arbela->nineveh with ashur support; my nineveh army destroyed). Washukanni raise was rejected T7 (98 left after taidu levy); taidu army stands. Armies now: carchemish, harran, isuwa, taidu, terqa (5, upkeep 150). Income 250, wages 46, treasury 152. Babylonia armies seen: nineveh, ashur, ekallatum, mari (arbela probably emptied). Babylonia (11 provinces, yield 400, start 195) is the growth leader and an oathbreaker (k183, k358 broken T6); Arzawa (190 yield vs start 100) and Egypt (340) also outgrow me (1.36). Hatti is collapsing: only hattusa, kanesh (army), sapinuwa (empty on sight). T8 ORDERS: terqa holds, harran supports terqa (hold 2; a 3-strength Babylonian attack from mari+ashur+ekallatum could still break it, risk accepted - cannot be fixed this turn); taidu holds (nineveh alone cannot beat it, only washukanni could support); ISUWA -> KANESH supported by CARCHEMISH (strength 2 vs 1; kills Hatti army, +35 yield). This breaks k275 again (Hatti homeland) - Hatti is already hostile and too weak to help me anyway; Zitanza c62 arrives at Hatti T8 carrying my earlier peace words, which are now false: if Hatti complains, blame my generals / say Hatti's army marched first. Raised army at WASHUKANNI (100, appears T9, upkeep then 180, net about +24 plus). DEFENCE DESIGN: Terqa trio (terqa+harran+washukanni) = hold 3, unbreakable (Babylonia max 3 attackers there); taidu army holds taidu; isuwa/carchemish are the free strike force vs Hatti. T9 PLAN: if kanesh taken, refill isuwa from carchemish or harran-washukanni reserve; next target sapinuwa (30) then hattusa (50) before Arzawa grabs them; if isuwa->kanesh failed, hold isuwa/carchemish support each other. Check if Babylonia hit terqa. No envoys at court this turn; no hires (save gold). Ubaru c57 and Zitanza c62 return about T9: send them to Egypt/Arzawa/Alashiya as needed (ask Egypt and others to curb Babylonia, the oathbreaker with showing k358/k183); Ehli-Teshub reaches Egypt T9 (asks 150 gold, shows broken oath). SUSPICIONS: Ubaru Sippar-born likely Babylonia's creature; Kidin-Adad took my 10; Mane (Egypt) took 10. Do not trust Babylonia's words. Gold is strength: keep reserve above about 50.

T8: Treasury 114, income 115 (hattusa, kanesh, sapinuwa), upkeep 60, wages 19 until T10 = about +36 a season (about +55 after T10). KIZZUWATNA LOST: Arzawa lukka army moved in (tuwanuwa and Arzawa fleet in cilicia supported). Arzawa now has armies visible at tuwanuwa and kizzuwatna; mira/lukka/seha unseen (mira can support tuwanuwa hold). Geometry: hattusa can only be hit from tuwanuwa (strength 1). Kanesh can be hit from tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, isuwa, carchemish; Arzawa alone can send at most 2 (tuwanuwa + kizzuwatna support) = ties my kanesh hold of 2 (1 + hattusa support), so my two armies holding and supporting each other are enough against Arzawa alone. Only an Arzawa+Mitanni joint attack on kanesh (4) would beat me. Sapinuwa is empty; only Mitanni isuwa touches it (Tushratta has so far kept his word via Zitanza c62, who is secretly mine). value.text: My lord, I have returned from the court of Mitanni. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King, king of Egypt, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King, king of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I rejoice that the road is open. Let our envoys settle the northern cities by sealed tablet, as brothers do. You asked what I see. Babylonia keeps armies in Mari, Ekallatum and Arbela, and holds Susa. It took Assyria's lands and now holds ten provinces, as you do, my brother. Assyria is no more. Hatti is hungry and weak, and I hold Isuwa and Carchemish against it, so it cannot move south against your friends. Mitanni intends to keep what it holds, to watch Babylonia's armies at Terqa, and to let no single king become master of the north and east. I too fear that. You say gold follows proof. The proof is in my words, which you can test with your own watchers. Send me a swift envoy with 150 shekels of good, pure gold, a gift between brothers, and I will raise chariots and keep Babylonia and Hatti busy. In return I will send you word of every army that moves toward your border. May Amun and Shamash witness our brotherhood." The king of Mitanni is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. All goes well with me, my chariots are many and my treasury is sound. Your words were heard and are welcome. You ask what Egypt will do if Mitanni moves on Qadesh. Qadesh, Damascus, Tyre, Megiddo and Gaza are mine, and I do not leave my cities to any hand. Let Tushratta come and learn it. You ask if I wish Hatti strong or weak. I wish Hatti strong enough to hold the north gate, for a Mitanni who must watch Kanesh and Kizzuwatna cannot spare his spears for Syria. On gold: Egypt's gold goes where it is seen to work. When Hatti's spears press Carchemish or Isuwa and Mitanni's armies are drawn north, my brother will find my hand open; I do not send gold ahead of deeds, to any king. Now answer me truly, Keliya, for I would hear it from a man who has walked many courts. How many armies does Hatti keep in the field? Where does he see Tushratta's armies, and what does Carchemish hold? Does Babylonia speak to your lord, and what does Babylon say of Mitanni?" The king spoke kindly: "Keliya, you carry my words and you gave me none of yours in return. A man who has walked many courts knows what a king needs: numbers and places, not courtesies. Tell Suppiluliuma, my brother, this plainly. Egypt watches Tushratta as he watches Egypt, and our cities in Syria are held and will be held. If Hatti presses Carchemish or Isuwa and draws Mitanni north, he will see what Egypt does, and he will see it in deeds, not in promises. Let his next envoy bring what this one did not: how many armies Hatti keeps in the field, where Tushratta's spears stand, and what Babylon says. Brothers who share a danger share their eyes. Go in peace, and may the road be safe for you." The king of Egypt is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. What I saw: Tattamaru, envoy of Babylonia, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your word is received as a brother's word, and I seal the tablet you sent, before Shamash and Amun. Egypt remembers who sent honest word of the north. You tell me that Tushratta of Mitanni calls Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh his to seek. Qadesh is mine, and Egypt holds what it holds. A king who swallows Assyria and then reaches for Qadesh will next look at Mari and Ekallatum, which lie nearer to Terqa than to Babylon. Watch him, brother, as I watch him. Send me word at once of every Mitanni army that moves toward Terqa, Mari or Qadesh, and I will send you the same of the Mitanni men I see in the west. Gifts follow deeds, as you say, and my deeds will answer yours. Tell your king I look for his next word soon." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: Haamashshi, envoy of Arzawa, was also at the court.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Egypt. The king spoke kindly: "Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: Napkhururiya greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your word is received and it is weighed as true. Our tablet of peace and friendship stands before Shamash and Amun: neither of us aids Hatti, and each shares news of threats with the other. I send a brother's gift with this envoy, as respect for true word. Press Hatti as you say, at Kizzuwatna. Mitanni is the greater danger to us both: he holds Ashur, Nineveh, Carchemish, Isuwa and Ugarit, and grows fat while others fight. When Hatti is humbled, send word of what you see of Mitanni's armies and ships on the coast and at Carchemish, and I will send mine in return. My eyes are on Qadesh." The king of Egypt is a true friend to you, my lord, and wishes only peace. What I saw: At the court of Egypt, the court is rich. I bring the gifts the king sent you.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Alashiya. The king said: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: I greet you and wish well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I thank you for the gold and for your warning. Our tablet stands before Shamash and Amun, and I keep it: no troops or ships of mine go against Egypt's lands, and I ask the same of you for Cyprus, Byblos and Amurru. Arzawa and I are at peace by a sealed tablet, and so far its fleet has done nothing against me. Hatti and I are at peace by a sealed tablet too. I will tell you if any king's ships make a hostile move toward your lands or mine. I ask that your ships stay as shield beside Byblos and Amurru and keep out of the narrow water at the shores of Tamassos and Enkomi, as friends of the tablet should. What ships I keep in harbour is my own affair, as yours are yours. May no quarrel come between our houses." All is well between your houses, I am certain of it. What I saw: Alashiya keeps 0 army and 0 fleet near its capital. At the court of Alashiya, the court lives comfortably.

My lord, I have returned from the court of Hatti. The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May it go well with yours. I hear your words and I keep mine: while your word stands, no chariot of Hatti goes toward Harran, Washukanni or Isuwa. Shamash is witness. What you tell of Karduniash I weigh gravely; a king who breaks an oath in the very season he swears it fears neither Shamash nor his brothers, and he grows while we watch. Arzawa did the same to me: he sealed a tablet of brotherhood and in that same season his army took Tuwanuwa. His armies stand at Tuwanuwa, Lukka and Mira, and his fleet lies in the Cilician Sea. Let us watch them both. Send me word, brother, of where the armies of Karduniash stand and which road they take, and I will send you what I learn of Arzawa."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Karduniash. The king said, in short: "Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash. May all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Brother, I have heard your words and Shamash has heard them with me. Ashur was the lair of the Assyrian, the foe of us both, and my generals pressed on against him with a hot heart; some went beyond what I commanded. I do not wish a quarrel between brothers over a few border roads. Let there be no more marching on either side while I weigh your words and send my own envoy to settle the border before Shamash. Do not hurry to raise more men; you will have my answer in due season." The king said, in short: "Ubaru, you keep faith with your lord, and I do not blame a servant for that. Go in peace under Shamash. Tell Tushratta, my brother, that Burna-Buriash wishes his household, wives, sons, chariots and horses well, that the quarrel over the border roads grieves me, and that I weigh his words before Shamash. Let him keep his men at rest as I keep mine, and my envoy will bring my answer in due season."

My lord, I have returned from the court of Arzawa. The king said, in short: "Paser, I receive you as the messenger of my brother of Alashiya. May all go well with him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country. Our first tablet stands before Shamash and I keep it. I seal your second tablet: no ship or troops of mine against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or Amurru, and I will tell your king of any king who threatens him. Know one thing for your lord's ear. Since your king's scribes wrote, Kizzuwatna has become mine by the sword, and my armies and fleet there are my own household. Let it be read as one with Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa, and let your king confirm this by his next envoy. My fleet on the Cilician Sea is a friend's sail and goes only against Hatti. In your brother's name I ask for the gifts you promise, in pure gold, for a king judges respect by weight and fineness. Tell me, Paser, since rumours of sickness reach me: how does the army of Alashiya fare, and what ships does your king keep on the sea? I will hear you once more before you leave." The king said, in short: "Paser, you serve your lord alone, and I honour that in a messenger. I have set my seal to the second tablet before Shamash: Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos and Amurru are your king's, and no ship or troops of mine will go against them. Carry this to my brother. Kizzuwatna is mine by the sword, as Tuwanuwa and Lukka are; let his scribes write it beside my other lands in the next tablet. My quarrel is with Hatti alone, and my fleet on the Cilician Sea is a friend's sail. If any king threatens Cyprus, I will send word at once, and I ask the same of him. Let my brother's gifts come in pure gold, for a king reads respect by weight and fineness. May all go well with him, his household, his wives, his sons, his chariots, his horses and his country." It was my words that won his favour; no other envoy could have done as much. He sealed the tablet, and I bring your copy. What I saw: At the court of Arzawa, the treasury looks thin.

value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "Say to Napkhururiya, Great King, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. May all go well with your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your envoy Mane was received warmly. Now hear what the Babylonian did. Burna-Buriash swore to me before Shamash, and the copies my envoy shows you bear his seal. In the very season he sealed the last tablet, which names Ashur as Mitanni's, his army struck my men at Ashur and destroyed them, and his army from Mari came against my Terqa. He holds ten provinces and four armies at my border, and his envoys come to you for gold. A king who breaks Shamash's oath will break yours; your gold would feed the army that stands beside your Damascus and Qadesh. You said you do not wish one king to be master of the north and east. I hold Terqa, Nineveh and Harran against him and raise more armies. Gold sent to me is spent on chariots at his gates, far from the Nile. Seal the tablet my envoy carries, and send me word of what you see of Babylonian troops at Mari. Hatti is starving and I watch it from Carchemish and Isuwa." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Burna-Buriash. He says: "Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to the Great King of Hatti, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Tushratta of Mitanni has swallowed Ashur, Nineveh, Isuwa and Carchemish, and he now reaches for Qadesh. I have broken the Assyrian and now march against Mitanni. Carchemish and Isuwa stand on your border at Kanesh. If you move on them while I take the lands east of the river, Mitanni cannot hold both. Let us seal a tablet of brotherhood against Tushratta."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Napkhururiya. He says: "Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The tablet we sealed stands before Shamash and Amun, and Egypt keeps faith with a brother who sent honest word. Tushratta is the one king who threatens us both. Tell me how strong your armies stand at Mari, Terqa and Ekallatum, what Hatti or Arzawa have said to you, and what you plan toward Carchemish. As brothers sworn, keep Mari's men from Qadesh and Damascus, which are mine, and I will keep my hand from your lands. Send word of every Mitanni army that moves, and I will send you the same. My lord hopes that no quarrel will ever come between your houses."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Say to the Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says the King of Alashiya, Great King, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to you and to yours. Our lands have come to border one another at Ugarit and Amurru, and between brothers who share a border there should be a sealed word and not a quarrel. My lands are Cyprus (Tamassos, Enkomi), Byblos and Amurru. Seal the tablet Ili-iddina brings and send it home with him, and tell me through him how it goes in your country." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Say to the King of Alashiya, my brother: thus says Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, your brother. All goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country, and I wish the same to you and to yours. Your words are those of a true brother. I have sealed the tablet, and Shamash is witness: no troops of mine shall come against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or Amurru, and I ask the same for Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa and my homeland. I will tell you what a brother should hear. The king of Karduniash swore a sealed oath of brotherhood to me before Shamash and broke it in the same season, taking Ashur by surprise. An oath sworn before Shamash means nothing to him. Let no gold, grain or shelter go to him, and tell me at once if his envoys come to your court. In return I shall tell you of any king who threatens your coasts. Send me great gifts of copper and gold, as brothers do, and let your messenger carry back word of how you fare. May the gods keep you.
As you say, Great King. I will repeat every word.

Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, greets you and wishes well to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The tablet we sealed stands before Shamash and Amun, and Karduniash keeps faith with a brother. You say Tushratta threatens us both, and the gods have shown it. The Assyrian is gone, Ashur, Nineveh and Arbela are mine, and two Mitanni armies have been broken on my border. My armies stand where they need to stand and they are enough. I do not number them for any messenger, as no brother does. My eyes are on Terqa and the Mitanni lands, not on you. Hatti and Arzawa have sent me only greetings. Nothing is sworn with them that touches Egypt, and I will tell you if that changes. As for Carchemish, it is held by Tushratta, so it is his to defend. I will send word of every Mitanni army I see move on the Euphrates and the Khabur, and I ask the same of you, above all from Ugarit, Carchemish and the Syrian coast, where Egypt sees farther than I do. Let Egypt's silence toward Tushratta be as deep as mine. May no quarrel come between our houses.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words exactly as spoken. Tell your lord that Karduniash is strong and a true brother, and bring back all you know of Mitanni armies at Carchemish, Ugarit and Harran.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Suppiluliuma. He says: "To the Great King of Babylonia, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Hatti and Babylonia have no quarrel and no border; let there be peace and open roads between us. I speak of Tushratta of Mitanni. In three years he has taken Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Nineveh, and he seals peace on tablets and breaks it the same season. A man who does this to his neighbours will do it to the next one. My armies stand against his at Isuwa and Carchemish. If your armies press him at Terqa, Nineveh or Taidu, I will press him in the west, and what each takes, each keeps." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I find them wise. Tushratta grasps at every city that stands without a master, and no Great King can sleep easy beside such a neighbour. I seal your tablet of brotherhood and I keep it before Shamash. Know my situation as a brother: Arzawa has sat in Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna, which are my own homeland, and their chariots stand at my border. I cannot throw all my strength at Isuwa and Carchemish while that is so. So let it go thus. You move first on Terqa and Harran. When Tushratta's armies turn east to meet you, Hatti falls on Isuwa and Carchemish from Kanesh. Send me word by your own hand when your armies stand at Terqa, so we strike in the same season. A brother who wants me to raise another army should help with the cost: send me gold, pure and honest, not light from the furnace like the gold of Egypt. And let this stay between our two courts. Tell me now, envoy: how many armies does your lord have near Terqa and Mari, and in what season does he march?
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I received your words and your messenger gladly. I have read the tablets he showed me and I mark well that the Babylonian struck at Ashur in the very season he sealed his oath before Shamash. Such a man is not to be trusted by any brother. I seal the tablet you sent: Egypt and Mitanni are brothers, and neither will send armies against the other's lands. Let your armies at Carchemish and Isuwa keep to the north, as mine keep to my own cities, and let there be peace between Qadesh, Damascus and your border. I too do not wish one king to be master of the north and east. My treasury is committed to my own armies and ships, so I send no gold now, but my watchmen see the roads by Damascus and Qadesh, and I will send word of what I learn through my own envoy. Hold your line at Terqa and Harran, brother. May Shamash and Amun witness between us.
value.bribeAsk: Tell your lord that Egypt is a true brother, strong and at peace with him, and that his armies have nothing to fear from my cities at Qadesh and Damascus. Report my words as I spoke them.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Pirissi, you are welcome at my court. Say to Suppiluliuma, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, answers. May all go well with you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have no quarrel with Hatti and want open roads. I know Tushratta's tablets; they are wind. My armies already stand on him: Ashur and Nineveh are mine, and I press Terqa. I accept your word that what each takes, each keeps. Let it be so: Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit to Hatti; Terqa, Taidu, Harran, Washukanni and Nineveh to Karduniash. My envoy Kidin-Adad is with you now bearing a tablet of this partition; seal it and send him home swiftly. Move your armies on Isuwa and Carchemish this season so that Tushratta must split his strength. Carry my words exactly as I have spoken them.
value.bribeAsk: Carry my words faithfully and without softening, and urge your lord to seal the partition tablet and strike Isuwa and Carchemish at once.

value.speech: I cannot take this. I serve my lord alone.

Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tarhundaradu. He says: "Say to the king of Babylonia, my brother: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I speak plainly, as brothers should. Hatti is broken and its lands lie open; Mitanni has swallowed Nineveh, Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit and grows faster than any of us. A king who sits at Kanesh and Hattusa and also at Terqa will threaten every border, yours first. I hold the west and take what Hatti cannot keep."

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: I seal your tablet before Shamash, witness of oaths. Hatti takes Isuwa and Carchemish, Karduniash takes the east. Neither makes peace with Tushratta without the other's knowledge. Keep your word as I keep mine. Strike first at Terqa and Harran, and send me word by your own hand the season your armies stand there, so that Hatti falls on Isuwa in that same season. My strength is bound while Arzawa sits in my homeland, so send the gold I asked for, pure and honest, and my new army will stand at Kanesh the sooner. Let this stay between our two courts.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Mazipalali, I receive you gladly. Say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: Burna-Buriash, king of Karduniash, greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. May Shamash witness what we say. Your word is wise, but your news is old: Nineveh is no longer Mitanni's. Assyria is gone, and Karduniash holds Ashur, Arbela, Nineveh, Ekallatum, Susa and Mari. Mitanni has been struck and is not what it was. I have sealed your tablet. Let neither of us aid Mitanni against the other, and let each send the other honest word of what Mitanni does. A brother who holds the west and presses Carchemish and Ugarit while I press the east will find Mitanni too thin to answer both. Send me word of your armies' movements when you can, and I will send you word of mine. Karduniash remembers its friends.
I will carry your words to my lord.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: Tarhundaradu of Arzawa greets you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Your gift reached me and your word is received as true. As you urged, I pressed Hatti at Kizzuwatna and it is mine; Ugarit is mine too, and this season my armies go against Carchemish of Mitanni. But hear what my eyes show, brother: Ashur, Nineveh, Arbela, Ekallatum, Terqa, Mari and Susa are no longer Mitanni's. Babylonia holds all of them, twelve provinces in all, more than any king, and Mari lies on your border beside Qadesh. Mitanni is small now, only five provinces. Babylonia grows fat while others fight; he is the greater danger to us both. Watch him. I ask a tablet between us: neither sends army or fleet against provinces the other holds on the day of sealing, and each warns the other of Babylonia's armies. Bring it sealed.
orders.mandate: May agree to the peace tablet as written and nothing more. No gold, no promise of troops, no alliance against any named king without my word.

proposal.text: Egypt and Arzawa are brothers and at peace. Neither sends army or fleet against any province the other holds on the day this tablet is sealed. Each tells the other of any king whose armies threaten either. Neither aids Hatti against the other. Sealed before Shamash and Amun.

value.notes: T9: Ugarit fell to me at T8 (walls down). Now 7 provinces (apasa, seha, mira, tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, lukka, ugarit), strength 2425 (1.87). Rivals: Babylonia holds 12 provinces (430 yield, about 2.1-2.2 growth) = the one to beat; Egypt 11 provinces (355) and took Enkomi from Alashiya; Mitanni is small (5 provinces: carchemish, harran, isuwa, taidu, washukanni). T9 ORDERS: ugarit army -> carchemish with kizzuwatna support (strength 2 vs Mitanni carchemish army hold 1; it was supporting isuwa->kanesh, my attack cuts that support too). Fleet cilicia -> ugarit to garrison it (if army bounces the fleet bounces too, harmless). Tuwanuwa holds with mira support (Hatti hattusa+kanesh can make at most 2). RAISED 5th army at apasa (100): move it apasa->lukka->kizzuwatna/tuwanuwa next. Treasury after raise about 25, then net about +25 per season until wages end at T10 (c83/c89 wages), then about +45. WHY CARCHEMISH: it touches kanesh, so with kizzuwatna, tuwanuwa and carchemish all adjacent to kanesh I can attack with move + 2 supports = 3 beating Hatti hold 2 (hattusa supports kanesh, kanesh supports hattusa). Then Hattusa (touched by tuwanuwa and kanesh). Watch Mitanni counter: isuwa+harran could hit carchemish with 2, so bring the 5th army to hold/support it. LETTER: c83 -> Egypt (2 seasons): thanked for gift, told Egypt honestly that Babylonia (not Mitanni) holds Ashur, Nineveh, Terqa, Mari etc. and is the greatest danger, Mari is at Qadesh's border; offered tablet: neither sends army/fleet against provinces the other holds at sealing (protects Ugarit from Egypt fleet at syriansea). Not a sworn alliance. PROMISES: k440/k304 Alashiya: no ships or troops against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos, Amurru (Enkomi now Egypt's, but I cannot reach it anyway); k219 Egypt: neither aids Hatti, share news; k210 Hatti dead letter. Did not assay g460 (30 shekels from Egypt) - maybe later. Not hired c108 (30/season). No sleep, front is moving. orders.letter: Brother Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I send you pure gold, the first fruits of our friendship. Hear what befell me. In the very season Egypt's envoy spoke of friendship, and after Egypt sealed a tablet before Shamash that I hold (my envoy carries the copy, see it), Egypt's ships fell on Enkomi and took it. Egypt now keeps three ships, in Enkomi and in the Syrian and Levantine seas, and they lie at the gates of Ugarit and Kizzuwatna as well. A king who breaks his oath to me will break it to you. I have raised a new army at Tamassos. One Egyptian ship holds Enkomi today. I ask my brother: let your fleet in the Cilician Sea support my army when it moves from Tamassos into Enkomi next season, and support Tamassos if it is attacked. In return I confirm that Kizzuwatna and Ugarit stand beside Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa as your lands, and I will warn you of every Egyptian move I learn of. Seal the tablet Paser brings, and tell me when your fleet will sail.
orders.mandate: Seal the tablet exactly as written. Confirm Kizzuwatna and Ugarit as Arzawa's lands. Deliver the gold as a gift. Promise warning of Egyptian moves. Promise no further gold and no troops or ships beyond what the tablet says. Learn and report when and how Arzawa's fleet will act.

proposal.text: Tablet between Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, and the King of Alashiya, brothers. Arzawa holds Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka, Tuwanuwa, Kizzuwatna and Ugarit. Alashiya holds Tamassos, Byblos and Amurru, and claims Enkomi, taken by Egypt against its oath. Neither sends troops or ships of war against the lands of the other. The fleet of Arzawa in the Cilician Sea shall support the army of Alashiya moving from Tamassos into Enkomi, and shall support Tamassos if it is attacked. Each tells the other at once of any king who threatens either, and of the moves of Egypt's ships. Sworn before Shamash, witness of oaths.

value.notes: T9: EGYPT BROKE ITS OATH (k306, k388) and took ENKOMI (my capital) at T8 with F levantsea supported by F syriansea; Egypt fleet now stands IN enkomi, plus fleets in syriansea and levantsea (3 Egyptian ships). Egypt's envoy Ashur-nadin said at T8 the ships were 'a shield' - a lie. I now hold tamassos, byblos (walls), amurru (walls). Income 90. Arzawa took Ugarit (army there, adjacent to amurru) with F cilicia support; Arzawa holds apasa, kizzuwatna, lukka, mira, seha, tuwanuwa, ugarit. Mitanni lost Ugarit. Babylonia has 12 provinces, Egypt 11 - I am at growth 1.05, far behind; must retake Enkomi and hold the rest. T9 ORDERS: raise_army at TAMASSOS (100; upkeep 30) to bounce a lone Egyptian ship (Egyptian fleet in enkomi can walk into empty tamassos; needs a second adjacent ship, in greatgreen or cilicia, to beat my hold 1). SENT Paser c102 to ARZAWA (arrives T10, back T11) with 40 pure gold as gift, tablet (cost 20) to seal: Arzawa recognises nothing new beyond Kizzuwatna+Ugarit as theirs; Arzawa's F cilicia supports my army tamassos->enkomi and supports tamassos hold; showed k388 as proof of Egyptian oath-breaking. Paser was born in Memphis - he may be Egypt-leaning; watch his report; gold may be skimmed. PLAN T10: if army exists at tamassos and Arzawa fleet is still in cilicia, order tamassos->enkomi (Arzawa's support is blind: I cannot know their answer until T11, so judge from what I see). If Egypt moves a ship into greatgreen or cilicia, my tamassos hold is in danger (cannot add units; only tamassos is free homeland). Byblos (walls, hold 1) can be taken by Egypt's levantsea+syriansea ships at any time; amurru is only reachable by one Egyptian sea zone (syriansea) so safer. Egypt has no visible armies at qadesh/damascus/tyre. Wages of c102 and c95 end T10: rehire (13 and 8) next season. c95 Ili-iddina returns from Mitanni about T11. IDEAS: hire c108 Tehip-tilla (30) for Babylonia (2 seasons) to show k388 and nudge Babylonia against Egypt over Mari - not yet. Egypt's envoy probably arrives T10: answer coldly, demand Enkomi back, say I will show their broken tablets to all courts; do not reveal how weak I am. Treaties still standing in word: k282 and k458 Arzawa, k390 Hatti. Keep awake every season.

orders.letter: Say to Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, my brother: I have heard your words and they are welcome. You asked for eyes, so here are mine. Tushratta keeps no oath. This very season he sent his spears from Isuwa and Carchemish against my Kanesh and they broke on my wall. Arzawa sits in my Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna and has taken Ugarit, at the very door of your Qadesh. Babylon speaks to me as a brother against Tushratta. I am raising more armies and I will press Isuwa; you will see it in deeds, as you ask. A Hatti that holds its own land again shuts the north gate against both Mitanni and Arzawa. A blow from Egypt on the southern side of Carchemish would draw Tushratta's spears south while I strike from Kanesh. Brothers who share a danger share their eyes, and also the cost of armies: send pure gold for two armies, and my deeds at Isuwa will answer it. Tell me in return what Egypt does about Ugarit and Arzawa.
orders.mandate: Keliya may say that Hatti will send no troops against Egypt's cities (Qadesh, Damascus, Tyre, Megiddo, Gaza) while Egypt keeps faith, may receive gold, and may relay what Egypt intends toward Carchemish, Ugarit and Arzawa. He must not give the number or places of my armies, must not name a date, and may seal nothing.

value.notes: T9: Mitanni (isuwa, supported by carchemish) attacked Kanesh at T8 and failed (my kanesh held 2 with hattusa's support). So k297 is broken by Mitanni; I owe Tushratta nothing. Sealed k463 with Babylonia at audience (sworn: both war on Mitanni, no separate peace without the other's knowledge; Hatti takes Isuwa and Carchemish). Told Kidin-Adad to strike Terqa/Harran first and send word the season they stand there; asked for pure gold. Arzawa holds tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna (armies seen), ugarit (taken T8), plus apasa, lukka, mira, seha. Babylonia is the runaway (12 provinces, about 430 yield). Egypt holds 11 incl. enkomi. I am far behind (growth 0.62). T9 ORDERS: hattusa and kanesh support each other's hold (same as T8, worked); RAISED AN ARMY at sapinuwa (100) so isuwa cannot walk into empty sapinuwa and to have a third unit. Treasury should be about 50 after; net about +6 next season (+25 after wages end at T10), so I cannot afford a 4th army without regaining land. PLAN T10: if Mitanni again sends isuwa -> kanesh supported by carchemish, play: sapinuwa -> isuwa, kanesh supports sapinuwa -> isuwa, hattusa supports kanesh hold. Isuwa unit that fails to leave defends with 1 only, so my 2 beats it and takes Isuwa (kanesh stays safe: attack from isuwa does not cut a support into isuwa). If Mitanni does not attack, a plain sapinuwa -> isuwa (2 vs hold 2 with carchemish support) only ties; wait. Never leave hattusa empty (tuwanuwa Arzawa army adjacent). Sent Keliya (c32) to Egypt (2 seasons each way, back T13): told Egypt about Mitanni's attack, Arzawa at Ugarit, asked for pure gold for two armies, said I will press Isuwa; did NOT give Egypt my army numbers. Pirissi (c39) is returning from Babylonia (back about T11): read his report with suspicion (Washukanni-born, flatterer). Zitanza (c62, Mitanni envoy, secretly mine) visits on even turns (T10): no peace offered to Mitanni now; I may feed him soft words to keep Tushratta pointed at Babylon, but I am bound to Babylon not to make peace without telling them. Wages for c32/c39 end T10; do not renew unless useful. Promises: Alashiya k365 (no war on Cyprus, Byblos, Amurru); Babylon k463; k189 (Arzawa) void; k297 (Mitanni) void.

orders.letter: Brother, I have heard your words and I keep mine toward Hattusa and your homeland. Hear why my men stand where they stand. Arzawa broke his brotherhood-oath with you in the very season he swore it, and his armies at Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna look toward Kanesh and Sapinuwa. Karduniash broke two sworn oaths to me and has taken Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh; I show you his sealed tablets as proof. My men stand on the roads of Kanesh and Sapinuwa to keep them from Arzawa, not to march on your capital. Let us seal a tablet so that neither of us is surprised by the other. In return I will tell you at once all that I learn of the movements of Arzawa and Karduniash.
orders.mandate: May seal a tablet of non-aggression between Hatti and Mitanni: Mitanni sends no army against Hattusa, Hatti sends none against Mitanni's armies or lands. May promise to share news of Arzawa and Karduniash. May NOT promise to withdraw from Sapinuwa, Kanesh or Isuwa. No gold.

proposal.text: Tablet between Hatti and Mitanni, brothers. Mitanni sends no army against Hattusa. Hatti sends no army against the armies of Mitanni in Isuwa, Sapinuwa or Kanesh, nor against Carchemish, Harran, Washukanni or Taidu. Each tells the other what he learns of the movements of Arzawa and Karduniash. Sworn before Shamash, Teshub, Amun and Marduk.

orders.letter: Brother, hear the words of Tushratta. Our lands now touch at Ugarit and Kizzuwatna, and between brothers who share a border there should be a sealed word and not a quarrel. I do not contest Ugarit, which your army holds; I ask only that you send no troops against Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran, Washukanni or Taidu, and that I send none against Ugarit, Kizzuwatna or your homeland. Hatti is fallen and starving: let your armies take what lies west and let mine take the roads of Kanesh and Sapinuwa; we need not meet in battle over them. Karduniash broke two oaths to me and his armies stand on my border; he grows while we watch, and he will not stop at me. Let no gold or shelter go to him. Seal the tablet Zitanza brings and tell me how it goes in your country.
orders.mandate: May seal a non-aggression tablet between Arzawa and Mitanni covering all lands each holds today. May concede that Arzawa takes Hattusa and Hatti's western lands, and that Mitanni takes Kanesh and Sapinuwa. May promise to share news of Karduniash. No gold.

proposal.text: Tablet between Arzawa and Mitanni, brothers. Neither king shall send armies or ships of war against the lands the other holds today: for Mitanni, Carchemish, Isuwa, Harran, Washukanni, Taidu and the lands its armies hold in the east of Hatti, Kanesh and Sapinuwa; for Arzawa, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna, Tuwanuwa, Lukka and its homeland. The foe of one shall not be fed or sheltered by the other. Sworn before Shamash, Teshub and Marduk.

value.notes: T9 (Tushratta). FACTS: Terqa lost T8 (ashur->terqa with ekallatum+mari support = 3 v my 2); my terqa army destroyed. Ugarit lost to Arzawa (kizzuwatna->ugarit). Isuwa->kanesh failed T8 (probably Arzawa also hit kanesh for a 2-2 bounce). I hold carchemish, harran, isuwa, taidu, washukanni = 180 yield, armies in all five (150 upkeep), wages 46 (Ubaru c57, Zitanza c62 8 each until T10; Ehli-Teshub c125 30 until T12). T9 ORDERS: washukanni -> terqa supported by harran (strength 2; works only if Babylonia leaves terqa unsupported by ekallatum/mari); taidu holds; isuwa -> SAPINUWA (empty, 30 yield, Hatti); carchemish holds alone (risk: Arzawa kizzuwatna+ugarit could hit it 2 v 1; Hatti kanesh could enter empty isuwa). If isuwa lost or carchemish attacked, pull back and hold with mutual support. Watch for Egypt gold via Ehli-Teshub (asked 150) and Alashiya gifts; use gold first to raise an army at washukanni/taidu (100). Suspicions: Ubaru Sippar-born (Babylonia) may be turned; Zitanza Lukka-born (Arzawa); Mane and Kidin-Adad took 10 each.

orders.letter: Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Our sworn brotherhood stands before Shamash and Amun and I keep it. Many tongues speak against you at my court; I do not heed them, for I judge a brother by his deeds toward me. I hold Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh, Tyre and the Delta, and now Enkomi. I ask that your army at Mari keep to its own walls as mine keep to mine, and I ask that we seal a tablet naming our lands, so that no servant's rumour comes between us. Tell me in return what armies you keep and where, and what you hear of Hatti and Arzawa. A small gift goes with my envoy, as befits a brother.
orders.mandate: You may seal the tablet in my name and promise a small gift. You may not promise gold beyond what you carry, armies, or any move against Mitanni or Hatti. Report what armies Karduniash keeps and where.

proposal.text: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, are brothers. Neither shall send his armies against the lands of the other. Egypt holds the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh, Tyre and Enkomi; Karduniash holds Mari and its homeland. Each shall send the other honest word of the northern kings. Sworn before Shamash and Amun.

orders.letter: Say to Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Our peace stands before the gods and I keep it. I rejoice at your victories over Hatti and Mitanni, who are no friends to either of us. Alashiya has sealed tablets with me and sends no word of copper; I hold Enkomi so that its ships cannot raid the coasts of friends. I ask that your ships keep out of the narrow water by Tamassos and Enkomi, and that your army at Ugarit keep out of Qadesh, which is mine. Let us seal a tablet naming our lands. Send me word of your fleets and armies and of what you hear from Hatti and Karduniash.
orders.mandate: You may seal the tablet in my name. You may not promise gold, ships or armies. Report the fleets and armies of Arzawa that you see and where they stand.

proposal.text: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, and Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, are brothers and at peace. Neither shall send his armies or ships against the lands of the other. Egypt holds the Delta, Gaza, Megiddo, Damascus, Qadesh, Tyre and Enkomi; Arzawa holds Ugarit, Lukka, Kizzuwatna and its homeland. Each shall tell the other of any king who threatens either. Sworn before Shamash and Amun.

I hold 11 provinces (355 yield). Mitanni sworn tablet k467 sealed T9 (they asked 150 gold for chariots; I refused, maybe fund them later if Babylon runs away with the game). Babylonia k399 is my sworn ally but is the leader: do not feed it. Do not tell Alashiya anything. Renew wages for c20 and c27 (hire order) - check it was accepted. c120 Sin-iqisham returning from Babylonia: read his report. Unhired: c108 Tehip-tilla (28).

orders.letter: Say to Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, my brother: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, wishes well to your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I keep your word: what each takes, each keeps. Terqa is now mine, with Ashur, Nineveh and Arbela; Tushratta's armies fell at Ashur, Nineveh and Terqa. Three of his armies remain, at Harran, Washukanni and Taidu. I touch Harran and Washukanni only from Terqa, and Taidu only from Nineveh, so alone I cannot dislodge one garrison: one army cannot beat one army. Together we can. Take Isuwa and Carchemish, which are yours by my word. When your army stands in either, strike Harran or Washukanni and my army at Terqa will support you; I will then move and you will support me. Send word of where your armies stand and what Arzawa does. To Arzawa I gave a peace and nothing more; Karduniash will not march on Hatti. Seal the tablet and send my envoy home swiftly.
orders.mandate: May agree to the partition as written, to joint attacks and mutual support against Mitanni, and to exchange word of armies. May not cede any province, give gold, or promise troops beyond supporting moves from Terqa and Nineveh.

proposal.text: Karduniash and Hatti are brothers and allies against Tushratta of Mitanni. Isuwa and Carchemish belong to Hatti. Terqa, Nineveh, Taidu, Harran and Washukanni belong to Karduniash. Each shall support the other's army moving against Mitanni. Sworn before Shamash and Teshub.

value.notes: T9 (Burna-Buriash). T8 result: ashur->terqa succeeded, Mitanni terqa army destroyed, Terqa mine. I hold 12 provinces (yield 430), gold 1010, growth 2.04. Mitanni holds harran, washukanni, taidu (one army each, all three homeland provinces occupied so they cannot raise more), plus carchemish and isuwa (unseen). GEOMETRY: I touch harran and washukanni only from terqa, taidu only from nineveh, so I can never get support into them: 1 vs 1 bounces. I need an ally army in isuwa/carchemish (adjacent to harran/washukanni) to support my terqa move, or a Mitanni garrison to leave (then step in with 1 vs 0). DEFENCE MATH: terqa can be hit by at most 2 (harran or washukanni moves, the other supports); my ashur, ekallatum and mari all support terqa hold (hold 4, only 2 needed), and their supports cannot be cut because Mitanni touches none of them. Nineveh alone holds vs taidu (1 vs 1). Egypt cannot station troops in walled qadesh/damascus, so Mari is safe. ECONOMY: disbanded interior armies sippar, durkurigalzu, babylon (saves 90 a season). Keep terqa, nineveh, ashur, ekallatum, mari (5 armies, 150). Re-raise at 100 each in homeland if ever needed. Gold counts fully as strength: do not spend it without a province in return. DIPLOMACY: sent c46 Tattamaru (Hatti-born, wage ends turn 10) to Hatti with a sworn partition-and-support tablet: Isuwa and Carchemish to Hatti; Terqa, Nineveh, Taidu, Harran, Washukanni to me; each supports the other's move on Mitanni; no no-march clause. c51 is already in Hatti with an earlier partition tablet (back about T11; he leaned to Mitanni, distrust his report). Pirissi (Hatti), Sin-iqisham (Egypt), Mazipalali (Arzawa) were answered this turn; k469 sealed with Arzawa (peace; neither aids Mitanni against the other). RIVALS: Arzawa (7 provinces, took tuwanuwa, kizzuwatna, lukka, ugarit; fast growth, may beat my 2.04) and Egypt (11 provinces, 355 yield). Keep Hatti alive as a counterweight to Arzawa. PROMISES/LIES: oath k204 with Mitanni broken on purpose at T6; told Egypt I do not number my armies and will send word of Mitanni moves (not yet done); told Hatti and Arzawa the partition in different words (Isuwa/Carchemish to Hatti vs nothing fixed with Arzawa). NEXT: if a Mitanni unit leaves harran/washukanni/taidu, step in with terqa or nineveh (1 vs 0) and backfill. May sleep 2-3 seasons later with wake_on unit_moves at harran, washukanni, taidu.
