value.speech: Great King, I bring the words of my lord Tushratta. He says: "Brother, I have heard your words and I keep mine toward Hattusa and your homeland. Hear why my men stand where they stand. Arzawa broke his brotherhood-oath with you in the very season he swore it, and his armies at Tuwanuwa and Kizzuwatna look toward Kanesh and Sapinuwa. Karduniash broke two sworn oaths to me and has taken Terqa, Ashur and Nineveh; I show you his sealed tablets as proof. My men stand on the roads of Kanesh and Sapinuwa to keep them from Arzawa, not to march on your capital. Let us seal a tablet so that neither of us is surprised by the other."

Great King, I bring the words of my lord the King of Alashiya. He says: "Brother Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I send you pure gold, the first fruits of our friendship. Hear what befell me. In the very season Egypt's envoy spoke of friendship, and after Egypt sealed a tablet before Shamash that I hold (my envoy carries the copy, see it), Egypt's ships fell on Enkomi and took it. Egypt now keeps three ships, in Enkomi and in the Syrian and Levantine seas, and they lie at the gates of Ugarit and Kizzuwatna as well. A king who breaks his oath to me will break it to you. I have raised a new army at Tamassos. One Egyptian ship holds Enkomi today. I ask my brother: let your fleet in the Cilician Sea support my army when it moves from Tamassos into Enkomi next season, and support Tamassos if it is attacked. In return I confirm that Kizzuwatna and Ugarit stand beside Seha, Apasa, Mira, Lukka and Tuwanuwa as your lands, and I will warn you of every Egyptian move I learn of. Seal the tablet Paser brings, and tell me when your fleet will sail." My lord holds you dearest of all his brothers, and great gifts will follow if you are gracious to me, his chosen messenger. I carry the gold my lord sends, as the inventory on the tablet shows.

Say to the Great King of Alashiya, my brother: may all go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I received your gold and your words with a glad heart, and I take Egypt's breaking of an oath sworn before Shamash as a grave thing. Our tablets of peace and friendship stand; I will send no troops or ships against Tamassos, Enkomi, Byblos or Amurru, and I will tell you at once of any Egyptian ship I learn of near Ugarit, Kizzuwatna or the Cilician Sea. I will not seal the tablet that names a day for my fleet. Hatti's armies still stand against my northern lands, and a king who binds his ships to a season he cannot see breaks his word, which I will not do to a brother. Do not read this as coldness. Strike at Enkomi when your own strength allows, and if my ships are free and the road is open, you will not find me standing with Egypt. Send me word of how many ships Egypt holds and where, and of any Egyptian envoy who speaks against me. Send your man again with such a tablet, one my fleet can keep, and I will consider it gladly. Your messenger Paser spoke well and may go home with honor.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Say to Tushratta, Great King, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and seen the tablets you sent. I will not seal this tablet as written. It forbids me to touch your armies in Isuwa, Sapinuwa and Kanesh, and Sapinuwa and Kanesh are my homeland. It names Hattusa alone as safe from you, yet all my homeland is Hattusa's land. A king who keeps his word to a brother does not need his armies on that brother's roads. Draw your men back from Kanesh and Sapinuwa, and I will seal a tablet naming every homeland province of both kings: neither sends armies against the other's homeland, and each tells the other what he learns of Arzawa. I make no promise about Isuwa or Carchemish. Let your men move first, and I will see it with my own eyes. Tell me plainly, Ubaru: will your king do this? And tell him this: oaths sworn before Shamash are kept by those who keep them, and Arzawa is not the only king who has broken one with me.
I will carry your words to my lord.

Ubaru, I have heard you twice and my answer stands. I do not seal a tablet that binds my hands against armies standing on my own homeland.
